Ad perfectionem autem divinæ naturæ, præcipue pertinent misericordia et justitia. Opera autem misericordiæ faciunt Deum amabilem; opera vero justitiæ reddunt eum terribilem. Utraque tamen faciunt eum gloriosum et honorandum. Ut ergo divina perfectio reluceret in rebus sub ratione misericordiæ, prædestinavit Deus nonnullos, quibus sola pietate præparavit gratiam viæ et gloriam patriæ. Volens quoque relucere in creaturis suam justitiam, quosdam reliquit, quos dicitur reprobare; quod secundum Augustinum, est nolle misereri. Unde Salomon ait: Fecit Deus impium ad diem malum. Et alibi dicit Scriptura: In diem perditionis servatur impius, et ad diem furoris ducetur. Verumtamen, quoniam bonitas atque perfectio Dei excellentius repræsentatur ac splendet in electis quam reprobis, ideo prædestinati, specialiter facti dicuntur ad gloriam Dei, juxta illud Isaiæ: Omnem qui invocat nomen meum, in gloriam meam creavi eum. Omnia hæc breviter tangit Apostolus quum ait, quod Deus ostendere volens iram et potentiam suam, sustinuit vasa iræ ut ostenderet divitias gloriæ suæ in vasis misericordiæ, id est in prædestinatis, de quibus subjungitur:
paras.en: In these words the Apostle makes plain, as far as man can grasp or it is expedient to know, what is the common reason of the divine predestination and rejection. For as Solomon says: [[Prov 16:4|The Lord hath made all things for himself|Omnia propter se ipsum operatus est Dominus]]; and in Ecclesiastes: [[Eccles 3:14|God hath made that he may be feared|Fecit Deus opera sua ut timeatur]] [Denis: "God hath made his works that he may be feared"]. From which it shines out that God made all things for himself as their end, namely that his perfection might appear in creatures, and so from considering them God might be glorified, loved and feared. And to the perfection of the divine nature belong above all mercy and justice. The works of mercy make God lovable; the works of justice make him terrible. Yet both make him glorious and worthy of honour. So that the divine perfection might shine out in things under the aspect of mercy, God predestined some, for whom out of mercy alone he prepared the grace of the way and the glory of the fatherland. And willing that his justice should shine out in creatures, he left some, whom he is said to reject; which, according to Augustine, is to will not to have mercy. Hence Solomon says: [[Prov 16:4|the wicked also for the evil day|impium ad diem malum]] [Denis: "God hath made the wicked for the evil day"]. And elsewhere the Scripture says: [[Job 21:30|the wicked man is reserved to the day of destruction, and he shall be brought to the day of wrath|In diem perditionis servatur impius, et ad diem furoris ducetur]]. Yet, since the goodness and perfection of God is represented and shines more excellently in the elect than in the reprobate, therefore the predestined are said to be made specially for the glory of God, according to that word of Isaias: [[Is 43:7|And every one that calleth upon my name, I have created him for my glory|Omnem qui invocat nomen meum, in gloriam meam creavi eum]]. The Apostle touches briefly on all this when he says that God, willing to show his wrath and power, endured the vessels of wrath that he might show the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy, that is, on the predestined, of whom there follows:

paras.t: Quos et vocavit ad fidem et gratiam per prædicationem Apostolorum, non solum ex Judæis, sed etiam ex gentibus: ex utroque enim populo quidam ad Christum conversi sunt; sicut in Osee propheta dicit: Vocabo, id est nominabo, non plebem meam, id est populum gentilem, plebem meam. Nam ante conversionem suam erant non plebs mea secundum præsentem justitiam, quamvis secundum æternam prædestinationem fuerint semper plebs mea. Et non dilectam meam, id est eamdem plebem quam tempore suæ idololatriæ non dilexi, quantum ad culpam, vocabo dilectam meam, id est mihi dilectam, quum fidem et caritatem habuerint. Tunc enim amici erunt. Et non misericordiam consecutam, id est gentilitatem, quæ ante Christi adventum expers erat gratiæ Dei, vocabo misericordiam consecutam, quum gratiam Christi receperit. Hoc quod dicitur, Misericordiam consecutam, construendum est separatim, ut sit sensus, quod plebs gentilis quum fuerit conversa, vocabitur misericordiam consecuta. Et erit, id est, continget quod subditur, quod etiam jam dudum constat impletum: In loco, id est in terris gentilium, […] me per servos meos […] Non plebs mea estis vos, o gentiles, quamdiu idolis deservitis; ibi vocabuntur gentes istæ ad fidem conversæ, filii adoptivi Dei vivi. Quotquot enim receperunt eum, dedit eis potestatem filios Dei fieri.
paras.en: [[9:24|whom also he hath called|Quos et vocavit]] to faith and grace through the preaching of the Apostles, [[9:24|not only of the Jews but also of the Gentiles|non solum ex Judæis, sed etiam ex gentibus]]: for from both peoples some were converted to Christ; [[9:25|As in Osee he saith|sicut in Osee propheta dicit]], the prophet: [[9:25|I will call|Vocabo]], that is, I will name, [[9:25|that which was not my people|non plebem meam]], that is, the Gentile people, [[9:25|my people|plebem meam]][[Osee 2:24||]][[1 Pet 2:10||]]. For before their conversion they were not my people according to present justice, though according to eternal predestination they were always my people. [[9:25|and her that was not beloved|Et non dilectam]], mine, that is, the same people whom I did not love, as to their guilt, in the time of their idolatry, I will call [[9:25|beloved|dilectam]], mine, that is, beloved by me, when they have faith and charity. For then they will be friends. [[9:25|and her that had not obtained mercy|Et non misericordiam consecutam]], that is, the Gentile world, which before Christ's coming had no share in the grace of God, I will call [[9:25|one that hath obtained mercy|misericordiam consecutam]], when it has received the grace of Christ. This phrase, *that hath obtained mercy*, is to be construed separately, so that the sense is that the Gentile people, when it has been converted, will be called one that has obtained mercy. [[9:26|And it shalt be|Et erit]], that is, there will come to pass what follows, which is plain to have been fulfilled long since: [[9:26|in the place|In loco]], that is, in the lands of the Gentiles, […] me through my servants […] [a line or two is missing from the transcription here, with the lemma *where it was said unto them*] *you are not my people*, O Gentiles, as long as you serve idols; [[9:26|there they shall be called the sons of the living God|ibi vocabuntur filii Dei vivi]][[Osee 1:10||]], these Gentiles converted to the faith, adopted sons of the living God. For [[John 1:12|as many as received him, he gave them power to be made the sons of God|Quotquot enim receperunt eum, dedit eis potestatem filios Dei fieri]].

paras.t: Consequenter declarat Apostolus non omnes Judæos incredulos esse Domino Salvatori. Isaias autem clamat, id est, manifeste prophetat et dicit, pro Israel, id est de salvatione Judæorum: Si fuerit numerus filiorum Israel tanquam arena maris, id est, quamvis populus Israel præ multitudine innumerabilis fuerit, reliquiæ salvæ fient, id est, aliqui, numero pauci respectu aliorum, salvabuntur credendo in Christum: sicut in primitiva Ecclesia factum agnoscimus. Quomodo autem salvæ fient, adjecit: Verbum enim consummans et abbrevians in æquitate: hoc est, doctrina Christi, seu verbum Evangelii, est consummans, id est observantem ad perfectionem perducens, et præcepta legis consiliis suis perficiens; et abbrevians, id est brevi sermone perfectionem includens, innumerabiles legis cærimonias observantiasque excludens; in æquitate, id est in approbatione et observatione præceptorum moralium, quæ justa sunt atque servanda, quum sint de actibus virtutum; quia verbum breviatum, id est compendiosum, faciet Dominus Christus super terram. Hoc verbum breviatum quod Christus prædicavit in mundo, est caritatis præceptum, qua Deus proximusque diligitur. De quo verbo dicit in Evangelio: In hoc tota lex pendet et Prophetæ.
paras.en: Next the Apostle makes plain that not all the Jews are unbelieving toward the Lord the Saviour. [[9:27|And Isaias cried out concerning Israel|Isaias autem clamat pro Israel]], *cried out*, that is, prophesies and says plainly, *concerning Israel*, that is, of the salvation of the Jews: [[9:27|If the number of the children of Israel be as the sand of the sea|Si fuerit numerus filiorum Israel tanquam arena maris]][[Is 10:22||]], that is, though the people of Israel be beyond counting for multitude, [[9:27|a remnant shall be saved|reliquiæ salvæ fient]], that is, some, few in number compared with the rest, will be saved by believing in Christ: as we know was done in the early Church. And how they will be saved he adds: [[9:28|For he shall finish his word and cut it short in justice|Verbum enim consummans et abbrevians in æquitate]] [the Latin reads "a word finishing and cutting short in equity"]: that is, the teaching of Christ, or the word of the Gospel, is *finishing*, that is, bringing him who keeps it to perfection, and perfecting the precepts of the law by its counsels; and *cutting short*, that is, enclosing perfection in a brief saying and shutting out the countless ceremonies and observances of the law; *in equity*, that is, in approving and keeping the moral precepts, which are just and to be kept, since they concern acts of the virtues; [[9:28|because a short word shall the Lord make upon the earth|quia verbum breviatum faciet Dominus super terram]], *short*, that is, compendious, the Lord Christ. This short word which Christ preached in the world is the precept of charity, by which God and neighbour are loved. Of which word he says in the Gospel: [[Matt 22:40|On these two commandments dependeth the whole law and the prophets|In hoc tota lex pendet et Prophetæ]] [Denis: "on this"].

paras.t: Sciendum vero, quod Isaias ubi præallegata verba inducit, loquitur de impugnatione filiorum Israel a rege Assyriorum, temporibus Ezechiæ regis Juda, vel Osee regis Israel, ut alii asserunt. Ideo quidam dicit prædicta verba Isaiæ ad litteram intelligenda esse de filiis Israel evadentibus manum regis Assyriorum. Sed hoc non videtur, quia Apostolus hoc loco apertissime ait, quod Isaias clamat pro filiis Israel qui salvantur per Christum, quemadmodum Osee propheta clamat pro gentibus ad fidem conversis. Præterea, quod adjungit Isaias, Verbum enim consummans et abbrevians, etc., est ratio verbi prædicti de salvatione reliquiarum Israel per Christum facta. Hieronymus autem, Augustinus, Ambrosius, et omnes pene doctores catholici, exponunt hoc ad litteram de verbo evangelicæ legis. Ergo salvatio illa non est intelligenda de temporali et corporali liberatione a rege Assyriorum, sed de salvatione spirituali atque æterna facta per Christum. Unde Hieronymus, Prophetarum studiosissimus explanator, exponendo præmemorata verba, dicit quod Isaias, descripta particulari, temporali ac figurativa liberatione Judæorum a rege Assyriorum, oculum mentis convertit ad salvationem universalem, spiritualem atque perfectam per Christum exhibitam. Et probat hoc S. Hieronymus auctoritate Apostoli, qui præsenti capitulo probat conversionem reliquiarum Israel prædicta auctoritate Isaiæ. Probatio autem per Scripturam, non valet nisi secundum sensum litteralem, ut Augustinus frequenter commemorat.
paras.en: It must be known that Isaias, where he brings in the words alleged, is speaking of the attack on the children of Israel by the king of the Assyrians, in the times of Ezechias king of Juda, or of Osee king of Israel, as others assert. Therefore a certain writer says that these words of Isaias are to be understood literally of the children of Israel escaping the hand of the king of the Assyrians. But this does not seem right, since the Apostle says most plainly in this place that Isaias cries out concerning the children of Israel who are saved through Christ, as the prophet Osee cries out concerning the Gentiles converted to the faith. Moreover, what Isaias adds, [[9:28|For he shall finish his word and cut it short|Verbum enim consummans et abbrevians]], etc., is the reason for the saying about the salvation of the remnant of Israel wrought through Christ. And Jerome, Augustine, Ambrose and almost all Catholic doctors explain this literally of the word of the law of the Gospel. That salvation, then, is not to be understood of a temporal and bodily deliverance from the king of the Assyrians, but of the spiritual and eternal salvation wrought through Christ. Hence Jerome, the most zealous explainer of the Prophets, expounding these words, says that Isaias, having described the particular, temporal and figurative deliverance of the Jews from the king of the Assyrians, turns the eye of his mind to the universal, spiritual and perfect salvation brought about through Christ. And St Jerome proves this by the authority of the Apostle, who in the present chapter proves the conversion of the remnant of Israel by this authority of Isaias. And proof from Scripture is valid only according to the literal sense, as Augustine often recalls.

paras.t: Et sicut prædixit Isaias in libro visionum suarum: Nisi Dominus Sabaoth, id est exercituum, vel virtutum, præsertim cœlestium: de quo angeli clamant: Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus Dominus Deus exercituum. Secundum Hieronymum, pro eo quod est Sabaoth, Septuaginta interpretes ponunt, Omnipotens. Quibus consonare videtur, quod Joannes in Apocalypsi verba Isaiæ inducens, sic ait: Requiem non habebant, dicentia: Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus Dominus Deus omnipotens. Itaque, Nisi Dominus Sabaoth reliquisset nobis Judæis semen, id est reliquias in Christum credentes, videlicet sanctos Apostolos et ceteros ex Judaismo conversos, de quibus per Prophetam dicitur: Isti sunt semen cui benedixit Dominus; sicut Sodoma facti essemus, et sicut Gomorrha similes fuissemus, id est, penitus damnati essemus propter nostram incredulitatem, sicut perierunt habitatores Sodomæ et Gomorrhæ, cum aliis trium urbium habitatoribus, scilicet Adama, Seboim et Segor. Quidam exponit hæc verba Isaiæ ad litteram de Judæis non occisis a rege Assyriorum tempore Ezechiæ. Sed expositio talis repellitur eisdem rationibus quibus præcedens.
paras.en: [[9:29|And Isaias foretold|Et sicut prædixit Isaias]], in the book of his visions[[Is 1:9||]]: [[9:29|Unless the Lord of Sabbath|Nisi Dominus Sabaoth]], that is, of hosts, or of powers, especially the heavenly ones: of whom the angels cry: [[Is 6:3|Holy, holy, holy, the Lord God of hosts|Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus Dominus Deus exercituum]]. According to Jerome, for *Sabaoth* the Seventy put *Almighty*. With whom it seems to agree that John in the Apocalypse, bringing in the words of Isaias, says: [[Apoc 4:8|they rested not day and night, saying: Holy, Holy, Holy, Lord God Almighty|Requiem non habebant, dicentia: Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus Dominus Deus omnipotens]]. So, [[9:29|Unless the Lord of Sabbath had left us a seed|Nisi Dominus Sabaoth reliquisset nobis semen]], us Jews, that is, a remnant believing in Christ, namely the holy Apostles and the others converted from Judaism, of whom it is said through the Prophet: [[Is 61:9|these are the seed which the Lord hath blessed|Isti sunt semen cui benedixit Dominus]]; [[9:29|we had been made as Sodom and we had been like unto Gomorrha|sicut Sodoma facti essemus, et sicut Gomorrha similes fuissemus]], that is, we should have been utterly damned for our unbelief, as the inhabitants of Sodom and Gomorrha perished[[Gen 19:24||]], with the inhabitants of three other cities, namely Adama, Seboim and Segor[[Deut 29:23||]]. A certain writer explains these words of Isaias literally of the Jews not slain by the king of the Assyrians in the time of Ezechias. But such an explanation is rejected for the same reasons as the preceding one.

paras.t: Movet præterea Apostolus dubium, omni admiratione dignissimum. Quid ergo dicemus? id est, quum ex verbis Isaiæ jam pateat, paucos Judæorum credidisse, et multos de gentibus, quod mirum apparet, quid ergo dicemus ad hoc? scilicet: Quod gentes quæ non sectabantur justitiam, id est gentiles idololatriæ dediti, non observantes justitias legis divinæ seu scriptæ, apprehenderunt, id est, consecuti sunt, justitiam: justitiam autem quæ ex fide est, id est justitiam evangelicæ legis, quæ salvat per fidem, non justitiam legis Mosaicæ. Israel vero, id est populus Judæorum, sectando legem, id est præceptum, justitiæ, quæ in cærimoniis et sacrificiis consistebat, vel legem Moysis; vel, Legem justitiæ veræ et christianæ sectando, id est aliqualiter imitando, non quia lex Christi præcessit, sed quia prænuntiata et declarata est eis aliquo modo per Prophetas, sicque cœperunt eam sequi, præstolando eam, et secundum eam aliquo modo vivendo; in legem justitiæ veræ et christianæ non pervenit, recipiendo gratiam Christi, per quam evangelica adimpletur justitia, de qua dicit Salvator: Nisi abundaverit justitia vestra plus quam Scribarum et Pharisæorum, non intrabitis in regnum cœlorum. Quare sic contigit?
paras.en: The Apostle further raises a question most worthy of all wonder. [[9:30|What then shall we say?|Quid ergo dicemus?]] that is, since it is now plain from the words of Isaias that few of the Jews believed and many of the Gentiles, which seems wonderful, what then shall we say to this? namely: [[9:30|That the Gentiles who followed not after justice|Quod gentes quæ non sectabantur justitiam]], that is, the Gentiles given to idolatry, not keeping the justices of the divine or written law, [[9:30|have attained to justice|apprehenderunt justitiam]], that is, have obtained it: [[9:30|even the justice that is of faith|justitiam autem quæ ex fide est]], that is, the justice of the law of the Gospel, which saves by faith, not the justice of the law of Moses. [[9:31|But Israel, by following after the law of justice|Israel vero, sectando legem justitiæ]], *Israel*, that is, the people of the Jews, *following after the law*, that is, the precept, *of justice*, which consisted in ceremonies and sacrifices, or the law of Moses; or, following after the law of true and Christian justice, that is, imitating it in some way, not because the law of Christ went before, but because it was in some way foretold and made known to them through the Prophets, and so they began to follow it, waiting for it and in some way living according to it; [[9:31|is not come unto the law of justice|in legem justitiæ non pervenit]], of true and Christian justice, by receiving the grace of Christ, through which the justice of the Gospel is fulfilled, of which the Saviour says: [[Matt 5:20|unless your justice abound more than that of the scribes and Pharisees, you shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven|Nisi abundaverit justitia vestra plus quam Scribarum et Pharisæorum, non intrabitis in regnum cœlorum]]. [[9:32|Why so?|Quare]] did it so come about?

paras.t: Et respondet Apostolus: Quia non ex fide, sed quasi ex operibus, id est, Judæi quærebant justificari, non virtute et merito fidei Christi, sed per opera legis scriptæ, quum tamen sine fide et gratia Christi, nemo unquam salvari potuerit, sicut ostensum est. Offenderunt enim, id est impegerunt, in lapidem offensionis, id est in Christum, qui bonus est lapis salutis, impiis autem est lapis offensionis. Quemadmodum enim tendens in via, et pede in lapidem impingens, impeditur seu retardatur in via a progressu ad terminum viæ; sic Judæi peccando per infidelitatem atque præsumptionem, in Christum impingentes, retrusi atque impediti sunt a via salutis, nec pervenerunt ad finem beatum. Dicitur autem Christus lapis, propter constantiæ firmitatem. Sicut scriptum est apud Isaiam: Ecce pono in Sion, id est in populo Judæorum, inter quos conversatus est Christus; vel in Jerusalem, et in templo ubi frequenter fuit et docuit; lapidem offensionis et petram scandali, id est Christum: qui occasionaliter factus est Judæis lapis offensionis, id est peccati, quoniam contempserunt blasphemaveruntque eum, quemadmodum Petrus ait in Actibus: Hic est lapis qui reprobatus est a vobis ædificantibus. Factus quoque est eis petra scandali, id est spiritualis ruinæ. Sæpe enim Judæi scandalizabantur in verbis atque operibus Christi, non tamen nisi ex sua mera perversitate, dicentes: Ecce homo vorax, potator vini, amicus publicanorum, et multa hujusmodi. Et omnis qui crediderit in eum fide per dilectionem operante, non confundetur in æternum, nec spe sua frustrabitur; sed honorificabit eum Christus, quum fuerit suo tribunali oblatus.
paras.en: And the Apostle answers: [[9:32|Because they sought it not by faith, but as it were of works|Quia non ex fide, sed quasi ex operibus]], that is, the Jews sought to be justified not by the power and merit of faith in Christ, but through the works of the written law, although without faith and the grace of Christ no one could ever be saved, as has been shown. [[9:32|For they stumbled at the stumblingstone|offenderunt enim in lapidem offensionis]], *stumbled*, that is, struck against, *the stumblingstone*, that is, Christ, who to the good is the stone of salvation, but to the wicked a stone of stumbling[[Is 8:14||]][[1 Pet 2:7||]]. For as one going on a road and striking his foot against a stone is hindered or held back on the road from going on to the end of it, so the Jews, sinning by unbelief and presumption, striking against Christ, were thrust back and hindered from the way of salvation, and did not come to the blessed end. Christ is called a stone because of the firmness of his constancy. [[9:33|As it is written|Sicut scriptum est]], in Isaias[[Is 28:16||]]: [[9:33|Behold I lay in Sion|Ecce pono in Sion]], that is, among the people of the Jews, among whom Christ lived; or in Jerusalem and in the temple, where he often was and taught; [[9:33|a stumbling-stone and a rock of scandal|lapidem offensionis et petram scandali]], that is, Christ: who was made, as the occasion, a stone of stumbling, that is, of sin, to the Jews, since they despised and blasphemed him, as Peter says in the Acts: [[Acts 4:11|This is the stone which was rejected by you the builders|Hic est lapis qui reprobatus est a vobis ædificantibus]][[Matt 21:42||]]. He was made to them also a rock of scandal, that is, of spiritual ruin. For the Jews were often scandalized at the words and works of Christ, though only from their own sheer perversity, saying: [[Matt 11:19|Behold a man that is a glutton and a wine drinker, a friend of publicans|Ecce homo vorax, potator vini, amicus publicanorum]], and many such things. [[9:33|And whosoever believeth in him shall not be confounded|et omnis qui credit in eum, non confundetur]], with faith that works by charity, shall not be confounded for ever, nor be cheated of his hope; but Christ will honour him when he is brought before his judgement seat.

paras.t: Hanc etiam scripturam allegat Petrus in prima sua Canonica, dicens: Propter quod continet Scriptura: Ecce ponam in Sion lapidem summum, angularem. Quod vero Petrus et Paulus adjecerunt, Qui crediderit in eum non confundetur, secundum translationem Septuaginta interpretum allegatur. Loco cujus, translatio nostra sic habet: Qui crediderit, non festinet. — Hic est lapis, qui juxta Danielis oraculum, exscissus est de monte sine manibus. De quo scriptum est per Zachariam: Super lapidem unum oculi septem sunt: quia in Christo fuerunt septem dona Spiritus Sancti.
paras.en: Peter too alleges this scripture in his first Canonical Epistle, saying: [[1 Pet 2:6|Wherefore it is said in the scripture: Behold, I lay in Sion a chief corner stone|Propter quod continet Scriptura: Ecce ponam in Sion lapidem summum, angularem]]. What Peter and Paul added, [[1 Pet 2:6|he that shall believe in him shall not be confounded|Qui crediderit in eum non confundetur]], is alleged according to the translation of the Seventy. In place of which our translation has: [[Is 28:16|He that believeth, let him not hasten|Qui crediderit, non festinet]]. This is the stone which, according to the oracle of Daniel, [[Dan 2:34|was cut out of a mountain without hands|exscissus est de monte sine manibus]]. Of which it is written through Zacharias: [[Zach 3:9|upon one stone there are seven eyes|Super lapidem unum oculi septem sunt]]: for in Christ were the seven gifts of the Holy Ghost[[Apoc 5:6||]].

10.title: Expositio capituli decimi: Fratres, voluntas quidem cordis mei, etc.
10.title_en: Exposition of the tenth chapter: Brethren, the will of my heart, indeed, etc.

paras.t: Ostendit beatus Apostolus affectum suum ad populum Judæorum in præcedenti capitulo, de eorum damnatione tristando; jam idem agit, pro eorum salute orando, et ait: Fratres, o vos Christifideles, voluntas quidem cordis mei, id est desiderium animæ meæ: sumitur enim hoc loco voluntas pro actu voluntatis; et obsecratio ad Deum, id est invocatio Dei per aliqua sacra: ut quum dicimus, Per incarnationem tuam libera nos. Quod genus orationis est ardentius, et ad impetrandum magis idoneum, quia non propriis, sed rei sacræ innititur meritis. Fit pro illis incredulis Judæis in salutem, tanquam in finem, id est ad hoc ut salventur.
paras.en: The blessed Apostle showed his affection for the people of the Jews in the preceding chapter by grieving over their damnation[[Rom 9:2||]]; now he does the same by praying for their salvation, and says: [[10:1|Brethren|Fratres]], O you faithful of Christ, [[10:1|the will of my heart, indeed|voluntas quidem cordis mei]], that is, the desire of my soul: for *will* is taken here for the act of the will; [[10:1|and my prayer to God|et obsecratio ad Deum]], that is, calling upon God through some holy things: as when we say, *By thy incarnation deliver us*. This kind of prayer is more ardent and more fit for obtaining, since it leans not on one's own merits but on those of the holy thing. [[10:1|is for them unto salvation|pro illis incredulis Judæis in salutem]], is made for those unbelieving Jews, *unto salvation* as its end, that is, that they may be saved.

paras.t: Cur autem pro eis orandum sit, subdit: Testimonium enim perhibeo illis, quod æmulationem Dei, id est zelum honorandi Deum, habent: nam Christum ejusque discipulos persequendo, putant se Deo præstare obsequium, eo quod putent Jesum non esse Christum; sed non secundum scientiam, id est, zelum istum non habent secundum veram discretionem. Cujus ratio sequitur: Ignorantes enim justitiam Dei. Communiter enim dicunt doctores, non esse intelligendum hoc de increata Dei justitia qua ipse in se justus est, sed de justitia quam efficit in nobis per fidem formatam: quæ justitia facit dignum vita æterna; eratque Judæis ignota, quoniam non putabant hominem justificari per fidem Christi sine operibus legis. Videtur tamen etiam de increata Dei justitia posse intelligi. Justitia quippe vel sapientia, aut similis divinæ naturæ perfectio, dupliciter noscitur: primo, quoad se ipsam; secundo, quoad suum effectum. Quamvis ergo Judæi agnoverint justitiam Dei quoad se ipsam, scientes Deum esse justum, non tamen quoad homines et justificationes ipsorum. Non enim arbitrabantur justum in conspectu Dei, vel divinæ justitiæ congruere, ut homo per fidem et gratiam sine operibus legis consequeretur salutem: quum tamen hoc justum sit ex parte Dei, qui adeo bonus est, ut decens et justum sit eum taliter tamque gratiose salvare. Et suam quærentes statuere, id est, propriam justitiam allegantes, et in legis carnalibus justitiis confidentes, seque propriis viribus legem posse implere præsumentes, justitiæ Dei non sunt subjecti: quia sic sentiendo, nec Deo obediunt, nec ad justitiam quam fecit Deus in nobis per fidem, confugiunt, pro ejus infusione rogando, sed contradicunt eidem.
paras.en: Why we should pray for them he adds: [[10:2|For I bear them witness that they have a zeal of God|Testimonium enim perhibeo illis quod æmulationem Dei habent]], that is, a zeal for honouring God: for in persecuting Christ and his disciples they think they are doing a service to God[[John 16:2||]], because they think that Jesus is not the Christ; [[10:2|but not according to knowledge|sed non secundum scientiam]], that is, they do not have this zeal according to true discretion. The reason for which follows: [[10:3|For they, not knowing the justice of God|Ignorantes enim justitiam Dei]]. For the doctors commonly say that this is not to be understood of the uncreated justice of God, by which he is just in himself, but of the justice which he works in us through formed faith: which justice makes one worthy of eternal life; and it was unknown to the Jews, since they did not think that man is justified by faith in Christ without the works of the law. Yet it seems that it can also be understood of the uncreated justice of God. For justice, or wisdom, or any like perfection of the divine nature, is known in two ways: first, as to itself; secondly, as to its effect. So although the Jews knew the justice of God as to itself, knowing that God is just, yet they did not know it as regards men and their justification. For they did not think it just in God's sight, or fitting to the divine justice, that man should obtain salvation through faith and grace without the works of the law: though this is just on God's side, who is so good that it is fitting and just for him to save in such a way and so graciously. [[10:3|and seeking to establish their own|Et suam quærentes statuere]], that is, alleging their own justice, trusting in the carnal justices of the law, and presuming that they could fulfil the law by their own strength, [[10:3|have not submitted themselves to the justice of God|justitiæ Dei non sunt subjecti]]: for, thinking thus, they neither obey God nor flee to the justice which God has made in us through faith, praying for its infusion, but speak against it.

paras.t: Finis enim legis scriptæ, est Christus: quia lex vetus dispositio erat ad Christum et evangelicam legem, juxta illud, Lex pædagogus noster fuit in Christo. Et sic Christus est finis ad quem ordinabatur lex scripta. Dicitur etiam finis terminans legem, quantum ad cærimonialia et judicialia. Dicitur insuper finis consummans atque perficiens legem, et ejus promissa exsolvens. Unde ait Salvator: Non veni legem solvere, sed implere. Et alibi quoque ait Scriptura: Lex per Moysen data est, veritas per Christum facta est. Sic ergo finis legis est Christus, valens ad justitiam habitualem et actualem justificationem, vel ad justitiam acquirendam et exercendam, omni credenti, tam sub veteri quam sub novo Testamento. Omnes enim fideles per fidem Salvatoris justificati sunt. Quod probat Apostolus auctoritate Moysis.
paras.en: [[10:4|For the end of the law is Christ|Finis enim legis scriptæ, est Christus]], of the written law: for the old law was a preparation for Christ and the law of the Gospel, according to that word: [[Gal 3:24|the law was our pedagogue in Christ|Lex pædagogus noster fuit in Christo]]. And so Christ is the end to which the written law was ordered. He is also called the end that terminates the law, as to the ceremonial and judicial precepts. He is called besides the end that consummates and perfects the law, and pays out its promises. Hence the Saviour says: [[Matt 5:17|I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil|Non veni legem solvere, sed implere]] [Denis: "to destroy the law"]. And elsewhere too the Scripture says: [[John 1:17|For the law was given by Moses: grace and truth came by Jesus Christ|Lex per Moysen data est, veritas per Christum facta est]] [Denis has "truth" only]. So, then, Christ is the end of the law, availing [[10:4|unto justice|ad justitiam]], for habitual justice and actual justification, or for acquiring and exercising justice, [[10:4|to everyone that believeth|omni credenti]], under the Old as well as under the New Testament. For all the faithful have been justified by faith in the Saviour. This the Apostle proves by the authority of Moses.

paras.t: Moyses enim scripsit in Levitico atque Numeris, quoniam justitiam quæ ex lege est, qui fecerit homo, id est, qui legis præcepta servaverit, vivet in ea, id est, merito hujus justitiæ mortem temporalem, quæ transgressoribus infligebatur, evadet, et vivet vita naturæ, imo et temporalia ad vitam necessaria sortietur. Unde et Moyses sæpius ait: Fac hoc vel hoc, ut bene sit tibi et longo vivas tempore in terra quam Dominus dederit tibi. Quod autem non vixerit homo in ista justitia virtute legis, vita gratiæ, patet ex eo quod per Ezechielem asserit Dominus: Dedi eis præcepta non bona, et judicia in quibus non vivent. De hoc dicta sunt multa superius.
paras.en: [[10:5|For Moses wrote|Moyses enim scripsit]], in Leviticus and Numbers[[Lev 18:5||]] [the margin's reference to Numbers is not legible in the transcription][[Ezech 20:11||]], [[10:5|that the justice which is of the law: The man that shall do it|quoniam justitiam quæ ex lege est, qui fecerit homo]], that is, he who keeps the precepts of the law, [[10:5|shall live by it|vivet in ea]], that is, by the merit of this justice he will escape the temporal death that was inflicted on transgressors, and will live the life of nature, nay, will also obtain the temporal things necessary for life. Hence Moses often says: Do this or that, [[Deut 5:16|that thou mayst live a long time, and it may be well with thee in the land, which the Lord thy God will give thee|ut bene sit tibi et longo vivas tempore in terra quam Dominus dederit tibi]]. But that man did not live in this justice by the power of the law, with the life of grace, is plain from what the Lord declares through Ezechiel: [[Ezech 20:25|I also gave them statutes that were not good, and judgments, in which they shall not live|Dedi eis præcepta non bona, et judicia in quibus non vivent]]. Much has been said of this above.

paras.t: Quæ autem ex fide est justitia, id est, de justitia Christi, quæ datur per fidem, sic dicit Moyses in Deuteronomio: Ne dixeris in corde tuo, id est, ne cogitare præsumas, Quis ascendet in cœlum? id est, nemo est qui in cœlum ascendere poterit. Noli sic cogitare, quoniam id est Christum deducere: id est, sic æstimare, est dicere quod nec Christus ascendit; sicque eum deducis ad inferos, sicut et ceteros mortuos, et ita pertineret ad eos de quibus ait in Psalmo: Posuerunt me in lacu inferiori, in tenebrosis et in umbra mortis. Sed nec dixeris in corde tuo, Aut quis descendit in abyssum, id est in infernum seu limbum? quasi dicas, Nullus descendit. Noli hoc dicere, quia hoc est Christum a mortuis revocare: id est, hoc esset dicere, quod Christus pro hominum liberatione nec mortuus esset, nec ad inferos descendisset. Si enim nullus descendit, opus non fuit Christum mori atque descendere.
paras.en: [[10:6|But the justice which is of faith, speaketh thus|Quæ autem ex fide est justitia, sic dicit]], that is, of the justice of Christ, which is given through faith, Moses speaks thus in Deuteronomy[[Deut 30:12||]][[Deut 30:13||]]: [[10:6|Say not in thy heart|Ne dixeris in corde tuo]], that is, do not presume to think, [[10:6|Who shall ascend into heaven?|Quis ascendet in cœlum?]] that is, there is no one who will be able to ascend into heaven. Do not think so, for [[10:6|That is to bring Christ down|id est Christum deducere]]: that is, to think so is to say that Christ too did not ascend; and so you bring him down to hell like the other dead, and so he would belong to those of whom he says in the Psalm: [[Ps 87:7|They have laid me in the lower pit: in the dark places, and in the shadow of death|Posuerunt me in lacu inferiori, in tenebrosis et in umbra mortis]]. But do not say in your heart either, [[10:7|Or who shall descend into the deep?|Aut quis descendit in abyssum]], that is, into hell or limbo? as though you said, no one has descended. Do not say this, for [[10:7|That is, to bring up Christ again from the dead|hoc est Christum a mortuis revocare]]: that is, this would be to say that Christ had neither died for the freeing of men nor descended into hell. For if no one has descended, there was no need for Christ to die and descend.

paras.t: Hæc expositio Glossæ sumpta ex sanctis doctoribus, Lyræ non placet. Ait enim circa hunc locum, quod ista expositio in nullo concordare videtur cum scriptura Deuteronomii allegata, nec cum littera sequenti. Ipse enim exponit hoc modo: Ne dixeris in corde tuo, Quis ascendet in cœlum? negative: id est Christum deducere, id est dicere quod nondum venit in mundum, adductus per obedientiam Patris. Aut quis descendit in abyssum? negative loquendo; hoc est Christum a mortuis revocare, id est dicere quod non fuit mortuus neque surrexit. Hanc expositionem probat per litteram sequentem: Quia si confitearis in ore tuo Dominum Jesum venisse in mundum, et in corde tuo credideris quod Deus illum suscitavit a mortuis, salvus eris. Hæc probatio bona esset, si verba ista immediate jungerentur verbis prædictis. Verum, interponuntur alia verba complura, videlicet: Sed quid dicit Scriptura? Prope est verbum in ore tuo, et in corde tuo: hoc est verbum fidei quod prædicamus. Et subditur: Quia si confitearis in ore tuo, etc. Ex quo patet insufficientia probationis.
paras.en: This explanation of the Gloss, taken from the holy doctors, does not please Lyra. For he says on this place that this explanation seems in no way to agree with the scripture of Deuteronomy alleged, nor with the text that follows. He himself explains it thus: [[10:6|Say not in thy heart: Who shall ascend into heaven?|Ne dixeris in corde tuo, Quis ascendet in cœlum?]] negatively: [[10:6|That is to bring Christ down|id est Christum deducere]], that is, to say that he has not yet come into the world, brought by obedience to the Father. [[10:7|Or who shall descend into the deep?|Aut quis descendit in abyssum?]] speaking negatively; [[10:7|That is, to bring up Christ again from the dead|hoc est Christum a mortuis revocare]], that is, to say that he did not die nor rise again. He proves this explanation by the text that follows: [[10:9|For if thou confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus|Quia si confitearis in ore tuo Dominum Jesum]] [Lyra adds "to have come into the world"] [[10:9|and believe in thy heart that God hath raised him up from the dead, thou shalt be saved|et in corde tuo credideris quod Deus illum suscitavit a mortuis, salvus eris]]. This proof would be good if these words were joined directly to the words before. But several other words come between, namely: [[10:8|But what saith the scripture? The word is nigh thee; even in thy mouth and in thy heart. This is the word of faith, which we preach|Sed quid dicit Scriptura? Prope est verbum in ore tuo, et in corde tuo: hoc est verbum fidei quod prædicamus]]. And there follows: *For if thou confess with thy mouth*, etc. From which the insufficiency of the proof is plain.

paras.t: Denique quantum capio, melior et verbis Moysis consonantior est expositio Glossæ quam Lyræ. Et ut veritas certius elucescat, sciendum quod Moyses hæc verba inducit ad auferendum impossibilitatem et excusationem de observantia legis per ipsum datæ. Sic namque habet translatio nostra, videlicet translatio Hieronymi: Mandatum hoc quod ego præcipio tibi, non supra te est, nec procul positum, nec in cœlo situm, ut possis dicere: Quis nostrum valet ascendere in cœlum, ut deferat illud ad nos? Neque trans mare positum, ut dicas: Quis ex nobis transfretare possit mare? Sed juxta est sermo valde, in ore tuo et in corde tuo, ut facias illum: id est, jam vobis data est lex, et in tabulis scripta digito Dei, ideo de ejus omissione ac transgressione excusationem non habetis. Dicit itaque Lyra: quia Deuteronomium figura erat novæ legis, idcirco Apostolus jam allegat scripturam hanc figuraliter de nova lege, ad cujus custodiam omnes tenentur, videlicet ad excludendum excusationem de prævaricatione novæ legis. Sed huic obviare videtur quod nunc dicit Apostolus Moysen prænuntiata verba dixisse de justitia fidei. Est ergo pensandum, quod Scriptura sacra non semper allegatur secundum sensum totalem, perfectum seu integrum, quia in eadem auctoritate Scripturæ, multæ particulares sententiæ includuntur, et ita scriptura talis allegari potest per determinationem ad sententias particulares inclusas. Sic agitur in præsenti. In prædicta enim scriptura includitur, secundum intentionem Moysis, aliquem posse in cœlum ascendere, et in abyssum descendere. Sed hoc credere, pertinet ad justitiam fidei. Ideo bene ait Apostolus Moysen ista disseruisse de justitia fidei, etiam ad litteram: quæ si quis dixerit impossibilia esse, derogat Christo, qui descendit ad inferos, et ascendit in cœlos. Ob id Moyses prohibet dicere, Quis ascendet in cœlum?
paras.en: Finally, as far as I understand, the explanation of the Gloss is better and more in accord with the words of Moses than Lyra's. And that the truth may shine out more surely, it must be known that Moses brings in these words to take away any impossibility of, and excuse for, not keeping the law given through him. For so our translation, namely Jerome's, has it: [[Deut 30:11|This commandment, that I command thee this day is not above thee, nor far off from thee|Mandatum hoc quod ego præcipio tibi, non supra te est, nec procul positum]]: [[Deut 30:12|Nor is it in heaven, that thou shouldst say: Which of us can go up to heaven to bring it unto us|nec in cœlo situm, ut possis dicere: Quis nostrum valet ascendere in cœlum, ut deferat illud ad nos?]] [[Deut 30:13|Nor is it beyond the sea: that thou mayst excuse thyself, and say: Which of us can cross the sea|Neque trans mare positum, ut dicas: Quis ex nobis transfretare possit mare?]] [[Deut 30:14|But the word is very nigh unto thee, in thy mouth and in thy heart, that thou mayst do it|Sed juxta est sermo valde, in ore tuo et in corde tuo, ut facias illum]]: that is, the law has now been given to you and written on tables by the finger of God, so you have no excuse for omitting or transgressing it. So Lyra says that since Deuteronomy was a figure of the new law, the Apostle now alleges this scripture figuratively of the new law, which all are bound to keep, namely so as to shut out any excuse for transgressing the new law. But against this seems to be what the Apostle now says, that Moses spoke the words just quoted of the justice of faith. It must be considered, then, that holy Scripture is not always alleged according to its total, perfect or entire sense, since in one and the same authority of Scripture many particular statements are included, and so such a scripture can be alleged by narrowing it to the particular statements included in it. So it is done here. For in that scripture it is included, according to the intention of Moses, that someone can ascend into heaven and descend into the deep. But to believe this belongs to the justice of faith. Therefore the Apostle rightly says that Moses spoke of these things concerning the justice of faith, even literally: and if anyone says that they are impossible, he detracts from Christ, who descended into hell and ascended into heaven. For this reason Moses forbids us to say, [[10:6|Who shall ascend into heaven?|Quis ascendet in cœlum?]]

paras.t: Sed quid dicit Scriptura in Deuteronomio de justitia fidei? Et respondet. Prope est verbum, id est sermo salutis fideique doctrina, in ore tuo ad loquendum, et in corde tuo ad credendum: jam enim Deus omnibus obtulit verbum salutis; hoc est verbum fidei quod prædicamus: id est, verbum istud, quod (teste Scriptura) prope est tibi in ore et corde, est verbum Christi, vel scriptum de Christo (quemadmodum ipse in Evangelio loquitur: De me ille, scilicet Moyses, scripsit), quod nos Apostoli evangelizamus, dicentes: Quia si confitearis, o Christiane seu homo quicumque, in ore tuo Dominum Jesum esse regem Messiam et Filium Dei, coram hominibus, etiam coram infidelibus, si ratio exigat; vel si solus es, coram Deo; et in corde, id est in intellectu tuo, qui est fidei subjectum, credideris fide formata, quod Deus Pater vel Trinitas illum suscitavit a mortuis; salvus eris salute perpetua, de qua ait Propheta: Vere in Domino Deo nostro salus Israel. Christus enim testatur: Qui me confessus fuerit coram hominibus, confitebor et ego eum coram Patre meo. Et Joannes: Quis est qui vincit mundum, nisi qui credit quoniam Jesus est Filius Dei?
paras.en: [[10:8|But what saith the scripture?|Sed quid dicit Scriptura?]] in Deuteronomy, of the justice of faith? And he answers: [[10:8|The word is nigh thee|Prope est verbum]][[Deut 30:14||]], that is, the message of salvation and the teaching of faith, [[10:8|even in thy mouth|in ore tuo]], for speaking, [[10:8|and in thy heart|et in corde tuo]], for believing: for God has now offered the word of salvation to all; [[10:8|This is the word of faith, which we preach|hoc est verbum fidei quod prædicamus]]: that is, this word which (as the Scripture testifies) is nigh you in mouth and heart is the word of Christ, or what was written of Christ (as he himself says in the Gospel: [[John 5:46|he wrote of me|De me ille scripsit]], namely Moses), which we Apostles preach, saying: [[10:9|For if thou confess|Quia si confitearis]], O Christian, or any man, [[10:9|with thy mouth the Lord Jesus|in ore tuo Dominum Jesum]] to be the king Messias and the Son of God, before men, even before unbelievers if reason requires it; or, if you are alone, before God; [[10:9|and believe in thy heart|et in corde tuo credideris]], that is, in your intellect, which is the subject of faith, with formed faith, [[10:9|that God hath raised him up from the dead|quod Deus illum suscitavit a mortuis]], God the Father, or the Trinity; [[10:9|thou shalt be saved|salvus eris]], with everlasting salvation, of which the Prophet says: [[Jer 3:23|truly in the Lord our God is the salvation of Israel|Vere in Domino Deo nostro salus Israel]]. For Christ testifies: [[Matt 10:32|Every one therefore that shall confess me before men, I will also confess him before my Father|Qui me confessus fuerit coram hominibus, confitebor et ego eum coram Patre meo]]. And John: [[1 John 5:5|Who is he that overcometh the world, but he that believeth that Jesus is the Son of God?|Quis est qui vincit mundum, nisi qui credit quoniam Jesus est Filius Dei?]] [the margin gives 1 John 5:1]

paras.t: Deinde ostendit Apostolus, quod vera justitia habetur et exercetur per fidem. Corde enim creditur ad justitiam, id est, corde credendo tendit seu proficit homo ad justificationis adeptionem vel augmentationem. Credendo enim meretur homo peccati remissionem, gratiæ infusionem, justitiæ exercitationem. Fides autem informis disponit ad hæc; fides vero formata, id est caritati unita, auget ac perficit ista. Per fidem enim habitat Christus in cordibus nostris, secundum Apostolum. Secundum Lucam quoque, Deus fide purificat corda hominum. Ore autem confessio fit ad salutem æternam adipiscendam, quia ut dictum est, per confessionem Christi prædictam meretur homo vitam æternam. Confessio quippe oris est effectus fidei cordis, quemadmodum oratio vocalis effectus est latriæ, et eleemosynarum largitio effectus est misericordiæ. Dicit enim Scriptura: Omnis qui credit in illum, non confundetur. Hoc in fine præcedentis capituli expositum est.
paras.en: Then the Apostle shows that true justice is had and exercised through faith. [[10:10|For, with the heart, we believe unto justice|Corde enim creditur ad justitiam]], that is, by believing with the heart a man tends or advances toward the gaining or the increase of justification. For by believing a man merits the remission of sin, the infusion of grace, the exercise of justice. Unformed faith disposes for these things; but formed faith, that is, faith united to charity, increases and perfects them. For through faith [[Eph 3:17|Christ may dwell by faith in your hearts|habitat Christus in cordibus nostris]], according to the Apostle. According to Luke too, God [[Acts 15:9|purifying their hearts by faith|fide purificat corda]] of men. [[10:10|but, with the mouth, confession is made unto salvation|Ore autem confessio fit ad salutem]], to gaining eternal salvation, since, as has been said, by the confession of Christ described a man merits eternal life. For the confession of the mouth is an effect of the faith of the heart, as vocal prayer is an effect of *latria* and the giving of alms an effect of mercy. [[10:11|For the scripture saith: Whosoever believeth in him shall not be confounded|Dicit enim Scriptura: Omnis qui credit in illum, non confundetur]][[Is 28:16||]]. This was explained at the end of the preceding chapter.

paras.t: Non enim est distinctio Judæi et Græci, id est gentilis fidelis, quantum ad consecutionem salutis et gratiæ Christi. In omni enim gente, qui timet Deum et operatur justitiam, acceptus est Deo, apud quem non est personarum acceptio. Ideo omnes generaliter salvantur et justificantur per fidem. Nam idem Dominus omnium ratione generalis dominii. De quo scriptum est: Domine, rex omnipotens, in ditione tua cuncta sunt posita; et alibi: Deus cœlorum, creator aquarum, et Dominus totius creaturæ. Dives in omnes qui invocant illum, id est omnium bonorum atque pulchrorum ac desiderabilium opulentia plenus, sufficiens ditare omnes qui intimo cordis affectu ejus pietatem implorant, imo indesinenter ditans hujusmodi. Prope enim est Dominus omnibus invocantibus eum. Omnis enim quicumque invocaverit nomen Domini, id est ipsum Dominum nomine designatum, salvus erit, modo in spe per gratiam, postmodum in re per gloriam, si tamen perseveranter ac rationabiliter invocet. Hoc apud Joelem enim scriptum est.
paras.en: [[10:12|For there is no distinction of the Jew and the Greek|Non enim est distinctio Judæi et Græci]], that is, of the believing Gentile, as regards obtaining salvation and the grace of Christ. For [[Acts 10:35|in every nation, he that feareth him and worketh justice is acceptable to him|In omni enim gente, qui timet Deum et operatur justitiam, acceptus est Deo]], with whom there is no respect of persons[[Acts 10:34||]]. Therefore all in general are saved and justified through faith. [[10:12|for the same is Lord over all|Nam idem Dominus omnium]], by reason of his general dominion. Of which it is written: [[Esth 13:9|O Lord, Lord, almighty king, for all things are in thy power|Domine, rex omnipotens, in ditione tua cuncta sunt posita]]; and elsewhere: [[Jdt 9:17|O God of the heavens, creator of the waters, and Lord of the whole creation|Deus cœlorum, creator aquarum, et Dominus totius creaturæ]]. [[10:12|rich unto all that call upon him|Dives in omnes qui invocant illum]], that is, full of the abundance of all good, beautiful and desirable things, able to enrich all who implore his mercy with the inmost affection of the heart, nay, enriching such unceasingly. For [[Ps 144:18|The Lord is nigh unto all them that call upon him|Prope enim est Dominus omnibus invocantibus eum]]. [[10:13|For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord|Omnis enim quicumque invocaverit nomen Domini]], that is, the Lord himself, designated by his name, [[10:13|shall be saved|salvus erit]], now in hope through grace, afterwards in reality through glory, provided he call perseveringly and reasonably. For this is written in Joel[[Joel 2:32||]].

paras.t: Consequenter probat, quod adeptio salutis per invocationem, præsupponit fidem. Quomodo ergo invocabunt eum, scilicet Deum vel Christum, in quem non crediderunt? Nequaquam. Invocatio enim fidem præsupponit, sicut alibi dicit Apostolus: Accedentem ad Deum oportet credere. Sed videtur obviare quod ait Salvator Samaritanæ: Vos adoratis quod nescitis. Et respondendum, quod Samaritani non habuerunt fidem quæ est virtus theologica, sicut nec hæreticus discredens in uno articulo fidei: non enim receperunt libros Prophetarum. Propterea nec veraciter adoraverunt. Unde Christus adjecit: Eos qui adorant, in spiritu et veritate adorare oportet. Aut quomodo credent ei, scilicet Deo, quem non audierunt, id est, de quo nihil dictum est eis? Fides enim est ex auditu. Nam teste Philosopho, auditus est sensus disciplinæ. Quum ergo fides non habeatur nisi per revelationem alterius, oportet ut primum audiatur, vel per locutionem internam ab angelo, vel per locutionem exteriorem ab homine. Quomodo autem audient sine prædicante, id est annuntiante? Loquitur autem Apostolus de auditu exteriori per hominem, quia hoc modo communiter adducti sunt homines ad fidem. Nihilominus, secundum Dionysium, quidam gentilium solo angelorum ministerio ad fidem conversi sunt.
paras.en: Next he proves that gaining salvation by calling upon him presupposes faith. [[10:14|How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed?|Quomodo ergo invocabunt, in quem non crediderunt?]], namely God or Christ? By no means. For calling upon him presupposes faith, as the Apostle says elsewhere: [[Heb 11:6|he that cometh to God must believe|Accedentem ad Deum oportet credere]]. But against this seems to be what the Saviour says to the Samaritan woman: [[John 4:22|You adore that which you know not|Vos adoratis quod nescitis]]. And the answer is that the Samaritans did not have the faith which is a theological virtue, as neither does a heretic who disbelieves one article of faith: for they did not receive the books of the Prophets. Therefore they did not truly adore either. Hence Christ added: [[John 4:24|they that adore him must adore him in spirit and in truth|Eos qui adorant, in spiritu et veritate adorare oportet]]. [[10:14|Or how shall they believe him of whom they have not heard?|Aut quomodo credent ei, scilicet Deo, quem non audierunt]], namely God, that is, of whom nothing has been told them? For [[10:17|Faith then cometh by hearing|Fides enim est ex auditu]]. For, as the Philosopher testifies, hearing is the sense of learning. Since, then, faith is not had except through another's revealing, it must first be heard, either by inward speech from an angel or by outward speech from a man. [[10:14|And how shall they hear without a preacher?|Quomodo autem audient sine prædicante]], that is, one who announces? The Apostle is speaking of outward hearing through a man, since in this way men have commonly been brought to the faith. None the less, according to Dionysius, some of the Gentiles were converted to the faith by the ministry of angels alone.

paras.t: Quomodo vero prædicabunt, id est, qua auctoritate vel efficacia prædicationis officium assument vel exsequentur hi per quos alii convertendi sunt, nisi mittantur a Deo, qui det eis os et sapientiam miraculorumque gratiam? Actus namque prædicandi præsupponit auctoritatem officii: ideo oportet ut a Deo vel ejus vicem gerente, prædicator verbi Dei mittatur. Sicut scriptum est: Quam speciosi pedes evangelizantium pacem, evangelizantium bona! id est, valde decori sunt pedes et gressus atque affectus Apostolorum, prædicantium reconciliationem mundi factam per Christum, et bona sæculi futuri, quæ oculus non vidit, nec auris audivit. Hoc ad litteram dictum est de prædicatione evangelicæ legis per Apostolos, quibus dixit Salvator: In quamcumque domum intraveritis, primum dicite, Pax huic domui. Nostra tamen translatio continet sic: Quam pulchri super montes pedes annuntiantis et prædicantis pacem, annuntiantis bonum! Ponit enim Isaias singulare loco pluralis.
paras.en: [[10:15|And how shall they preach|Quomodo vero prædicabunt]], that is, by what authority or power of preaching shall those through whom others are to be converted take up or carry out the office of preaching, [[10:15|unless they be sent|nisi mittantur]] by God, who gives them a mouth and wisdom and the grace of miracles? For the act of preaching presupposes the authority of an office: therefore the preacher of the word of God must be sent by God or by one who stands in his place. [[10:15|as it is written: How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, of them that bring glad tidings of good things?|Sicut scriptum est: Quam speciosi pedes evangelizantium pacem, evangelizantium bona!]] that is, most comely are the feet and steps and affections of the Apostles, who preach the reconciliation of the world wrought through Christ, and the good things of the world to come, which [[1 Cor 2:9|eye hath not seen, nor ear heard|oculus non vidit, nec auris audivit]]. This is said literally of the preaching of the law of the Gospel by the Apostles, to whom the Saviour said: [[Luke 10:5|Into whatever house you enter, first say: Peace be to this house|In quamcumque domum intraveritis, primum dicite, Pax huic domui]]. Our translation, however, has it thus: [[Is 52:7|How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that bringeth good tidings, and that preacheth peace: of him that sheweth forth good|Quam pulchri super montes pedes annuntiantis et prædicantis pacem, annuntiantis bonum]]. For Isaias puts the singular in place of the plural.

paras.t: Sed non omnes obediunt Evangelio, id est annuntiationi nostræ de Christo, fidem recipiendo. Isaias enim dicit: Domine, quis credidit auditui nostro, id est mysteriis Christi quæ ego aliique Prophetæ a Spiritu Sancto audivimus, et aliis audienda proponimus? tanquam dicat, Pauci credent. Hoc tamen ad litteram de populo Judæorum prædictum est, quorum pauci conversi sunt. Unde in Joanne legitur: Quum tanta signa fecisset coram eis Jesus, non credebant in eum, ut sermo Isaiæ impleretur quem dixit: Domine, quis credidit auditui nostro?
paras.en: [[10:16|But all do not obey the gospel|Sed non omnes obediunt Evangelio]], that is, our announcing of Christ, by receiving the faith. [[10:16|For Isaias saith: Lord, who hath believed our report?|Isaias enim dicit: Domine, quis credidit auditui nostro]][[Is 53:1||]], that is, the mysteries of Christ which I and the other Prophets have heard from the Holy Ghost and set before others to hear? As if he said: few will believe. Yet this was foretold literally of the people of the Jews, of whom few were converted. Hence we read in John: [[John 12:37|And whereas he had done so many miracles before them, they believed not in him|Quum tanta signa fecisset coram eis Jesus, non credebant in eum]]: [[John 12:38|That the saying of Isaias the prophet might be fulfilled, which he said: Lord, who hath believed our hearing?|ut sermo Isaiæ impleretur quem dixit: Domine, quis credidit auditui nostro?]]

paras.t: Ergo fides est ex auditu, tam ejus qui in fide instruitur, quem oportet audire prædicantem, quam ejus qui prædicat, quem oportet audiri. Auditus autem qui ad fidem exigitur, est per verbum Christi, quod venit ad aures corporis, et aperit aures mentis. Nisi enim proponeretur verbum Dei, non esset auditus fidem dispositive inducens. Ipse vero habitus fidei, non est nisi a Deo per creationem.
paras.en: [[10:17|Faith then cometh by hearing|Ergo fides est ex auditu]], both of him who is instructed in the faith, who must hear the preacher, and of him who preaches, who must be heard. [[10:17|and hearing by the word of Christ|auditus autem per verbum Christi]], the hearing which is required for faith is by the word of Christ, which comes to the ears of the body and opens the ears of the mind. For unless the word of God were set forth, there would be no hearing to lead to faith by disposing for it. But the habit of faith itself is only from God, by creation.

paras.t: Sed dico, interrogando ut magis apte respondeam: Numquid non audierunt prædicationem Evangelii, qui obedire noluerunt? quasi dicat, Utique audierunt. Quod probat auctoritate Psalmistæ: Et quidem in omnem terram Judææ, vel in principales plagas terræ, exivit sonus eorum, id est prædicatio Apostolorum; et in fines orbis terræ exierunt verba eorum, quia ubique prædicaverunt Apostoli per se ipsos et suos discipulos, ut patet in diversis legendis et historiis. Joannes quippe implevit Christi Ecclesiis Asiam, Petrus Italiam, Andreas Achaiam, Matthæus Æthiopiam, Thomas Indiam, Bartholomæus Armeniam, Paulus totum pene orbem. Hinc enim scriptum est: Paravit Dominus brachium sanctum suum in oculis omnium gentium; et: Viderunt omnes termini terræ salutare Dei nostri.
paras.en: [[10:18|But I say|Sed dico]], asking, that I may answer the more fittingly: [[10:18|Have they not heard?|Numquid non audierunt]] the preaching of the Gospel, those who would not obey? As if he said: certainly they heard. Which he proves by the authority of the Psalmist[[Ps 18:5||]]: [[10:18|Yes, verily: Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth|Et quidem in omnem terram exivit sonus eorum]], of Judea, or into the chief regions of the earth, that is, the preaching of the Apostles; [[10:18|and their words unto the ends of the whole world|et in fines orbis terræ exierunt verba eorum]] went forth, since the Apostles preached everywhere, themselves and through their disciples, as is plain in various legends and histories. For John filled Asia with Churches of Christ, Peter Italy, Andrew Achaia, Matthew Ethiopia, Thomas India, Bartholomew Armenia, Paul almost the whole world. For this is why it is written: [[Is 52:10|The Lord hath prepared his holy arm in the sight of all the Gentiles|Paravit Dominus brachium sanctum suum in oculis omnium gentium]]; and: [[Ps 97:3|All the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God|Viderunt omnes termini terræ salutare Dei nostri]].

paras.t: Deinde ostendit inexcusabilitatem Judæorum. Sed dico, quærendo: Numquid Israel, id est populus Judæorum, non cognovit Christum et ejus doctrinam? Probat autem Apostolus quod utique cognoverunt. Primus Moyses, id est Prophetarum præcipuus, et ejus quod jam subditur, primus assertor, dicit in Deuteronomio: Ego ad æmulationem vos adducam in non gentem, in gentem insipientem, in iram vos mittam. Translatio Hieronymi talis est: Ego provocabo eos in eo qui non est populus, et in gente stulta irritabo illos; ignis succensus est in furore meo. Loquitur autem in persona Dei, ut sit sensus: Ego ad æmulationem, id est invidiam, vos Judæos adducam, non efficienter, sed permissive, quomodo per Prophetam dico: Propheta quum erraverit, ego Dominus decepi prophetam illum; in non gentem, id est gentiles, ita quod eis invidebitis, quum receperint libros Prophetarum ac legis, et in Christum crediderint: sicut jam diu cernimus adimpletum; in gentem insipientem, id est idola colentem, quod est summa stultitia et divinorum cognitionibus destituta. Dicuntur autem gentiles, non gens: Primo, quoniam tempore suæ idololatriæ non pertinebant ad Deum, nec erant plebs ejus. Secundo, quia ob vitæ suæ vilitatem, a Judæis reputabantur ut canes. Nam Christus asserit: Non est bonum sumere panem filiorum, et mittere canibus; et Moyses, Projicietis ea canibus: ubi per canes significantur gentiles. — Vel sic: Ego ad æmulationem, id est invidiam contra Christum, vos adducam in non gentem, in gentem insipientem, id est, ita ut derelicti a me propter vestram malitiam, efficiamini non gens mea, et populus stultus. In iram vos mittam, id est, in indignationem et iracundiam contra Christum et ejus discipulos mitti a dæmone permittam; vel, In iram, id est in vindictam justitiæ meæ, videlicet in pœnam vobis a Romanis inflictam, mittam vos effective, propter peccata in Christum commissa.
paras.en: Then he shows that the Jews are without excuse. [[10:19|But I say|Sed dico]], asking: [[10:19|Hath not Israel known?|Numquid Israël non cognovit?]], that is, the people of the Jews, Christ and his teaching? The Apostle proves that they certainly knew. [[10:19|First, Moses saith|Primus Moyses dicit]], *first*, that is, the chief of the Prophets and the first to assert what follows, in Deuteronomy: [[10:19|I will provoke you to jealousy by that which is not a nation: by a foolish nation I will anger you|Ego ad æmulationem vos adducam in non gentem, in gentem insipientem, in iram vos mittam]]. Jerome's translation is thus: [[Deut 32:21|I will provoke them with that which is no people, and will vex them with a foolish nation|Ego provocabo eos in eo qui non est populus, et in gente stulta irritabo illos]]; [[Deut 32:22|A fire is kindled in my wrath|ignis succensus est in furore meo]]. He speaks in the person of God, so that the sense is: *I will provoke* you Jews *to jealousy*, that is, envy, not by causing it but by permitting it, as I say through the Prophet: [[Ezech 14:9|when the prophet shall err, and speak a word: I the Lord have deceived that prophet|Propheta quum erraverit, ego Dominus decepi prophetam illum]]; *by that which is not a nation*, that is, the Gentiles, so that you will envy them when they have received the books of the Prophets and the law and believed in Christ: as we have long seen fulfilled; *by a foolish nation*, that is, one that worships idols, which is the height of folly, and is without knowledge of divine things. The Gentiles are called *not a nation*: first, because in the time of their idolatry they did not belong to God and were not his people. Secondly, because for the vileness of their life they were reckoned as dogs by the Jews. For Christ declares: [[Matt 15:26|It is not good to take the bread of the children, and to cast it to the dogs|Non est bonum sumere panem filiorum, et mittere canibus]]; and Moses: [[Ex 22:31|shall cast it to the dogs|Projicietis ea canibus]]: where by dogs the Gentiles are signified. Or thus: *I will provoke you to jealousy*, that is, to envy against Christ, *by that which is not a nation, by a foolish nation*, that is, so that, forsaken by me because of your malice, you are made not my nation and a foolish people. *I will anger you* [Latin: "I will send you into wrath"], that is, I will permit you to be sent by the devil into indignation and anger against Christ and his disciples; or, *into wrath*, that is, into the vengeance of my justice, namely into the punishment inflicted on you by the Romans, I will send you, effectively, for the sins committed against Christ.

paras.t: Post hæc ostendit Apostolus auctoritate Isaiæ Judæorum excæcationem propter suam contra Christum perversitatem, et gentium illuminationem. Isaias autem audet, id est, audacter se habet prænuntiando cæcitatem Judæorum illuminationemque gentium: ex qua prænuntiatione imminebat ei persecutio a Judæis sui temporis, imo et periculum mortis; et dicit in persona Christi: Inventus sum per fidem et contemplationem, a non quærentibus me, id est a gentilibus, qui me non requirebant, quousque misi ad eos Apostolos meos: et ita eos misericorditer præveni. Palam, non per speciem, sed per fidem illuminatam, per Scripturas et signa, apparui his qui me non interrogabant, id est prædictis gentilibus, qui non sciscitabantur ab aliis quomodo possent venire ad me. Ad Israel autem, id est populum Judæorum, dicit Isaias capitulo præmemorato, in Christi persona: Tota die, id est assidue eo tempore quo inter Judæos conversabar ac docui, expandi manus meas corporales ac spirituales ad populum non credentem et contradicentem mihi, ingratos, perfidos atque blasphemos Judæos, quibus varia beneficia spiritualia et corporalia præbui, esurientes alendo, ægros sanando, ignorantes docendo, et tandem in cruce pro eorum salute brachia extendendo.
paras.en: After this the Apostle shows by the authority of Isaias the blinding of the Jews for their perversity against Christ, and the enlightening of the Gentiles. [[10:20|But Isaias is bold|Isaias autem audet]], that is, bears himself boldly in foretelling the blindness of the Jews and the enlightening of the Gentiles: from which foretelling persecution threatened him from the Jews of his time, nay, danger of death; [[10:20|and saith|et dicit]], in the person of Christ: [[10:20|I was found by them that did not seek me|Inventus sum a non quærentibus me]][[Is 65:1||]], *found* through faith and contemplation, that is, by the Gentiles, who did not seek me until I sent my Apostles to them: and so I mercifully went before them. [[10:20|I appeared openly to them that asked not after me|palam apparui iis qui me non interrogabant]], *openly*, not face to face but by enlightened faith, through the Scriptures and signs, that is, to the Gentiles just mentioned, who did not ask of others how they might come to me. [[10:21|But to Israel he saith|Ad Israël autem dicit]], that is, to the people of the Jews, Isaias says in the chapter mentioned[[Is 65:2||]], in the person of Christ: [[10:21|All the day long|Tota die]], that is, continually in the time when I lived and taught among the Jews, [[10:21|have I spread my hands|expandi manus meas]], bodily and spiritual hands, [[10:21|to a people that believeth not and contradicteth me|ad populum non credentem et contradicentem mihi]], the ungrateful, faithless and blaspheming Jews, to whom I gave various spiritual and bodily benefits, feeding the hungry, healing the sick, teaching the ignorant, and at last stretching out my arms on the cross for their salvation.

paras.t: Quia hoc loco dicit Apostolus, Israel seu Judæos cognovisse Christum, considerandum quomodo hoc intelligendum sit. Quidam igitur dicunt, quod legisperiti sciverunt eum esse Christum, propter miracula et Scripturas. Unde Nicodemus legisperitus dixit: Scimus quia a Deo venisti magister; nemo enim potest hæc signa facere quæ tu facis, nisi fuerit Deus cum illo. Ex invidia ergo averterunt populum, ne crederent eum esse Christum. Glossa vero affirmat Judæos sic cognovisse, ut nec ratione nec auctoritate contradicere potuerint, sed non vere cognoverunt, ita ut menti eorum bene sederet. Thomas dicit (de cujus dicto sæpe miratus sum), idem dicit Ambrosius, quod certe noverunt eum esse Christum in lege promissum ut hominem, sed non cognoverunt naturam ejus divinam. Verum, quum Petrus apostolus apertissime dicat: Fratres, scio quia per ignorantiam peccastis, sicut et principes vestri; et Paulus: Si cognovissent, inquit, nunquam Dominum gloriæ crucifixissent. Christus quoque Pharisæos redarguit, quod ejus adventum non cognoverunt ex vaticinio Danielis, qui tempus illud determinavit: Faciem (inquit) cœli judicare nostis, signa autem temporum non potestis? Unde secundum Augustinum, divino moderamine factum est ut primus Christi adventus esset occultus, quoniam si manifestus fuisset, nemo illum judicare aut occidere præsumpsisset. Hinc igitur puto Judæos sic agnovisse Christum, sicut cognoverunt diaboli: qui a principio nativitatis usque ad horam passionis, nunquam habuerunt certam et stabilem de Christo notitiam, sed conjecturalem, nutantem atque ambiguam. Interdum enim, visis aliquibus mirabilibus Christi, dixerunt: Scimus quis sis; et: Jesu Fili Dei, quid venisti torquere nos? Interdum vero, visis humilitatibus et pœnalitatibus ejus, æstimaverunt eum non esse Christum. Propter quod mortem ejus procuraverunt. Ita Judæi quandoque verisimiliter suspicabantur eum esse Christum, ut quum dixerunt: Si tu es Christus, dic nobis palam. Quandoque autem scandalizabantur in verbis, factis, ac passionibus Christi, putantes eum non esse Christum. Tandem vero, prævalente invidia, et sacerdotum ac legisperitorum persuasione populum avertente, pene omnes opinati sunt eum non esse Christum, dicentes concorditer: Sanguis ejus super nos et super filios nostros; et, Si non esset hic malefactor, non tradidissemus eum.
paras.en: Since the Apostle says in this place that Israel, or the Jews, knew Christ, it must be considered how this is to be understood. Some, then, say that the doctors of the law knew that he was the Christ, because of the miracles and the Scriptures. Hence Nicodemus, a doctor of the law, said: [[John 3:2|we know that thou art come a teacher from God; for no man can do these signs which thou dost, unless God be with him|Scimus quia a Deo venisti magister; nemo enim potest hæc signa facere quæ tu facis, nisi fuerit Deus cum illo]]. So out of envy they turned the people away, lest they should believe him to be the Christ. The Gloss affirms that the Jews knew in such a way that they could not gainsay it by reason or authority, but did not truly know, so that it settled well in their mind. Thomas says (at whose saying I have often wondered), and Ambrose says the same, that they certainly knew him to be the Christ promised in the law as a man, but did not know his divine nature. But Peter the apostle says most plainly: [[Acts 3:17|brethren, I know that you did it through ignorance: as did also your rulers|Fratres, scio quia per ignorantiam peccastis, sicut et principes vestri]] [Denis: "you sinned through ignorance"]; and Paul: [[1 Cor 2:8|For if they had known it, they would never have crucified the Lord of glory|Si cognovissent, inquit, nunquam Dominum gloriæ crucifixissent]], he says. Christ too rebuked the Pharisees for not knowing his coming from the prophecy of Daniel, who fixed that time: [[Matt 16:3|You know then how to discern the face of the sky: and can you not know the signs of the times?|Faciem (inquit) cœli judicare nostis, signa autem temporum non potestis?]], he says. Hence, according to Augustine, it was done by divine governance that Christ's first coming should be hidden, since if it had been manifest no one would have dared to judge or slay him. Hence, then, I think that the Jews knew Christ in the way the devils knew him: who from the beginning of his birth until the hour of his Passion never had a certain and settled knowledge of Christ, but a conjectural, wavering and doubtful one. For sometimes, having seen some of Christ's wonders, they said: [[Luke 4:34|I know thee who thou art|Scimus quis sis]] [Denis: "we know"]; and: [[Matt 8:29|Jesus Son of God? art thou come hither to torment us|Jesu Fili Dei, quid venisti torquere nos?]] But sometimes, having seen his humiliations and sufferings, they thought that he was not the Christ. For which reason they brought about his death. So the Jews sometimes suspected, with likelihood, that he was the Christ, as when they said: [[John 10:24|If thou be the Christ, tell us plainly|Si tu es Christus, dic nobis palam]]. But sometimes they were scandalized at Christ's words, deeds and sufferings, thinking him not to be the Christ. At last, envy prevailing, and the persuasion of the priests and doctors of the law turning the people away, almost all held that he was not the Christ, saying with one voice: [[Matt 27:25|His blood be upon us and upon our children|Sanguis ejus super nos et super filios nostros]]; and: [[John 18:30|If he were not a malefactor, we would not have delivered him up to thee|Si non esset hic malefactor, non tradidissemus eum]].

11.title: Elucidatio capituli undecimi: Dico ergo: Numquid repulit Deus populum suum?
11.title_en: Explanation of the eleventh chapter: I say then: Hath God cast away his people?
11.note: A few words are missing from the transcription in the commentary on verses 2, 26 and 34; they await a scan of the page.

paras.t: De reprobatione Judæorum jam multa commemoravit Apostolus. Ne ergo ex hoc gentiles occasionem acciperent spernendi ac insultandi Judæis, ostendit Apostolus genus Judæorum non omnino esse abjectum. Dico ergo per modum interrogantis, ut aliorum quæstioni respondeam: Numquid repulit Deus populum suum? Numquid omnino abjecit Judæos? Absit. Nam et ego Paulus apostolus Israelita sum, natus ex semine Abraham, de tribu Benjamin, filii Jacob. Non repulit, id est, non dimisit, sed gratiose vocavit, Deus populum suum Judaicum, quem prædestinavit ad vitam, videlicet Apostolos et alia multa millia Judæorum. Et hoc declarat Apostolus per simile quod contigit sub Elia.
paras.en: The Apostle has already recounted much about the rejection of the Jews. So, lest the Gentiles should take occasion from this to despise and insult the Jews, the Apostle shows that the race of the Jews has not been altogether cast off. [[11:1|I say then|Dico ergo]], by way of asking, that I may answer the question of others: [[11:1|Hath God cast away his people?|Numquid repulit Deus populum suum?]] Has he altogether cast off the Jews? [[11:1|God forbid! For I also am an Israelite of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin|Absit. Nam et ego Israelita sum, ex semine Abraham, de tribu Benjamin]], I Paul the apostle, born of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin, the son of Jacob. [[11:2|God hath not cast away his people|Non repulit, id est, non dimisit, sed gratiose vocavit, Deus populum suum]], *hath not cast away*, that is, has not dismissed but graciously called, his Jewish people, whom he predestined to life, namely the Apostles and many other thousands of the Jews. And the Apostle makes this plain by a likeness of what happened under Elias.

paras.t: […] moribus, id est, scire et considerare debetis. In Elia, id est de Elia propheta, quid dicit Scriptura, quomodo interpellat Deum, id est ad judicandum invocat Deum zelo justitiæ, non affectu invidiæ, adversus Israel, id est decem tribus idololatriæ deditas? dicens: Domine, Prophetas tuos occiderunt, tempore Achab et Jezabel, quoniam reprehenderunt idololatriam eorum, altaria tua suffoderunt, id est, funditus destruxerunt, ne remanerent loca cultus divini. Solebant autem filii Israel etiam boni immolare in excelsis seu locis sublimibus, constructis illic primo altaribus. Et ego relictus sum solus cultor tuus. Putabat namque Elias omnes bonos in Israel fuisse occisos, præsertim Prophetas, nesciens quomodo Abdias procurator Achab, abscondisset centum de Prophetis Domini in speluncis. Spiritus enim prophetiæ, nec semper, neque de omnibus simul illuminat corda Prophetarum, quia et donum prophetiæ non inest per modum habitus. Unde quum David dixisset ad Nathan prophetam quomodo vellet ædificare domum Domino, statim respondit: Omnia quæ sunt in corde tuo fac. Quod paulo post Deus prohibuit. Eliseus quoque de muliere Sunamite loquens: Anima ejus, inquit, in amaritudine est, et Dominus celavit me. Propterea dicit Gregorius, quod Prophetæ ex magno usu prophetandi, quædam dixerunt per spiritum proprium, quæ putabant se dicere per spiritum prophetiæ. Hoc tamen de scripturis Prophetarum veritatem non habet, quoniam nihil scripserunt nisi per Spiritum Sanctum. Et quærunt animam meam, id est, vitam meam exstinguere quærunt. Jezabel enim cum suis ministris quærebat Eliam occidere.
paras.en: […] [the opening of the lemma *Know you not* is missing from the transcription] [*from*] experience, that is, you ought to know and consider [[11:2|what the scripture saith of Elias|in Elia quid dicit Scriptura?]], that is, of Elias the prophet, [[11:2|how he calleth on God against Israel?|quomodo interpellat Deum adversus Israel]], *calleth on God*, that is, calls on God to judge, with zeal for justice, not with the feeling of envy, *against Israel*, that is, the ten tribes given to idolatry? saying: [[11:3|Lord, they have slain thy prophets|Domine, Prophetas tuos occiderunt]][[3 Kings 19:10||]], in the time of Achab and Jezabel, because they rebuked their idolatry, [[11:3|they have dug down thy altars|altaria tua suffoderunt]], that is, destroyed them to the ground, so that no places of divine worship should remain. For the children of Israel, even the good, used to sacrifice in the high places, or lofty places, altars having first been built there[[3 Kings 3:3||]]. [[11:3|And I am left alone|Et ego relictus sum solus]], as thy worshipper. For Elias thought that all the good in Israel had been slain, especially the Prophets, not knowing how Abdias, Achab's steward, had hidden a hundred of the Lord's Prophets in caves[[3 Kings 18:4||]]. For the spirit of prophecy does not enlighten the hearts of the Prophets always, nor about all things at once, since the gift of prophecy is not present in the manner of a habit. Hence when David had told Nathan the prophet how he wished to build a house for the Lord, he at once answered: [[1 Par 17:2|Do all that is in thy heart|Omnia quæ sunt in corde tuo fac]]. Which a little later God forbade[[1 Par 17:4||]]. Eliseus too, speaking of the Sunamite woman, says: [[4 Kings 4:27|her soul is in anguish, and the Lord hath hid it from me|Anima ejus, inquit, in amaritudine est, et Dominus celavit me]].
