For this reason Gregory says that the Prophets, from great practice in prophesying, said some things by their own spirit which they thought they were saying by the spirit of prophecy. But this does not hold of the writings of the Prophets, since they wrote nothing except by the Holy Ghost. [[11:3|and they seek my life|Et quærunt animam meam]], that is, they seek to put out my life. For Jezabel with her servants was seeking to kill Elias[[3 Kings 19:2||]].

paras.t: Sed quid dicit illi Eliæ divinum responsum, tollens ejus errorem? Deinde ponitur responsio Dei. Reliqui mihi, id est, ad gloriam nominis mei ab idololatria præservavi, septem millia virorum. Hoc dicitur, vel quia tot erant determinate, vel ad designandum universitatem bonorum relictorum. Per septenarium enim universitas, per millenarium vero perfectio designatur. Porro de mulieribus, et his qui infra annum vicesimum erant, Deum colentibus, non fit mentio, secundum consuetudinem Hebræorum, qui nec pueros nec feminas soliti sunt numerare. Hi tamen forsan plures fuerunt quam viri, maxime quum feminæ soleant esse devotiores viris. Qui non curvaverunt genua sua ante Baal Deum Achab et Jezabel.
paras.en: [[11:4|But what saith the divine answer to him?|Sed quid dicit illi divinum responsum?]], to Elias, taking away his error? Then the answer of God is given[[3 Kings 19:18||]]: [[11:4|I have left me|Reliqui mihi]], that is, I have kept from idolatry for the glory of my name, [[11:4|seven thousand men|septem millia virorum]]. This is said either because there were exactly so many, or to signify the whole number of the good who were left. For by seven the whole, and by a thousand perfection, is signified. No mention is made of the women, and of those under the age of twenty, who worshipped God, according to the custom of the Hebrews, who were not accustomed to count either children or women[[Num 1:2||]]. Yet these were perhaps more than the men, especially since women are usually more devout than men. [[11:4|that have not bowed their knees to Baal|Qui non curvaverunt genua sua ante Baal]], the god of Achab and Jezabel.

paras.t: Sic ergo et in hoc tempore novæ legis, et primi adventus Christi, seu prædicationis Apostolorum: de quo scriptum est, Ecce nunc tempus acceptabile; reliquiæ, id est aliqui pauci ex multis Deo relicti, id est a Deo conservati, secundum electionem gratiæ, id est per gratiosam electionem, vel per gratiam ex divina electione procedentem, salvæ factæ sunt, id est liberatæ, vocatæ et justificatæ per Christum. Si autem gratia, id est, si per gratiam salutem hanc consecutæ sunt, jam non ex operibus, id est, non propter merita propria sunt salvatæ. Ideo dicit alibi Apostolus: Non ex operibus justitiæ quæ fecimus nos, sed secundum suam misericordiam salvos nos fecit; et Christus, Non vos me elegistis, sed ego elegi vos. Alioqui gratia jam non est gratia: id est, si dicantur salvæ factæ istæ reliquiæ per gratiam, et etiam propter merita, tunc gratia non erit gratia, quia non gratis præstatur, sed erit debitum. Dictum est enim superius: Ei qui operatur, merces non imputatur secundum gratiam, sed secundum debitum.
paras.en: [[11:5|Even so then, at this present time also|Sic ergo et in hoc tempore]], of the new law and of the first coming of Christ, or of the preaching of the Apostles: of which it is written, [[2 Cor 6:2|Behold, now is the acceptable time|Ecce nunc tempus acceptabile]][[Is 49:8||]]; [[11:5|there is a remnant|reliquiæ]], that is, some few out of many left to God, that is, kept by God, [[11:5|according to the election of grace|secundum electionem gratiæ]], that is, by a gracious election, or by grace proceeding from the divine election, [[11:5|saved|salvæ factæ sunt]], that is, freed, called and justified through Christ. [[11:6|And if by grace|Si autem gratia]], that is, if they obtained this salvation by grace, [[11:6|it is not now by works|jam non ex operibus]], that is, they were not saved on account of their own merits. Therefore the Apostle says elsewhere: [[Tit 3:5|Not by the works of justice which we have done, but according to his mercy, he saved us|Non ex operibus justitiæ quæ fecimus nos, sed secundum suam misericordiam salvos nos fecit]]; and Christ: [[John 15:16|You have not chosen me: but I have chosen you|Non vos me elegistis, sed ego elegi vos]]. [[11:6|otherwise grace is no more grace|Alioqui gratia jam non est gratia]]: that is, if this remnant were said to have been saved by grace and also on account of merits, then grace would not be grace, since it would not be given freely, but would be a debt. For it was said above: [[Rom 4:4|to him that worketh, the reward is not reckoned according to grace but according to debt|Ei qui operatur, merces non imputatur secundum gratiam, sed secundum debitum]].

paras.t: Quid ergo restat concludendum ex his? Hoc utique quod subditur: Quod quærebat Israel, id est communis et major pars Judæorum, hoc non est consecutus, videlicet salvationem veram per Christum. Electio autem, id est prædictæ electæ reliquiæ, consecuta est gratiam istam. Ceteri vero Judæorum excæcati sunt corde, sicut scriptum est: Dedit, non influendo malitiam, sed permittendo eamdem, illis excæcatis Judæis, Deus spiritum compunctionis, id est animum invidiosum, eos pungentem ex invidia Christi ac Christifidelium; deditque eis hoc modo oculos interiores, ut non viderent, id est rationem obtenebratam, ne Christum et ejus mysteria intelligant, et aures cordis, ut non audiant obedienter prædicationem Evangelii, usque in hodiernum diem. Hæc dictio, Ut, tenetur hic consecutive, non causaliter. Nostra translatio continet sic: Audite audientes, et nolite intelligere; et videte visiones, et nolite cognoscere; excæca cor populi hujus, etc.
paras.en: [[11:7|What then?|Quid ergo]] remains to be concluded from these things? This, certainly, which follows: [[11:7|That which Israel sought, he hath not obtained|Quod quærebat Israel, hoc non est consecutus]], *Israel*, that is, the common and greater part of the Jews, namely true salvation through Christ. [[11:7|but the election hath obtained it|electio autem consecuta est]], that is, the chosen remnant spoken of, has obtained this grace. [[11:7|And the rest have been blinded|Ceteri vero Judæorum excæcati sunt]], the rest of the Jews, in heart, [[11:8|As it is written: God hath given them|sicut scriptum est: Dedit illis Deus]][[Is 6:9||]], *hath given*, not by pouring in malice but by permitting it, to those blinded Jews, [[11:8|the spirit of insensibility|spiritum compunctionis]] [Latin *compunctionis*, "of stinging"], that is, an envious mind, stinging them with envy of Christ and of Christ's faithful; and in this way he gave them inward [[11:8|eyes that they should not see|oculos, ut non viderent]], that is, a darkened reason, so that they should not understand Christ and his mysteries, [[11:8|and ears that they should not hear|et aures cordis, ut non audiant]], ears of the heart, that they may not hear obediently the preaching of the Gospel, [[11:8|until this present day|usque in hodiernum diem]]. The word *that* is taken here consecutively, not causally. Our translation has it thus: [[Is 6:9|Hearing, hear, and understand not: and see the vision, and know it not|Audite audientes, et nolite intelligere; et videte visiones, et nolite cognoscere]]; [[Is 6:10|Blind the heart of this people|excæca cor populi hujus]], etc.

paras.t: Et David dicit in Psalmo: Fiat mensa eorum coram ipsis in laqueum, id est, mensa Judæorum illaqueet eos. Quod et factum est: sive per mensam intelligatur sacra Scriptura, quam Judæi carnaliter intelligendo, laqueo dæmonum strangulantur; sive mensa, quam Christo crucifixo fecerunt, offerentes ei acetum et fel: propter quam mensam meruerunt illaqueari. Unde prædictis verbis præposuit David in Christi persona: Et dederunt in escam meam fel, etc. Potest quoque per mensam intelligi corporalis mensa Judæorum, quando post Christi ascensionem congregati sunt in Jerusalem ut Pascha celebrarent et epularentur, et antequam egrederentur, a Romanis obsessi sunt. Quælibet harum mensa, facta est eis et in captionem, qua capti sunt ab invisibilibus ac visibilibus hostibus, scilicet dæmonibus quantum ad animam, et Romanis quantum ad corpora, et in scandalum, id est ruinam de uno peccato in aliud, et in retributionem illis aliarum pœnarum, ipsis inflictarum in ultionem sanguinis Christi.
paras.en: [[11:9|And David saith|Et David dicit]] in the Psalm: [[11:9|Let their table be made a snare|Fiat mensa eorum coram ipsis in laqueum]][[Ps 68:23||]], before them, that is, let the table of the Jews ensnare them. Which has been done: whether by the table we understand holy Scripture, by understanding which carnally the Jews are strangled in the snare of the demons; or the table which they made for Christ crucified, offering him vinegar and gall: for which table they deserved to be ensnared. Hence before these words David put, in the person of Christ: [[Ps 68:22|And they gave me gall for my food|Et dederunt in escam meam fel]], etc. By the table can also be understood the bodily table of the Jews, when after Christ's ascension they gathered in Jerusalem to celebrate and feast the Pasch, and before they went out were besieged by the Romans. Each of these tables was made for them [[11:9|and a trap|et in captionem]], by which they were taken by invisible and visible enemies, namely by the demons as to the soul and by the Romans as to the body, [[11:9|and a stumbling block|et in scandalum]], that is, a fall from one sin into another, [[11:9|and a recompense unto them|et in retributionem illis]] of other punishments inflicted on them in vengeance for the blood of Christ.

paras.t: Obscurentur oculi eorum interiores, ne videant, id est, lumine fidei priventur, ne suum errorem aut Christi veritatem intelligant; et dorsum eorum, id est affectum, qui more dorsi onera cordis portat, semper incurva a rectitudine justitiæ atque amore cœlestium ad ista terrena. Vel, Dorsum eorum semper incurva, id est, servituti aliorum subjice eos: sicut jam cernimus factum, quia Judæi ubique serviunt aliis. Sic enim in Psalmo habetur: Divertit ab oneribus dorsum ejus.
paras.en: [[11:10|Let their eyes be darkened, that they may not see|Obscurentur oculi eorum interiores, ne videant]], their inward eyes, that is, let them be deprived of the light of faith, so that they may not understand their own error or the truth of Christ; [[11:10|and bow down their back always|et dorsum eorum semper incurva]], *their back*, that is, their affection, which like a back carries the burdens of the heart, bow it down always from the uprightness of justice and the love of heavenly things to these earthly ones. Or, *bow down their back always*, that is, subject them to the servitude of others: as we now see done, since the Jews everywhere serve others. For so it is in the Psalm: [[Ps 80:7|He removed his back from the burdens|Divertit ab oneribus dorsum ejus]].

paras.t: Dico ergo: Numquid sic offenderunt excæcati Judæi ut caderent a statu salutis, videlicet ut ex eorum peccato nulli sequatur utilitas? Absit. Non enim permitteret Deus mala, nisi aliqua bona consequerentur ex eo. Sed illorum delicto, id est Judæorum obstinatio atque perfidia, salus est gentibus, id est, occasionem salutis gentilibus præbuit: quia Judæis prædicationem Christi et Apostolorum spernentibus, facta est justa ad gentes transmigratio, prout in Actibus Paulus Barnabasque dixerunt: Vobis oportebat primum loqui verbum Dei; sed quia repulistis illud, ecce convertimur ad gentes: sic enim præcepit nobis Dominus. Ut illos æmulentur, id est, quatenus Judæi imitentur gentiles ad fidem conversos, exemplo eorum fidem amplectendo: sicut jam particulariter factum est, et circa finem sæculi generaliter fiet, quum venerit Elias et restituerit omnia.
paras.en: [[11:11|I say then: Have they so stumbled, that they should fall?|Dico ergo: Numquid sic offenderunt excæcati Judæi ut caderent]], the blinded Jews, from the state of salvation, namely so that no profit should follow from their sin? [[11:11|God forbid!|Absit]] For God would not permit evils unless some goods followed from them. [[11:11|But by their offence salvation is come to the Gentiles|Sed illorum delicto, salus est gentibus]], that is, the obstinacy and faithlessness of the Jews has given the Gentiles an occasion of salvation: since, when the Jews despised the preaching of Christ and of the Apostles, there was a just passing over to the Gentiles, as Paul and Barnabas said in the Acts: [[Acts 13:46|To you it behoved us first to speak the word of God: but because you reject it|Vobis oportebat primum loqui verbum Dei; sed quia repulistis illud]] … [[Acts 13:46|behold we turn to the Gentiles|ecce convertimur ad gentes]]: [[Acts 13:47|For so the Lord hath commanded us|sic enim præcepit nobis Dominus]]. [[11:11|that they may be emulous of them|Ut illos æmulentur]], that is, that the Jews may imitate the Gentiles converted to the faith, embracing the faith by their example: as has already been done in part, and will be done generally about the end of the world, when [[Matt 17:11|Elias indeed shall come, and restore all things|venerit Elias et restituerit omnia]].

paras.t: Quod si delictum illorum, id est, incredulitas Judæorum, divitiæ sunt mundi, id est occasio spiritualium divitiarum, videlicet cœlestium gratiarum gentilium, sicut jam dictum est, et diminutio eorum, id est, si depauperatio vel paucitas Judæorum ad fidem conversorum, puta Apostoli, divitiæ sunt gentium, id est instrumentales causæ per quas spiritualiter ditatæ sunt gentes, participando copiosa munera gratiæ Christi; quanto magis plenitudo eorum, id est, omnimoda et plena conversio Judæorum, in fine mundi futura, utilis tunc erit aliis? Bonum enim est potior causa boni, quam malum.
paras.en: [[11:12|Now if the offence of them|Quod si delictum illorum]], that is, the unbelief of the Jews, [[11:12|be the riches of the world|divitiæ sunt mundi]], that is, the occasion of spiritual riches, namely of the heavenly graces of the Gentiles, as has been said, [[11:12|and the diminution of them|et diminutio eorum]], that is, if the impoverishment, or the fewness, of the Jews converted to the faith, namely the Apostles, [[11:12|the riches of the Gentiles|divitiæ sunt gentium]], that is, the instrumental causes through which the Gentiles have been spiritually enriched, sharing in the plentiful gifts of the grace of Christ; [[11:12|how much more the fulness of them?|quanto magis plenitudo eorum?]], that is, the entire and full conversion of the Jews, which is to come at the end of the world, how much more profitable will it then be to others? For good is a more powerful cause of good than evil is.

paras.t: Vobis enim dico gentibus ad fidem conversis: Quamdiu quidem ego sum gentium apostolus, id est ad gentium conversionem specialiter deputatus, sicut Dominus aiebat ad me: Vade, quia ad gentes longe mittam te: hoc autem tamen toto tempore prædicationis meæ: ministerium meum honorificabo, id est, apostolatus mei officium, scilicet actum prædicationis, reverenter implebo, faciendo ultra debitum, intendendo videlicet non gentium solum, sed et Judæorum conversioni, si quo modo, id est aliquo modo, ad æmulandum fidem meam provocem verbis, signis ac moribus, carnem meam, id est Judæos mihi carnali affinitate conjunctos, et salvos faciam dispositive ac instrumentaliter aliquos ex illis. Scio enim me non omnes posse convertere, quum hoc in fine mundi futurum sit. Si enim amissio, id est perditio, eorum reconciliatio est mundi, id est gentilium occasionaliter; quæ assumptio, id est, quis erit fructus assumptionis electorum Judæorum ad fidem, nisi vita ex mortuis, id est spiritualis vivificatio gentium, a morte peccati resurgentium, per prædicationem electorum Judæorum, videlicet Apostolorum? Magis enim proficere debet electorum assumptio, quam reproborum repulsio.
paras.en: [[11:13|For I say to you, Gentiles|Vobis enim dico gentibus]], converted to the faith: [[11:13|As long indeed as I am the apostle of the Gentiles|Quamdiu quidem ego sum gentium apostolus]], that is, specially appointed for the conversion of the Gentiles, as the Lord said to me: [[Acts 22:21|Go, for unto the Gentiles afar off will I send thee|Vade, quia ad gentes longe mittam te]]: and this through the whole time of my preaching: [[11:13|I will honour my ministry|ministerium meum honorificabo]], that is, I will fulfil reverently the office of my apostleship, namely the act of preaching, doing more than is due, namely working for the conversion not of the Gentiles only but of the Jews too, [[11:14|If, by any means, I may provoke to emulation|si quo modo, ad æmulandum provocem]], *by any means*, that is, in some way, to emulate my faith, by words, signs and conduct, [[11:14|them who are my flesh|carnem meam]], that is, the Jews joined to me by kinship of the flesh, [[11:14|and may save some of them|et salvos faciam aliquos ex illis]], by disposing them and as an instrument. For I know that I cannot convert all, since this is to come at the end of the world. [[11:15|For if the loss of them|Si enim amissio eorum]], that is, their perdition, [[11:15|be the reconciliation of the world|reconciliatio est mundi]], that is, of the Gentiles, as an occasion, [[11:15|what shall the receiving of them be|quæ assumptio]], that is, what will be the fruit of the receiving of the chosen Jews into the faith, [[11:15|but life from the dead?|nisi vita ex mortuis?]], that is, the spiritual quickening of the Gentiles, rising again from the death of sin through the preaching of the chosen Jews, namely the Apostles? For the receiving of the elect ought to profit more than the rejection of the reprobate.

paras.t: Denique, quod Judæi quamdam habilitatem habeant ad conversionem, nec de eis desperandum sit, manifestat Apostolus per similitudinem delibationis et massæ, radicis quoque et rami. Delibatio autem est modicum quid de re aliqua sumptum, ad experiendum valorem totius. Itaque ait: Quod si delibatio sancta est, id est, si parvus grex ex multitudine Judæorum ad gratiam Dei assumptus, videlicet ordo Apostolorum et aliorum ex Judaismo credentium, sanctus est; et massa, id est, tunc etiam tota multitudo poterit sanctificari. Et si radix sancta, id est, quum ipsi Patriarchæ et Prophetæ, de quibus velut de radicibus pullulavit plebs Judæorum, fuerint sancti; et rami, id est nati ex eis, poterunt sanctificari. Hæ ergo similitudines intelligendæ sunt quantum ad potentiam seu aptitudinem, non quantum ad actum, quia et delibatio, massa, radix, et ramus, non conveniunt hominibus nisi metaphorice.
paras.en: Lastly, that the Jews have a certain aptness for conversion, and that we must not despair of them, the Apostle makes plain by the likeness of the firstfruit and the lump, and of the root and the branch. A firstfruit is a little of something taken to test the worth of the whole. So he says: [[11:16|For if the firstfruit be holy|Quod si delibatio sancta est]], that is, if the little flock taken from the multitude of the Jews into the grace of God, namely the order of the Apostles and of the others believing from Judaism, is holy; [[11:16|so is the lump also|et massa]], that is, then the whole multitude too will be able to be sanctified. [[11:16|and if the root be holy|Et si radix sancta]], that is, since the Patriarchs and Prophets themselves, from whom as from roots the people of the Jews sprang, were holy; [[11:16|so are the branches|et rami]], that is, those born of them will be able to be sanctified. These likenesses, then, are to be understood as to potency, or aptitude, not as to act, since firstfruit, lump, root and branch do not apply to men except metaphorically.

paras.t: Consequenter Apostolus reprimit gentes a contemptu Judæorum, eo quod gentes per fideles Judæos conversæ sint. Quod si, id est quamvis, aliqui ex ramis, id est populo isto ex Patriarchis nato, fracti sunt, id est a fide et gratia Patriarcharum alienati ac mortui; tu autem, gentilis, quum oleaster esses, id est propter peccata tua similis olivæ silvestri, amaræ ac sterili, insertus, id est divina miseratione incorporatus, atque per gratiam adunatus, es in illis, id est in ramis sanctis ac stantibus, scilicet Apostolis ceterisque electis Judæis; vel, In illis, id est loco ramorum fractorum; et socius radicis, id est collega et consors seu particeps Patriarcharum, imitando fidem ipsorum, et pinguedinis olivæ, id est socius spiritualis opulentiæ, consolationis et gratiæ Apostolorum seu electorum Judæorum, quorum quilibet erat sicut oliva fructifera in domo Dei, factus es; noli gloriari inaniter et superbe adversus ramos fractos, id est infideles Judæos, quasi non possent reparari. Quod si gloriaris contra illos inaniter, ecce dico tibi verbum, per quod poteris errorem tuum advertere: non tu radicem, id est plebem Judaicam, portas, eam sustentando aut roborando; sed radix, id est plebs ista, portat te, docens ac roborans te in via Christi. Gentiles enim ex Judæis spiritualiter nati sunt, recipiendo per eos fidem et Evangelium Christi: idcirco non debent insultare Judæis.
paras.en: Next the Apostle restrains the Gentiles from contempt of the Jews, since the Gentiles were converted through the faithful Jews. [[11:17|And if some of the branches be broken|Quod si aliqui ex ramis fracti sunt]], *if*, that is, although, *some of the branches*, that is, of this people born of the Patriarchs, *be broken*, that is, estranged from the faith and grace of the Patriarchs and dead; [[11:17|and thou, being a wild olive|tu autem, gentilis, quum oleaster esses]], O Gentile, that is, like a wild olive tree, bitter and barren, because of your sins, [[11:17|art ingrafted in them|insertus es in illis]], *ingrafted*, that is, incorporated by the divine mercy and united through grace, *in them*, that is, in the holy branches that stand, namely the Apostles and the other chosen Jews; or, *in them*, that is, in place of the broken branches; [[11:17|and art made partaker of the root|et socius radicis, et pinguedinis olivæ factus es]], that is, a colleague and sharer, or partaker, of the Patriarchs, by imitating their faith, [[11:17|and of the fatness of the olive tree|et pinguedinis olivæ]], that is, a sharer of the spiritual wealth, consolation and grace of the Apostles, or of the chosen Jews, each of whom was [[Ps 51:10|as a fruitful olive tree in the house of God|sicut oliva fructifera in domo Dei]]; [[11:18|Boast not against the branches|noli gloriari adversus ramos]], vainly and proudly, the broken branches, that is, the unbelieving Jews, as though they could not be restored. [[11:18|But if thou boast|Quod si gloriaris]] vainly against them, behold I tell you a word by which you can see your error: [[11:18|thou bearest not the root|non tu radicem portas]], that is, the Jewish people, sustaining or strengthening it; [[11:18|but the root thee|sed radix, id est plebs ista, portat te]], that is, this people bears you, teaching and strengthening you in the way of Christ. For the Gentiles were born spiritually of the Jews, receiving through them the faith and the Gospel of Christ: therefore they ought not to insult the Jews.

paras.t: Deinde Apostolus solvit objectionem gentilium, arguentium se posse gloriari contra ramos fractos, quamvis non contra radices ramosque stantes. Dicis ergo tu, gentilis: Fracti sunt rami, id est, Judæi a gratia exciderunt, ut ego inserar (secundum modum jam declaratum). Bene, id est, ita sit, et verum dicis: nam propter incredulitatem suam et cordis obstinationem fracti sunt. Tu autem fide, virtute et merito fidei tibi concessæ, stas corde erectus ad Deum. Verumtamen noli altum sapere, id est superbire, vel de te ipso sublimiter quid sentire, præferendo te illis, quasi tu tantum dilectus sis Deo, ut Deus permiserit illos frangi quatenus tu inseraris: illi enim fracti sunt directe et per se propter suam incredulitatem, sed propter tuam insertionem fracti sunt indirecte et occasionaliter: sed time judicia Dei, filiali ac casto timore. Hoc quod dictum est, Noli altum sapere, quidam allegare solent adversus studiosos qui libros difficiles et profundos legere solent, non intelligentes mentem Apostoli, neque pensantes formam et finem introductionis horum verborum. Aliqui tamen ambulant in mirabilibus super se: quibus melius esset circa propriorum vitiorum eradicationem, atque dominicæ passionis meditationem occupari assidue.
paras.en: Then the Apostle answers the objection of the Gentiles, who argue that they can boast against the broken branches, though not against the roots and the branches that stand. [[11:19|Thou wilt say then: The branches were broken off|Dicis ergo: Fracti sunt rami]], you Gentile, that is, the Jews have fallen from grace, [[11:19|that I might be grafted in|ut ego inserar]] (in the manner already explained). [[11:20|Well|Bene]], that is, be it so, and you speak truly: for [[11:20|because of unbelief they were broken off|propter incredulitatem fracti sunt]], their unbelief and obstinacy of heart. [[11:20|But thou standest by faith|Tu autem fide stas]], by the power and merit of the faith granted you, you stand with your heart raised up to God. [[11:20|Be not highminded|noli altum sapere]], that is, do not be proud, or think highly of yourself, setting yourself above them, as though you were so loved by God that God allowed them to be broken so that you might be grafted in: for they were broken directly and of themselves because of their unbelief, but on account of your grafting in they were broken indirectly and as an occasion: [[11:20|but fear|sed time]] the judgements of God, with a filial and chaste fear. This saying, *be not highminded*, some are accustomed to allege against students who read difficult and deep books, not understanding the Apostle's mind nor weighing the form and purpose of the bringing in of these words. Yet some do [[Ps 130:1|walked in great matters, nor in wonderful things above me|ambulant in mirabilibus super se]] [Denis: "walk in wonderful things above themselves"]: for whom it would be better to busy themselves constantly with rooting out their own vices and meditating on the Lord's Passion.

paras.t: Cur autem gentilis contra Judæos superbire non debeat, subditur. Si enim Deus naturalibus ramis, id est Judæis filiis Prophetarum ac Patriarcharum, qui ratione originis videbantur specialiter pertinere ad numerum electorum, qui a Christo appellati sunt filii regni, non pepercit, sed eos propter superbiam dereliquit et sprevit; vide ne forte nec tibi parcat, qui alienigena eras et oleaster. Ex præinductis infert Apostolus saluberrimam admonitionem. Vide ergo, o gentilis Christiane, id est, diligenter considera, bonitatem, id est misericordiam, et severitatem, id est rigorem justitiæ, Dei, ut dicas veraciter cum Psalmista: Misericordiam et judicium cantabo tibi, Domine; et rursus, Universæ viæ Domini, misericordia et veritas. In eos quidem qui ceciderunt, peccando et pœnam debitam sustinendo, scilicet in Judæos, vide severitatem, id est districtam Dei justitiam qua illos juste reliquit; in te autem ad Christum converso, vide bonitatem Dei, id est clementiam Dei, si permanseris in bonitate, id est in bona et virtuosa conversatione; alioqui et tu excideris a mystico corpore Christi, atque a radice ac oliva prædictis, erisque stirps inutilis, et igni traderis. Quum ergo ignoremus an permansuri simus in bonitate, oportet nos semper esse timoratos atque sollicitos, attendentes et vigiliter implentes illud Deuteronomii: Custodi temetipsum et animam tuam sollicite, et ne obliviscaris verborum Dei tui cunctis diebus vitæ tuæ.
paras.en: Why the Gentile ought not to be proud against the Jews is added: [[11:21|For if God hath not spared the natural branches|Si enim Deus naturalibus ramis non pepercit]], that is, the Jews, sons of the Prophets and Patriarchs, who by reason of their origin seemed to belong in a special way to the number of the elect, and who were called by Christ [[Matt 8:12|the children of the kingdom|filii regni]], but forsook and despised them for their pride; [[11:21|fear lest perhaps also he spare not thee|vide ne forte nec tibi parcat]], who were a foreigner and a wild olive. From what has been brought forward the Apostle draws a most wholesome warning. [[11:22|See then the goodness and the severity of God|Vide ergo bonitatem et severitatem Dei]], O Gentile Christian, that is, consider carefully the goodness, that is, the mercy, and the severity, that is, the rigour of justice, of God, so that you may truly say with the Psalmist: [[Ps 100:1|Mercy and judgment I will sing to thee, O Lord|Misericordiam et judicium cantabo tibi, Domine]]; and again: [[Ps 24:10|All the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth|Universæ viæ Domini, misericordia et veritas]]. [[11:22|towards them indeed that are fallen|In eos quidem qui ceciderunt]], by sinning and bearing the punishment due, namely the Jews, see [[11:22|the severity|severitatem]], that is, the strict justice of God by which he justly left them; [[11:22|but towards thee, the goodness of God|in te autem bonitatem Dei]], converted to Christ, see the goodness, that is, the clemency, of God, [[11:22|if thou abide in goodness|si permanseris in bonitate]], that is, in a good and virtuous way of life; [[11:22|Otherwise thou also shalt be cut off|alioqui et tu excideris]] from the mystical body of Christ, and from the root and olive tree spoken of, and you will be a useless stock and be given to the fire[[John 15:6||]]. Since, then, we do not know whether we shall abide in goodness, we must always be fearful and careful, attending to and watchfully fulfilling that word of Deuteronomy: [[Deut 4:9|Keep thyself therefore, and thy soul carefully. Forget not the words|Custodi temetipsum et animam tuam sollicite, et ne obliviscaris verborum]] [Denis: "the words of thy God all the days of thy life"].

paras.t: Sed et illi fracti rami, infideles Judæi, si non permanserint finaliter in incredulitate, inserentur consortio electorum seu radici suæ, videlicet Patriarchis, et erunt veri filii eorum, non solum carnali origine, sed fide ac opere. Potens est enim Deus, cui nihil difficile est, iterum inserere illos, impios justificando: ideo desperandum non est. Nam si tu, gentilis, ex naturali excisus es oleastro, id est a conversatione vitiosa et sterili liberatus, et per hoc a te ipso mutatus: qui eras oleaster naturalis per similitudinem, quoniam in gentilitate natus ac enutritus fuisti; et contra naturam, id est solitum cursum naturæ, quæ non solet surculum malum inserere arbori bonæ, insertus, id est intime copulatus, es per fidem, caritatem et gratiam in bonam olivam, id est olivæ bonæ, pingui et fructuosæ, videlicet sanctis Patriarchis atque Apostolis, spirituali pinguedine internæ consolationis, sincerissimæ contemplationis ac fervidæ dilectionis copiose repletis; quanto magis hi qui sunt secundum naturam, id est Judæi qui sunt naturales rami, ut patuit, inserentur, id est incorporabuntur, suæ olivæ, id est populo suo electo, si non permanserint in incredulitate? Nempe, ut ait Origenes, facilius esse videtur propriæ arboris ramos suæ radici reddere, quam inserere alienos. Si ergo gentiles inserti sunt fidei Apostolorum ac Prophetarum, multo facilius Judæi inseri poterunt, si tamen fecerint quod in se est.
paras.en: [[11:23|And they also|Sed et illi]], the broken branches, the unbelieving Jews, [[11:23|if they abide not still in unbelief|si non permanserint in incredulitate]], to the end, [[11:23|shall be grafted in|inserentur]], into the fellowship of the elect, or into their root, namely the Patriarchs, and they will be their true sons, not only by carnal origin but by faith and works. [[11:23|for God is able to graft them in again|potens est enim Deus iterum inserere illos]], to whom nothing is hard[[Jer 32:17||]], by justifying the ungodly: therefore we must not despair. [[11:24|For if thou were cut out of the wild olive tree, which is natural to thee|Nam si tu, gentilis, ex naturali excisus es oleastro]], you Gentile, that is, freed from a vicious and barren way of life, and by this changed from yourself: you who were a wild olive by nature, by likeness, since you were born and brought up in heathenism; [[11:24|and, contrary to nature|et contra naturam]], that is, against the usual course of nature, which does not graft a bad shoot onto a good tree, [[11:24|wert grafted into the good olive tree|insertus es in bonam olivam]], *grafted*, that is, closely joined, through faith, charity and grace, into a good olive tree, rich and fruitful, namely the holy Patriarchs and Apostles, abundantly filled with the spiritual fatness of inward consolation, most pure contemplation and fervent love; [[11:24|how much more shall they that are the natural branches be grafted into their own olive tree?|quanto magis hi qui sunt secundum naturam, inserentur suæ olivæ?]], that is, the Jews, who are the natural branches, as has appeared, *be grafted*, that is, incorporated, *into their own olive tree*, that is, their own chosen people, if they do not abide in unbelief? For, as Origen says, it seems easier to restore the branches of a tree to their own root than to graft in strange ones. If, then, the Gentiles have been grafted into the faith of the Apostles and Prophets, much more easily will the Jews be able to be grafted in, provided they do what lies in them.

paras.t: Nolo enim vos ignorare, o fratres, mysterium, id est divinum secretum, seu occultum Dei judicium hoc, quod subditur, ut non sitis vobis ipsis, id est in propriis oculis, sapientes: quia cæcitas ex parte, id est, quod spiritualis excæcatio, contigit in Israel, id est in populo Judæorum: quæ cæcitas duratura est donec plenitudo gentium, id est universitas gentilium prædestinata, intraret statum salutis et Christi ovile, et sic, ingressis gentilibus, omnis Israel, id est totus populus Judæorum […] credendo in Christum. Quod erit circa terminum mundi, prædicantibus Elia et Enoch: qui patefacta Antichristi nequitia, populum Judæorum tunc superstitem existentem convertent, quemadmodum per Prophetam Dominus protestatur: Ecce ego mittam vobis Eliam prophetam, antequam veniat dies Domini magnus et horribilis; et convertet cor patrum ad filios, et cor filiorum ad patres. De qua etiam finali Judæorum conversione et longa eorum interim desolatione scriptum est per Prophetam: Dies multos sedebunt filii Israel sine rege, et sine principe, et sine sacrificio, et sine altari, et sine ephod, et sine theraphim; et post hæc revertentur filii Israel, et quærent Dominum Deum suum, et David regem suum; et pavebunt ad Dominum et ad bonum ejus in novissimo dierum. Per David autem omnes intelligunt Christum.
paras.en: [[11:25|For I would not have you ignorant, brethren, of this mystery|Nolo enim vos ignorare, o fratres, mysterium]], that is, this divine secret, or hidden judgement of God, which follows, [[11:25|lest you should be wise in your own conceits|ut non sitis vobis ipsis sapientes]], that is, in your own eyes: [[11:25|that blindness in part has happened in Israel|quia cæcitas ex parte contigit in Israël]], that is, that a spiritual blinding has befallen the people of the Jews: which blindness is to last [[11:25|until the fulness of the Gentiles should come in|donec plenitudo gentium intraret]], that is, the whole predestined number of the Gentiles, into the state of salvation and the fold of Christ, [[11:26|And so all Israel|et sic, ingressis gentilibus, omnis Israel]], the Gentiles having come in, that is, the whole people of the Jews […] [the words *should be saved* and a line after them are missing from the transcription] by believing in Christ. Which will be about the end of the world, when Elias and Enoch preach: who, having laid bare the wickedness of Antichrist, will convert the people of the Jews then living, as the Lord declares through the Prophet: [[Mal 4:5|Behold, I will send you Elias the prophet, before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord|Ecce ego mittam vobis Eliam prophetam, antequam veniat dies Domini magnus et horribilis]]. [[Mal 4:6|And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers|et convertet cor patrum ad filios, et cor filiorum ad patres]]. Of this final conversion of the Jews, and of their long desolation in the meantime, it is written through the Prophet: [[Osee 3:4|For the children of Israel shall sit many days without king, and without prince, and without sacrifice, and without altar, and without ephod, and without theraphim|Dies multos sedebunt filii Israel sine rege, et sine principe, et sine sacrificio, et sine altari, et sine ephod, et sine theraphim]]. [[Osee 3:5|And after this the children of Israel shall return and shall seek the Lord, their God, and David, their king: and they shall fear the Lord, and his goodness, in the last days|et post hæc revertentur filii Israel, et quærent Dominum Deum suum, et David regem suum; et pavebunt ad Dominum et ad bonum ejus in novissimo dierum]]. And by David all understand Christ.

paras.t: Sicut scriptum est apud Isaiam, secundum translationem Septuaginta interpretum: Veniet ex Sion, id est, ex populo Judæorum nascetur et egredietur Christus, qui eripiat modo, quantum ad aliquos, et avertat in fine mundi communiter impietatem, id est infidelitatem et cetera vitia, ab Jacob, id est a populo Judæorum. Et hoc illis a me testamentum, id est, evangelica lex seu firma promissio hereditatis æternæ dabitur Judæis a me, quum abstulero peccata eorum, in fine mundi quum convertero eos ad Christum. Sic enim alibi scriptum est: Revertetur et miserebitur nostri; deponet omnes iniquitates nostras, et projiciet in profundum maris omnia peccata nostra. Porro, translatio Hieronymi talis est: Timebunt qui ab occidente nomen Domini, et qui ab ortu gloriam ejus, quum venerit quasi torrens violentus, et venerit Sion redemptor, et eis qui redeunt ab iniquitate in Jacob: hoc fœdus meum cum eis.
paras.en: [[11:26|as it is written|Sicut scriptum est]], in Isaias, according to the translation of the Seventy: [[11:26|There shall come out of Sion|Veniet ex Sion]], that is, Christ will be born of and come forth from the people of the Jews, [[11:26|he that shall deliver|qui eripiat]], now, as to some, [[11:26|and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob|et avertat impietatem ab Jacob]], at the end of the world generally, ungodliness, that is, unbelief and the other vices, from Jacob, that is, from the people of the Jews. [[11:27|And this is to them my covenant|Et hoc illis a me testamentum]], that is, the law of the Gospel, or the firm promise of the eternal inheritance, will be given by me to the Jews, [[11:27|when I shall take away their sins|quum abstulero peccata eorum]], at the end of the world, when I shall convert them to Christ. For so it is written elsewhere: [[Mich 7:19|He will turn again, and have mercy on us: he will put away our iniquities: and he will cast all our sins into the bottom of the sea|Revertetur et miserebitur nostri; deponet omnes iniquitates nostras, et projiciet in profundum maris omnia peccata nostra]]. Jerome's translation is as follows: [[Is 59:19|And they from the west, shall fear the name of the Lord: and they from the rising of the sun, his glory when he shall come as a violent stream|Timebunt qui ab occidente nomen Domini, et qui ab ortu gloriam ejus, quum venerit quasi torrens violentus]], [[Is 59:20|And there shall come a redeemer to Sion, and to them that return from iniquity in Jacob|et venerit Sion redemptor, et eis qui redeunt ab iniquitate in Jacob]]: [[Is 59:21|This is my covenant with them|hoc fœdus meum cum eis]] [the margin's chapter number is not legible in the transcription].

paras.t: Secundum Evangelium quidem, id est propter Evangelium Christi cui contradicunt, sunt Judæi jam inimici Deo et bonis hominibus: et hoc, propter vos, id est ad vestram utilitatem: quia ut dictum est, ideo permisit eos Deus excæcari, ut eorum excæcatio esset occasio illuminationis gentilium. Secundum electionem autem, id est propter gratiam eligentis, sunt quidam eorum carissimi Deo, id est singulariter præelecti, sicut Apostoli, propter patres, id est, ut promissiones factæ Patriarchis implerentur in his electis reliquiis Judæorum. Vel: Secundum electionem, id est ob exhibitionem beneficiorum Dei eis collatorum, et quia ad cultum Dei specialiter deputati fuerunt, sunt carissimi: et hoc, propter patres, id est, quia de semine Patriarcharum sunt. Cur autem propter patres sint carissimi secundum electionem, subjungitur: Sine pœnitentia enim, id est sine variatione propositi et dolore, sunt dona Dei gratuita, et vocatio Dei, qua vocat vel vocare decrevit electos ad gratiam: hoc est, Deum non pœnitet de hoc quod aliquibus Judæorum decrevit atque promisit salutem conferre. Idcirco, sicut promisit Patriarchis conversionem Judæorum, sic fiet. Unde scriptum est: Porro Triumphator in Israel pœnitudine non flectetur: neque enim homo est, ut agat pœnitentiam. Et Jacobus: Apud quem non est transmutatio, nec vicissitudinis obumbratio. Quod ergo in Genesi ait, Pœnitet me fecisse hominem, metaphorice dicitur; sicut et illud, Tactus dolore cordis intrinsecus. Vel sic: Sine pœnitentia enim hominis præcedente, sunt dona Dei, et vocatio ad fidem. Non enim propter meritum proprium quisquam ad fidem vocatur, gratiamque primam sortitur.
paras.en: [[11:28|As concerning the gospel, indeed, they are enemies|Secundum Evangelium quidem, inimici]], that is, on account of the Gospel of Christ, which they gainsay, the Jews are now enemies to God and to good men: and this [[11:28|for your sake|propter vos]], that is, for your profit: since, as has been said, God permitted them to be blinded so that their blinding might be the occasion of the enlightening of the Gentiles. [[11:28|but as touching the election|Secundum electionem autem]], that is, on account of the grace of him who chooses, some of them are [[11:28|most dear|carissimi]] to God, that is, singularly chosen beforehand, as the Apostles, [[11:28|for the sake of the fathers|propter patres]], that is, so that the promises made to the Patriarchs might be fulfilled in this chosen remnant of the Jews. Or: *as touching the election*, that is, because of the showing of the benefits of God bestowed on them, and because they were specially appointed to the worship of God, they are *most dear*: and this *for the sake of the fathers*, that is, because they are of the seed of the Patriarchs. Why they are most dear for the sake of the fathers as touching the election is added: [[11:29|For the gifts and the calling of God are without repentance|Sine pœnitentia enim sunt dona et vocatio Dei]], *without repentance*, that is, without change of purpose and without sorrow, *are the gifts* of God, the free gifts, *and the calling of God*, by which he calls, or has decreed to call, the elect to grace: that is, God does not repent of having decreed and promised to bestow salvation on some of the Jews. Therefore, as he promised the Patriarchs the conversion of the Jews, so it will be done. Hence it is written: [[1 Kings 15:29|But the triumpher in Israel will not spare, and will not be moved to repentance: for he is not a man that he should repent|Porro Triumphator in Israel pœnitudine non flectetur: neque enim homo est, ut agat pœnitentiam]] [Denis omits "will not spare"]. And James: [[Jas 1:17|with whom there is no change nor shadow of alteration|Apud quem non est transmutatio, nec vicissitudinis obumbratio]]. What is said in Genesis, then, [[Gen 6:7|it repenteth me that I have made them|Pœnitet me fecisse hominem]] [Denis: "that I have made man"], is said metaphorically; as also that word: [[Gen 6:6|And being touched inwardly with sorrow of heart|Tactus dolore cordis intrinsecus]]. Or thus: the gifts of God and the calling to faith are *without* the *repentance* of man going before. For no one is called to faith, or gains first grace, on account of his own merit.

paras.t: Ponit præterea sanctus Apostolus convenientiam quamdam, ad declarandum quod Judæi tandem misericordiam consequuntur. Sicut enim aliquando, scilicet tempore idololatriæ vestræ, et vos, gentiles, non credidistis Deo, sed idolis; nunc autem tempore evangelicæ prædicationis, misericordiam, id est gratiam Dei, consecuti estis propter illorum, videlicet Judæorum, incredulitatem, id est occasione incredulitatis eorum: quia illorum damnatio et excisio fuit occasionaliter vestra salus atque insertio, sicut ostensum est. Ita et isti Judæi nunc, tempore gratiæ, non crediderunt in vestram misericordiam, id est, non crediderunt quod veraciter misericordiam consecuti essetis; vel, Non crediderunt, id est, credendo non pervenerunt, in vestram misericordiam, id est in fidem et gratiam a Deo vobis clementer exhibitam; ut et ipsi misericordiam consequantur, id est, miseratio vobis impensa, fiat eis miserationis acquirendæ occasio: quoniam Deus, qui nunc misertus est gentilibus, tandem dignum ducet misereri Judæis, qui olim fuerunt populus peculiaris. Sic ergo de Judæis et gentilibus factum est: Conclusit enim, id est, esse convicit, seu concludi permisit, Deus omnia, id est genera hominum, scilicet Judæos et gentiles, in incredulitate: uterque enim populus multoties idolis deservivit; ut omnium misereatur, id est, quosdam ex omnibus illis convertat ac salvet. Hæc dictio, ut, tenetur hic consecutive, non causaliter: quia non ideo permisit Deus illos errare, ut misereretur eis. Sic enim nostra malitia esset directa causa glorificationis, seu manifestatio pietatis divinæ, et ita placeret Deo. Indirecte tamen est causa ejus, ut dictum est, secundum quod bonus Deus non permitteret mala, nisi bona elicerentur ex malo.
paras.en: The holy Apostle further sets out a certain correspondence, to make plain that the Jews will at last obtain mercy. [[11:30|For as you also in times past did not believe God|Sicut enim aliquando et vos non credidistis Deo]], namely in the time of your idolatry, you Gentiles, but believed idols; [[11:30|but now have obtained mercy|nunc autem misericordiam consecuti estis]], in the time of the preaching of the Gospel, mercy, that is, the grace of God, [[11:30|through their unbelief|propter illorum, videlicet Judæorum, incredulitatem]], namely that of the Jews, that is, on the occasion of their unbelief: since their damnation and cutting off was, as an occasion, your salvation and grafting in, as has been shown. [[11:31|So these also now have not believed, for your mercy|Ita et isti nunc non crediderunt in vestram misericordiam]], these Jews, now, in the time of grace, that is, they did not believe that you had truly obtained mercy; or, *have not believed*, that is, have not come by believing, *into your mercy*, that is, into the faith and grace mercifully shown you by God; [[11:31|that they also may obtain mercy|ut et ipsi misericordiam consequantur]], that is, that the mercy bestowed on you may become for them an occasion of obtaining mercy: since God, who has now had mercy on the Gentiles, will at last deem it fitting to have mercy on the Jews, who were once his own people. So, then, it has been done with Jews and Gentiles: [[11:32|For God hath concluded all in unbelief|Conclusit enim Deus omnia in incredulitate]], *concluded*, that is, convicted them of being so, or permitted them to be shut up, *all*, that is, the kinds of men, namely Jews and Gentiles: for both peoples many times served idols; [[11:32|that he may have mercy on all|ut omnium misereatur]], that is, that he may convert and save some from all of them. The word *that* is taken here consecutively, not causally: for God did not permit them to go astray in order to have mercy on them. For so our malice would be the direct cause of glorification, or the showing forth of the divine mercy, and so would please God. Yet it is an indirect cause of it, as has been said, inasmuch as the good God would not permit evils unless goods were drawn out of evil.

paras.t: Ex consideratione insuper mirabilium quæ de prædestinatione ac reprobatione, et eorum quæ sequuntur ex illis, inducta sunt, admirans Apostolus, stupens ac tremens exclamat: O altitudo, id est sublimis profunditas et profunda sublimitas, divitiarum, id est plenitudinis, sapientiæ, quantum ad divina et superiora, et scientiæ, quantum ad humana ac inferiora, Dei omnia cognoscentis! Cujus notitia quamvis in se una et simplex consistat, multis tamen nominibus designatur, secundum diversitatem eorum quæ cognoscuntur. Quanta autem sit altitudo sapientiæ et scientiæ Dei, ex Scriptura aliquo modo innotescit. Ait enim Psalmista: Magnus Dominus noster, et sapientiæ ejus non est numerus; item, Mirabilis facta est scientia tua ex me, confortata est, et non potero ad eam. Altitudo autem divitiarum sapientiæ Dei aliud non est, nisi sapientia Dei altissima atque plenissima. Quam incomprehensibilia sunt judicia ejus! Sive per judicia Dei intelligamus dispositiones rerum seu decreta Dei de rebus, secundum quod dispositiones istæ sunt in mente divina, sive effectus divinæ justitiæ, quos Deus judicando efficit in rebus: certum est quod judicia ista omnem capacitatem mentis humanæ prorsus excedunt, quemadmodum sapientia, scientia et justitia unde procedunt. Propter quod scriptum est: Fortissime, magne et potens, Dominus exercituum nomen tibi; magnus consilio, et incomprehensibilis cogitatu. In Job quoque: Digne eum invenire non possumus; magnus fortitudine et judicio et justitia, et enarrari non potest: ideo timebunt eum viri, et non audebunt contemplari omnes qui sibi videntur sapientes. Et quam investigabiles sunt viæ ejus, id est processus seu executiones operum divinorum! quia nec modum emanationis rerum a Deo, nec gubernationis, nec modum beatificationis electorum intelligere possumus. Ideo Salomon dicit: Cunctæ res difficiles; non potest homo eas explicare sermone.
paras.en: Moreover, from considering the wonders that have been brought forward about predestination and rejection, and the things that follow from them, the Apostle, wondering, astonished and trembling, cries out: [[11:33|O the depth|O altitudo]], that is, lofty depth and deep loftiness, [[11:33|of the riches|divitiarum]], that is, of the fulness, [[11:33|of the wisdom|sapientiæ]], as to divine and higher things, [[11:33|and of the knowledge|et scientiæ]], as to human and lower things, [[11:33|of God|Dei]], who knows all things! Whose knowledge, though in itself it is one and simple, is yet designated by many names according to the diversity of the things known. How great is the depth of the wisdom and knowledge of God is made known in some way from Scripture. For the Psalmist says: [[Ps 146:5|Great is our Lord, and great is his power: and of his wisdom there is no number|Magnus Dominus noster, et sapientiæ ejus non est numerus]]; and again: [[Ps 138:6|Thy knowledge is become wonderful to me: it is high, and I cannot reach to it|Mirabilis facta est scientia tua ex me, confortata est, et non potero ad eam]]. And the depth of the riches of the wisdom of God is nothing else than the wisdom of God, most high and most full. [[11:33|How incomprehensible are his judgments|Quam incomprehensibilia sunt judicia ejus]]! Whether by the judgements of God we understand the dispositions of things, or God's decrees about things, as these dispositions are in the divine mind, or the effects of the divine justice which God works in things by judging: it is certain that these judgements altogether exceed every capacity of the human mind, as do the wisdom, knowledge and justice from which they proceed. For which reason it is written: [[Jer 32:18|O most mighty, great, and powerful, the Lord of hosts is thy name|Fortissime, magne et potens, Dominus exercituum nomen tibi]]. [[Jer 32:19|Great in counsel, and incomprehensible in thought|magnus consilio, et incomprehensibilis cogitatu]]. In Job too: [[Job 37:23|We cannot find him worthily: he is great in strength, and in judgment, and in justice, and he is ineffable|Digne eum invenire non possumus; magnus fortitudine et judicio et justitia, et enarrari non potest]]. [[Job 37:24|Therefore men shall fear him, and all that seem to themselves to be wise, shall not dare to behold him|ideo timebunt eum viri, et non audebunt contemplari omnes qui sibi videntur sapientes]]. [[11:33|and how unsearchable his ways|Et quam investigabiles sunt viæ ejus]], that is, the processes or carryings out of the divine works! since we can understand neither the manner of the coming forth of things from God, nor of their governance, nor the manner of the beatifying of the elect. Therefore Solomon says: [[Eccles 1:8|All things are hard: man cannot explain them by word|Cunctæ res difficiles; non potest homo eas explicare sermone]].

paras.t: Quis enim cognovit sensum Domini, id est dictamen intellectus divini de rebus, videlicet, quid Deus de creaturis suis facere cogitavit, quid de singulis sentiat, quid de omnibus intra se judicet? Nescit quoque homo an amore dignus sit, an odio. Ideo in libro Sapientiæ legitur: Sensum tuum, Domine, quis sciet, nisi tu dederis sapientiam, et miseris Spiritum tuum de cœlis? […] quis consiliarius ejus fuit, id est, quis dedit Deo consilium de dispositionibus et productionibus rerum? Nullus plane, quia non indiget alicujus auxilio aut doctrina. Aut quis prior dedit illi, id est, quis aliquid perfectionis contulit Deo, exsistens ante eum, et retribuetur ei a Deo donum condignum? Nullus utique, quia omnia alia habent a Deo, quidquid habent boni, et sunt. Hoc sumpsit Apostolus ex eo quod scriptum est in Isaia: Quis adjuvit Spiritum Domini, aut quis consiliarius ejus fuit, et ostendit illi? Cum quo iniit consilium, et instruxit eum, etc.?
paras.en: [[11:34|For who hath known the mind of the Lord?|Quis enim cognovit sensum Domini]], that is, the judgement of the divine intellect about things, namely what God has thought to do with his creatures, what he thinks of each, what he judges within himself of all? Man does not know either whether he is worthy of love or of hatred. Therefore we read in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 9:17|And who shall know thy thought, except thou give wisdom, and send thy holy Spirit from above|Sensum tuum, Domine, quis sciet, nisi tu dederis sapientiam, et miseris Spiritum tuum de cœlis?]] […] [a word or two is missing from the transcription here: *Or*] [[11:34|who hath been his counsellor?|quis consiliarius ejus fuit]], that is, who has given God counsel about the disposing and producing of things? Plainly no one, since he needs no one's help or teaching. [[11:35|Or who hath first given to him|Aut quis prior dedit illi]], that is, who, existing before him, has bestowed any perfection on God, [[11:35|and recompense shall be made him?|et retribuetur ei]] by God, a worthy gift? No one at all, since all other things have from God whatever good they have, and their being. The Apostle took this from what is written in Isaias: [[Is 40:13|Who hath forwarded the spirit of the Lord? or who hath been his counsellor, and hath taught him?|Quis adjuvit Spiritum Domini, aut quis consiliarius ejus fuit, et ostendit illi?]] [[Is 40:14|With whom hath he consulted, and who hath instructed him|Cum quo iniit consilium, et instruxit eum]], etc.?

paras.t: Quoniam ex ipso, et per ipsum, et in ipso sunt omnia. De hujus verbi intellectu multa dici possent; sed breviter dico, quod Deus est causa rerum in triplici genere causandi. Est enim causa efficiens, causa formalis, formans seu exemplaris, et causa finalis. Dicitur autem causa efficiens, ratione potentiæ qua cuncta creavit; causa exemplaris, ratione sapientiæ qua universa disposuit et distinxit; causa finalis, ratione bonitatis qua omnia ad se ipsum reducit, conservat, et ad proprios fines inclinat. Quoniam ergo potentia attribuitur Patri, sapientia Filio, bonitas Spiritui Sancto, idcirco quod dicitur, Ex ipso, proprie refertur ad Patrem; quod vero adjicitur, Per ipsum, refertur ad Filium (omnia enim facta sunt per ipsum); et quod subditur, In ipso, refertur ad Spiritum Sanctum, cui ratione clementiæ competit res conservare, perficere, inclinare ad optima. Et ita in verbis Apostoli notatur trinitas Personarum, et distinctiva proprietas causalitatis earum. Verumtamen, quum unaquæque divina Persona sit verus creator, perfecta causa omnium rerum, et unicuique earum conveniat potentia, sapientia et bonitas; ideo de qualibet trium Personarum intelligi potest quoniam ex ipsa, et per ipsam, et in ipsa sunt omnia. Nam et quælibet earum est omnium rerum causa efficiens, creando; exemplaris, secundum æternam rationem ideam seu speciem producendo; finalis, universa propter debitum finem, et maxime propter ultimum finem, agendo et conservando. De hoc primo Sententiarum aptior locus est. Ipsi Deo uni ac trino honor et gloria in sæcula sæculorum. Amen. Nil justius, nilque ad promerendum efficacius, quam ut toto corde optemus Deum ab omnibus honorificari et glorificari, totisque viribus faciamus hoc ipsum.
paras.en: [[11:36|For of him, and by him, and in him, are all things|Quoniam ex ipso, et per ipsum, et in ipso sunt omnia]]. Much could be said about the meaning of this word; but I say briefly that God is the cause of things in a threefold kind of causing. For he is the efficient cause, the formal, forming or exemplary cause, and the final cause. He is called the efficient cause by reason of the power by which he created all things; the exemplary cause by reason of the wisdom by which he disposed and distinguished all things; the final cause by reason of the goodness by which he leads all things back to himself, preserves them and inclines them to their own ends. Since, then, power is attributed to the Father, wisdom to the Son and goodness to the Holy Ghost, what is said, *of him*, refers properly to the Father; what is added, *by him*, refers to the Son ([[John 1:3|All things were made by him|omnia enim facta sunt per ipsum]]); and what follows, *in him*, refers to the Holy Ghost, to whom by reason of clemency it belongs to preserve things, perfect them and incline them to what is best. And so in the Apostle's words the trinity of Persons is noted, and the distinguishing property of their causality. Yet since each divine Person is truly creator, the perfect cause of all things, and power, wisdom and goodness belong to each of them, therefore it can be understood of any of the three Persons that of it, and by it, and in it are all things. For each of them is the efficient cause of all things, by creating; the exemplary, by producing them according to the eternal reason, idea or form; the final, by working and preserving all things for their due end, and above all for the last end. Of this there is a fitter place in the First Book of the Sentences. [[11:36|to him be glory for ever. Amen|Ipsi gloria in sæcula Amen]], to God, one and three, be honour and glory for ever and ever. Amen. Nothing is more just, and nothing more effective for meriting, than that we should desire with our whole heart that God be honoured and glorified by all, and do this very thing with all our strength.

12.title: Elucidatio capituli duodecimi: Obsecro itaque vos, fratres, etc.
12.title_en: Explanation of the twelfth chapter: I beseech you therefore, brethren
12.note: Some words are lost in the transcription in v. 2, at the end of v. 17 and at the end of the article.

paras.t: Post reductionem Romanorum ad sanctam concordiam, jam instruuntur in moribus. Obsecro itaque, id est, per sacrum aliquod rogo, vos, fratres, videlicet per misericordiam Dei, id est per pietatem ac bonitatem divinam, ut propter dignitatem ac reverentiam ejus acquiescatis petitioni meæ ; vel, Per misericordiam Dei, id est per effectum divinæ pietatis, scilicet per gratiam Dei mihi et vobis impensam. Potius autem dicit, Obsecro, quam, Jubeo, quia ut Seneca ait, generosus est animus hominis, et facilius ducitur quam trahitur. Unde et Philemoni scribens Apostolus : Fiduciam, inquit, multam habens imperandi tibi, propter caritatem magis obsecro. Ut exhibeatis, id est, agatis et sponte offeratis Domino, corpora vestra, non solum exteriora vestra, hostiam viventem, id est vivifice mortificatam, et mortifice vivificatam : quatenus corpora vestra fiant hostiæ per carnalium desideriorum mortificationem seu exstirpationem, juxta illud : Mortificate membra vestra quæ sunt super terram ; et iterum, Quoniam propter te mortificamur tota die. Sint vero hostiæ viventes, per operationes virtuosas vitam æternam mercantes. Sanctam, id est a carnalibus sordibus expurgatam. Deo placentem, id est, ad ultimum finem Deique gloriam, ordinatam. Rationabile, id est discretum ac moderatum, sit obsequium vestrum, quod Deo offertis in corporis vestri castigatione : ne caro ultra vires maceretur et debilitetur, sicque de cetero operum bonorum instrumentum esse non possit; et ne nimis delicate tractetur, aut minus juste affligatur. Quum enim corpus sit animæ instrumentum, regendum est secundum exigentiam utilitatemque animæ, ut tantum affligatur in parcimonia cibi, potus, somni, vestitus, et omnium exteriorum consolationum, quantum anima ferre potest sine corporis defectione. Idcirco discretio summe necessaria est, quæ est mater et custos ac fotrix virtutum. Propterea enim scriptum et jussum est : In omni oblatione offeres sal. Et Christus : Habete (inquit) in vobis sal. Hinc etiam scriptum est per Jeremiam : Quia plus fecit quam potuit, idcirco periit. Corporalis igitur exercitatio moderanda est secundum quod expedit profectui animæ in interioribus suis.
paras.en: After bringing the Romans back to holy concord, he now instructs them in conduct. [[12:1|I beseech you therefore|Obsecro itaque vos]], that is, I ask by something sacred, [[12:1|brethren|fratres]], namely [[12:1|by the mercy of God|per misericordiam Dei]], that is, by the divine goodness and kindness, that out of reverence for its dignity you may yield to my request; or, by the mercy of God, that is, by the effect of the divine kindness, namely by the grace of God bestowed on me and on you. He says "I beseech" rather than "I command," because, as Seneca says, the mind of man is noble, and is more easily led than dragged. So too the Apostle, writing to Philemon, says: [[Philem 1:8|though I have much confidence|Fiduciam, inquit, multam habens]] [[Philem 1:8|to command thee|imperandi tibi]], [[Philem 1:9|For charity sake I rather beseech|propter caritatem magis obsecro]]. [[12:1|that you present|Ut exhibeatis]], that is, that you do and freely offer to the Lord, [[12:1|your bodies|corpora vestra]], not only your outward things, [[12:1|a living sacrifice|hostiam viventem]], that is, put to death so as to live, and given life so as to die: so that your bodies may become victims by the mortifying or rooting out of carnal desires, according to the words: [[Col 3:5|Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth|Mortificate membra vestra quæ sunt super terram]]; and again, [[Ps 43:22|Because for thy sake we are killed all the day long|Quoniam propter te mortificamur tota die]] [the margin gives Ps. xxxvi, 22, a misreading of xliii, 22]. And let them be living victims, earning eternal life by virtuous works. [[12:1|holy|Sanctam]], that is, cleansed from carnal filth. [[12:1|pleasing unto God|Deo placentem]], that is, directed to the last end and to the glory of God. [[12:1|your reasonable service|rationabile obsequium vestrum]]: let your service, which you offer God in chastising your body, be reasonable, that is, discreet and moderate: lest the flesh be wasted and weakened beyond its strength, and so be unable thereafter to be the instrument of good works; and lest it be treated too delicately, or afflicted with too little justice. For since the body is the soul's instrument, it is to be ruled according to the soul's need and benefit, so that it is afflicted by sparing food, drink, sleep, clothing and all outward comforts as far as the soul can bear without the body breaking down. For this, discretion is supremely necessary, which is the mother, guardian and nurse of the virtues. This is why it is written and commanded: [[Lev 2:13|In all thy oblations thou shalt offer salt|In omni oblatione offeres sal]]. And Christ says: [[Mark 9:49|Have salt in you|Habete (inquit) in vobis sal]]. Hence also it is written through Jeremias: [[Jer 48:36|because he hath done more than he could, therefore they have perished|Quia plus fecit quam potuit, idcirco periit]] [the margin's "Jer. xxxvi, 36" is xlviii, 36; Denis has *periit*, "he perished"]. Bodily exercise, then, is to be moderated according to what helps the soul's progress in its inward life.

paras.t: Et nolite conformari affectu, actu, consensu, aut simili modo, huic sæculo, id est mundanis et vanis hominibus. Amicitia enim hujus mundi, inimica est Deo. Qui ergo voluerit amicus hujus mundi fieri, inimicus Dei constituetur. Ideo monet Joannes : Nolite diligere mundum, neque ea quæ in mundo sunt. Sed reformamini, id est, amissam Dei similitudinem rursus acquirite, in novitate sensus vestri, id est, adipiscendo spiritualem atque internam mentis vestræ innovationem. Deformati enim sumus in primo parente, perdendo originalem justitiam per quam Deo assimilabamur, et incurrendo originale peccatum et vulnera animæ quibus primo parenti lapso conformamur. Jubemur ergo exuere veterem hominem cum actibus suis, et induere novum qui secundum Deum creatus est, ut renovetur sicut aquilæ juventus animæ nostræ, obtinendo quotidie virorem virtutum, et gratiarum cœlestium recentem decorem, sicque redeamus ad pristinam Baptismatis innocentiam, atque originalis justitiæ conformitatem. Hoc est quod in prima Canonica admonet beatissimus Petrus : Deponentes omnem malitiam, quasi modo geniti infantes rationabiles, lac concupiscite, ut in eo crescatis in salutem ; et Jeremias, Innova dies nostros sicut a principio. Sic itaque reformari studete, ut probetis, id est, experimento discatis, et experiri possitis per gustum Spiritus Sancti habitantis in vobis, quæ sit voluntas Dei, id est, quid Deus velit, quid Deo complaceat : cujus utique voluntas bona est, quia non vult nisi bona, et beneplacens electis fidelibus et amicis, qui sunt unum cum Deo per unionem affectuum, et perfecta, id est sanctissima, et cunctis rebus præstantior.
paras.en: [[12:2|And be not conformed|Et nolite conformari]], in affection, act, consent or any like way, [[12:2|to this world|huic sæculo]], that is, to worldly and vain men. For [[Jas 4:4|the friendship of this world is the enemy of God|Amicitia enim hujus mundi, inimica est Deo]]. [[Jas 4:4|Whosoever therefore will be a friend of this world becometh an enemy of God|Qui ergo voluerit amicus hujus mundi fieri, inimicus Dei constituetur]]. So John warns: [[1 John 2:15|Love not the world, nor the things which are in the world|Nolite diligere mundum, neque ea quæ in mundo sunt]]. [[12:2|but be reformed|Sed reformamini]], that is, regain the likeness of God that was lost, [[12:2|in the newness of your mind|in novitate sensus vestri]], that is, by gaining a spiritual and inward renewal of your mind. For we were deformed in our first parent, by losing the original justice by which we were made like God, and by incurring original sin and the wounds of the soul by which we are made like our fallen first parent. So we are commanded to [[Col 3:9|stripping yourselves of the old man with his deeds|exuere veterem hominem cum actibus suis]] [Denis: "to put off the old man with his deeds"], [[Col 3:10||]]and to put on the new, [[Eph 4:24|who according to God is created|qui secundum Deum creatus est]], so that the youth of our soul [[Ps 102:5|shall be renewed like the eagle's|renovetur sicut aquilæ juventus]], gaining daily the freshness of the virtues and the new beauty of heavenly graces; and so we return to the first innocence of Baptism and to conformity with original justice. This is what the most blessed Peter urges in his first Canonical Epistle: [[1 Pet 2:1|laying away all malice|Deponentes omnem malitiam]], [[1 Pet 2:2|As newborn babes, desire the rational milk without guile, that thereby you may grow unto salvation|quasi modo geniti infantes rationabiles, lac concupiscite, ut in eo crescatis in salutem]] [Denis has "as newborn babes endowed with reason, desire milk"]; and Jeremias: [[Lam 5:21|renew our days, as from the beginning|Innova dies nostros sicut a principio]]. So strive to be reformed in this way, [[12:2|that you may prove|ut probetis]], that is, that you may learn by experience, and be able to experience by the taste of the Holy Ghost who dwells in you[[2 Tim 1:14||]], [[12:2|what is the good and the acceptable and the perfect will of God|quæ sit voluntas Dei]], that is, what God wills, what is pleasing to God: whose will is indeed [[12:2|good|bona]], because He wills nothing but good things, [[12:2|and the acceptable|et beneplacens]] to the elect, the faithful and His friends, who are one with God by union of affections, [[12:2|and the perfect|et perfecta]], that is, most holy, and more excellent than all things.

paras.t: Advertendum autem, quod voluntas Dei quandoque accipitur pro potentia sive actione volitiva existente in Deo qua vult : quæ semper impletur. De qua ait per Isaiam : Consilium meum stabit, et omnis voluntas mea fiet; et Psalmista, Omnia quæcumque voluit Dominus, fecit. Hæc est voluntas beneplaciti : et secundum hanc acceptionem voluntatis divinæ, procedit expositio jam inducta. Secundo, voluntas Dei dicitur id quod vult, vel signum voluntatis divinæ. Sicque præceptum et consilium dicuntur voluntas Dei : quæ non semper impletur. Ideo petimus eam impleri, dicentes : Fiat voluntas tua sicut in cœlo et in terra. Et de hac quoque voluntate potest exponi littera, hoc modo : Probetis, per exsecutionem, quæ sit [...] id est jussio, consultio, prohibitio voluntatis divinæ : quæ jussio, consultio, etc., est bona, in quantum concernit bona naturæ et statum incipientium ; est et beneplacens Deo ac bonis hominibus, prout respicit bona gratiæ et statum proficientium ; est quoque perfecta, secundum quod respicit bona gloriæ, quæ jubet finaliter appeti, et statum perfectorum. Qui autem sanctam atque internam vitam ducit, experimentaliter noscit et gustat, quid placeat, et quid displiceat Deo. Dum enim remorsum non habet, sed Deo sollicite servit, et delectatur in ipso, omne peccatum detestans, tunc Spiritus Sanctus perhibet ei testimonium quod voluntas sua unita et concors sit Deo. Unde ait Salvator : Si quis voluerit voluntatem Dei facere, cognoscet de doctrina an ex Deo sit.
paras.en: It is to be noted that the will of God is sometimes taken for the power or act of willing existing in God, by which He wills: and this is always fulfilled. Of it He says through Isaias: [[Is 46:10|My counsel shall stand, and all my will shall be done|Consilium meum stabit, et omnis voluntas mea fiet]]; and the Psalmist: [[Ps 134:6|Whatsoever the Lord pleased he hath done|Omnia quæcumque voluit Dominus, fecit]]. This is the will of good pleasure [*voluntas beneplaciti*: God's will as it is in Himself]; and the explanation already given goes by this sense of the divine will. Secondly, the will of God means that which He wills, or the sign of the divine will. In this sense precept and counsel are called the will of God; and this is not always fulfilled. So we ask that it be fulfilled, saying: [[Matt 6:10|Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven|Fiat voluntas tua sicut in cœlo et in terra]]. The text can also be explained of this will, in this way: [[12:2|that you may prove|Probetis]], by carrying it out, [[12:2|what is|quæ sit]] […] [a few words are lost in the transcription], that is, the command, counsel or prohibition of the divine will: which command, counsel, etc., is [[12:2|good|bona]], in so far as it concerns the goods of nature and the state of beginners; it is also [[12:2|acceptable|beneplacens]] to God and to good men, as it regards the goods of grace and the state of those making progress; it is also [[12:2|perfect|perfecta]], as it regards the goods of glory, which it commands to be sought as the final end, and the state of the perfect [beginners, the proficient and the perfect: the three classical stages of the spiritual life]. Whoever leads a holy and inward life knows and tastes by experience what pleases God and what displeases Him. For while he has no remorse, but serves God carefully and delights in Him, detesting every sin, the Holy Ghost bears him witness that his will is united with God and in accord with Him. Hence the Saviour says: [[John 7:17|If any man will do the will of him, he shall know of the doctrine, whether it be of God|Si quis voluerit voluntatem Dei facere, cognoscet de doctrina an ex Deo sit]].

paras.t: Consequenter jubet Apostolus, ut omne obsequium et exercitium nostrum internum sit rationabile seu discretum. Dico enim, id est præcipio, per gratiam quæ data est mihi, id est apostolica auctoritate mihi gratiose collata, omnibus qui sunt inter vos, Judæis et gentilibus ad fidem conversis, non plus sapere quam oportet sapere, id est non magis investigare, discutere, contemplari divina mysteria fideique arcana, quam oportet vel expedit, quam Scriptura docet, quam intellectus vester capere valet. Propter quod Dionysius et Damascenus testantur : Non est audendum aliquid de supersubstantiali Deitate asserere, præter ea quæ nobis in sacris eloquiis tradita sunt. Denique scrutator majestatis opprimetur a gloria, tanquam temerarius et præsumptor. Idcirco legitur : Altiora te ne quæsieris, et fortiora te ne scrutatus fueris ; sed quæ præcepit tibi Deus, illa cogita semper. Per hæc tamen et similia non prohibetur humilis perscrutatio, profunda et diligens inquisitio sacræ Scripturæ in locis difficilibus, et in his quæ hujusmodi loca concernunt, quum dicat Psalmista : Mirabilia testimonia tua, ideo scrutata est ea anima mea. Sed semper in tali studio innitendum est auxilio gratiæ Dei. Propter quod ait idem Psalmographus : Revela oculos meos, et considerabo mirabilia de lege tua. Sed sapere ad sobrietatem, Et unicuique vestrum præcipio sapere, sicut Deus divisit mensuram fidei, id est secundum modum quem fides docet esse servandum in hoc, ut scilicet unusquisque secundum exigentiam sui officii occupet se in perscrutatione divinorum. Vel, Secundum mensuram fidei, id est secundum qualitatem donorum quæ per fidem præstantur. Qui enim majora dona sapientiæ et scientiæ receperunt, profundius investigare possunt divina quam simplices : imo ut asserit Dionysius, quod uni cibus est, hoc alteri est venenum.
paras.en: Next the Apostle commands that all our inward service and exercise be reasonable, that is, discreet. [[12:3|For I say|Dico enim]], that is, I command, [[12:3|by the grace that is given me|per gratiam quæ data est mihi]], that is, by the apostolic authority graciously conferred on me, [[12:3|to all that are among you|omnibus qui sunt inter vos]], Jews and Gentiles converted to the faith, [[12:3|not to be more wise than it behoveth to be wise|non plus sapere quam oportet sapere]], that is, not to search into, discuss or contemplate the divine mysteries and the secrets of the faith more than is fitting or expedient, more than Scripture teaches, more than your understanding can grasp. For this reason Dionysius and Damascene testify: One must not dare to assert anything of the supersubstantial Godhead beyond what has been handed down to us in the sacred words. Moreover, [[Prov 25:27|he that is a searcher of majesty shall be overwhelmed by glory|scrutator majestatis opprimetur a gloria]], as rash and presumptuous. So we read: [[Ecclus 3:22|Seek not the things that are too high for thee, and search not into things above thy ability: but the things that God hath commanded thee, think on them always|Altiora te ne quæsieris, et fortiora te ne scrutatus fueris ; sed quæ præcepit tibi Deus, illa cogita semper]]. Yet by these and like words humble searching is not forbidden, nor deep and careful inquiry into Holy Scripture in its difficult places and in what concerns such places, since the Psalmist says: [[Ps 118:129|Thy testimonies are wonderful: therefore my soul hath sought them|Mirabilia testimonia tua, ideo scrutata est ea anima mea]]. But in such study one must always lean on the help of the grace of God. For this reason the same Psalmist says: [[Ps 118:18|Open thou my eyes: and I will consider the wondrous things of thy law|Revela oculos meos, et considerabo mirabilia de lege tua]]. [[12:3|but to be wise unto sobriety|Sed sapere ad sobrietatem]]. [[12:3|and according as God hath divided to every one the measure of faith|et unicuique sicut Deus divisit mensuram fidei]]: to each of you I command to be wise according as God hath divided the measure of faith, that is, according to the measure which faith teaches must be kept in this: namely, that each should busy himself with searching into divine things according to the needs of his office. Or, according to the measure of faith, that is, according to the quality of the gifts given through faith. For those who have received greater gifts of wisdom and knowledge can search into divine things more deeply than simple folk: indeed, as Dionysius asserts, what is food to one is poison to another.

paras.t: Quod autem diversis diversa data sint dona mensurate divisa, diversos actus habentia, ostendit per simile in corpore humano. Sicut enim in uno corpore naturali, organico, animato, multa membra, videlicet oculos, manus, pedes, habemus, omnia autem membra non eumdem actum habent ; ita multi fideles unum corpus mysticum, caritate connexum, sumus in Christo capite nostro, a quo motum virtutum et vitam gratiæ participamus, sicut a capite cetera membra motum et vitam naturalem recipiunt ; singuli autem sumus alter alterius membra, id est, unusquisque nostrum est membrum alterius mysticum, puta per similitudinem spiritualem : quoniam sicut unum membrum servit atque communicat alteri suam utilitatem, ut oculus videt toti corpori, manus operantur pro sustentatione totius corporis ; sic unus fidelium communicare debet alteri dona sibi concessa, quemadmodum Petrus hortatur : Unusquisque sicut accepit gratiam, in alterutrum illam administrantes. Gratiæ etenim gratis datæ, quamvis aliquibus specialiter dentur, ordinantur tamen ad commodum aliorum.
paras.en: That different gifts, divided by measure, have been given to different people, with different acts, he shows by a comparison with the human body. [[12:4|For as in one body|Sicut enim in uno corpore]], natural, organic, living, [[12:4|we have many members|multa membra habemus]], namely eyes, hands, feet, [[12:4|but all the members have not the same office|omnia autem membra non eumdem actum habent]]; [[12:5|So we, being many, are one body in Christ|ita multi … unum corpus … sumus in Christo]], many faithful, one mystical body joined by charity, in Christ our head, from whom we share the motion of the virtues and the life of grace, as the other members receive motion and natural life from the head[[Eph 4:15||]][[Eph 4:16||]]; [[12:5|and every one members one of another|singuli autem sumus alter alterius membra]], that is, each of us is a mystical member of the other, by a spiritual likeness: since just as one member serves another and shares its usefulness with it, as the eye sees for the whole body and the hands work for the upkeep of the whole body, so one of the faithful should share with another the gifts granted to him, as Peter urges: [[1 Pet 4:10|As every man hath received grace, ministering the same one to another|Unusquisque sicut accepit gratiam, in alterutrum illam administrantes]]. For graces freely given [*gratiæ gratis datæ*: gifts such as prophecy or tongues, given for the good of others rather than for the holiness of the one who has them], though given to some in particular, are ordained to the benefit of others.
