First, because by His passion […] [a few words are lost at the page break, probably "He merited"] such lordship, even though He had it before. For it is not unfitting that the same thing should belong to someone for different reasons. Secondly, because after the passion Christ's lordship began to be shown and known everywhere. For this reason He says: [[Matt 28:18|All power is given to me in heaven and in earth|Data est mihi omnis potestas in cœlo et in terra]]. It can also be explained thus: [[14:9|that he might be Lord both of the dead and of the living|Ut et vivorum et mortuorum dominetur]], that is, that He might engage in His service the spiritually living and dead, namely the just and the wicked. So He Himself says: [[John 12:32|if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all things to myself|si exaltatus fuero a terra, omnia traham ad me ipsum]].

paras.t: Quum ergo Christus constitutus sit omnium judex, Tu autem, judicande, quid, id est, qua temeritate, quo fructu, judicas sententia definitiva fratrem tuum? Aut tu quare spernis fratrem tuum, tanquam peccatorem aut vilem? Unde scriptum est : Væ qui spernis, nonne et ipse sperneris? Quum fatigatus desieris contemnere, contemneris. Et alius Propheta : Numquid non pater unus omnium nostrum? numquid non Deus unus creavit nos? Quare ergo despicit unusquisque nostrum fratrem suum? Male ergo agis, o homo, judicando spernendoque proximum. Omnes enim stabimus ante tribunal Christi, id est coram Christo sedente in sede judiciaria in die judicii, tanquam judicandi ab eo. Tribunal autem est sedes judicis. Quod vero jam dicitur quod omnes stabimus ante tribunal Christi tanquam judicandi, intelligendum est, vel de judicio condemnationis, vel remunerationis. Scriptura autem frequenter per judicium, intelligit damnationis judicium, sicut ibi : Omnis qui credit in eum, non judicatur; et, Si nosipsos judicaremus, non utique judicaremur.
paras.en: Since, then, Christ has been appointed judge of all[[Acts 10:42||]], [[14:10|But thou, why judgest thou thy brother|Tu autem … quid … judicas … fratrem tuum]]: but you, who are to be judged, why, that is, with what rashness, to what profit, do you judge your brother with a final sentence? [[14:10|Or thou, why dost thou despise thy brother|Aut tu quare spernis fratrem tuum]], as a sinner or a worthless man? So it is written: [[Is 33:1|Woe to thee|Væ]] [[Is 33:1|thou that despisest, shalt not thyself also be despised|qui spernis, nonne et ipse sperneris]]? [[Is 33:1|when being wearied thou shalt cease to despise, thou shalt be despised|Quum fatigatus desieris contemnere, contemneris]]. And another Prophet: [[Mal 2:10|Have we not all one father? hath not one God created us? why then doth every one of us despise his brother|Numquid non pater unus omnium nostrum? numquid non Deus unus creavit nos? Quare ergo despicit unusquisque nostrum fratrem suum]]? You do wrong, then, O man, in judging and despising your neighbour. [[14:10|For we shall all stand before the judgment seat of Christ|Omnes enim stabimus ante tribunal Christi]], that is, before Christ seated on the judgment seat on the day of judgment, as men to be judged by Him. A tribunal is the judge's seat. What is said here, that we shall all stand before the judgment seat of Christ as men to be judged, is to be understood either of the judgment of condemnation or of reward. But Scripture often means by judgment the judgment of damnation, as here: [[John 3:18|He that believeth in him is not judged|Omnis qui credit in eum, non judicatur]]; and, [[1 Cor 11:31|if we would judge ourselves, we should not be judged|Si nosipsos judicaremus, non utique judicaremur]].

paras.t: Scriptum est enim in Isaia : Vivo ego, dicit Dominus, id est juro per me ipsum, qui major est per quem jurem non habeo, quoniam mihi flectetur omne genu, cœlestium, terrestrium et infernorum, id est, omnia mihi subjicientur, præsertim […] bitur Domino, id est, omnis conscientia confitebitur mihi tunc opera sua ; vel, Omnis lingua, id est omne genus hominum, cujuscumque loquelæ, confitebitur Domino, confessione laudis divinæ, vel propriæ culpæ. Nostra translatio est talis : In memetipso juravi : egredietur de ore meo justitiæ verbum, et non revertetur, quia mihi curvabitur omne genu, et jurabit omnis lingua. Quod licet ad litteram dictum videatur de conversione, adoratione et genuflexione omnium gentium in primo Christi adventu et tempore prædicationis evangelicæ, Apostolus tamen Spiritu Sancto copiosissime adimpletus, præsenti loco insinuat hoc posse intelligi de subjectione et adductione omnium hominum in secundo Christi adventu.
paras.en: [[14:11|For it is written|Scriptum est enim]] in Isaias[[Is 45:23||]]: [[14:11|As I live, saith the Lord|Vivo ego, dicit Dominus]], that is, I swear by Myself, for I have none greater by whom to swear[[Heb 6:13||]] [the margin has a bare "13" here: apparently Heb 6:13, "he swore by himself"], [[14:11|every knee shall bow to me|mihi flectetur omne genu]], [[Phil 2:10|of those that are in heaven, on earth, and under the earth|cœlestium, terrestrium et infernorum]] [Denis adds these words from Phil 2:10], that is, all things will be made subject to Me, above all […] [the transcription loses the words at the page break, with "and every tongue shall confess"] to the Lord, that is, every conscience will then confess its works to Me; or, every tongue, that is, every race of men, of whatever speech, [[14:11|shall confess to God|confitebitur Domino]] with the confession of divine praise, or of its own guilt. Our translation reads: [[Is 45:23|I have sworn by myself, the word of justice shall go out of my mouth, and shall not return|In memetipso juravi : egredietur de ore meo justitiæ verbum, et non revertetur]], [[Is 45:24|For every knee shall be bowed to me, and every tongue shall swear|quia mihi curvabitur omne genu, et jurabit omnis lingua]]. Though this seems to be said literally of the conversion, adoration and bending of the knee of all nations at Christ's first coming and in the time of the preaching of the Gospel, the Apostle, filled most abundantly with the Holy Ghost, hints in this place that it can be understood of the subjection and bringing in of all men at Christ's second coming.

paras.t: Itaque unusquisque nostrum pro se rationem reddet Deo, id est, reddere compelletur seu exigetur. Multi tamen non poterunt rationem reddere Deo de actibus suis, quia omnino irrationabiliter vixerunt. Aliqui etiam non exigentur reddere rationem, vel quia nullam culpam habebunt, et in hac vita satisfecerunt ; vel quia infideles fuerunt, et jam judicati sunt, qui in die judicii non judicabuntur judicio discussionis. Non ergo amplius invicem judicemus judicio usurpato vel temerario ; sed hoc judicate magis, id est, bonum et observandum esse discernite, ne ponatis offendiculum, id est occasionem peccati, fratri, id est proximo, viro vel feminæ, vel scandalum, id est occasionem tristitiæ. Communiter autem unum pro alio sumitur.
paras.en: [[14:12|Therefore every one of us shall render account to God for himself|Itaque unusquisque nostrum pro se rationem reddet Deo]], that is, will be compelled or required to render it. Yet many will not be able to render an account to God of their acts, because they lived altogether without reason [*rationem reddere*, "to render an account", is literally "to give a reason"]. Some too will not be required to render an account: either because they will have no guilt and made satisfaction in this life; or because they were unbelievers and are already judged[[John 3:18||]], who on the day of judgment will not be judged with the judgment of discussion [that is, of examining their deeds]. [[14:13|Let us not therefore judge one another any more|Non ergo amplius invicem judicemus]] with a usurped or rash judgment; [[14:13|But judge this rather|sed hoc judicate magis]], that is, discern this to be good and to be kept, [[14:13|that you put not a stumblingblock|ne ponatis offendiculum]], that is, an occasion of sin, [[14:13|in your brother's way|fratri]], that is, before your neighbour, man or woman, [[14:13|or a scandal|vel scandalum]], that is, an occasion of sadness. But commonly the one is taken for the other.

paras.t: Advertendum vero, quod duplex est scandalum, puta activum et passivum. Scandalum activum est dictum vel factum minus rectum, præbens alteri occasionem ruinæ : et de hoc scandalo non est dubium quin sit semper vitandum. Scandalum vero passivum, est malum seu casus quem alter incurrit ex dicto vel facto alterius. De hoc scandalo quæstio est an sit semper vitandum. — Pro quo sciendum, quod scandalum passivum est duplex : Unum, quod nascitur ex malitia scandalizati, qui ex sua perversitate non vult dicta seu facta alterius, quamvis bona, bene interpretari : quod appellatur scandalum Pharisæorum. Alterum, quod nascitur ex infirmitate vel ignorantia scandalizati : quod dicitur scandalum pusillorum. Præterea quædam sunt bona spiritualia, quædam temporalia : et utraque sunt duplicia. Nam spiritualium bonorum quædam sunt de necessitate salutis, ut observatio præceptorum in omnibus, et consiliorum in religiosis. Hæc ergo bona nullo modo omittenda sunt propter quodcumque scandalum evitandum. Plus enim tenetur homo providere propriæ salutis, quam alienæ. Quædam vero non sunt de necessitate salutis : et hæc ad tempus occultanda vel deserenda sunt propter scandalum pusillorum vitandum, videlicet donec ratio eis reddatur, et melius informentur. Si vero ratione reddita non acquiescunt, nec cessant scandalizari, non erit scandalum tale amplius ex ignorantia vel infirmitate, sed ex eorum malitia. Propter quod bona ista omittenda non sunt propter scandalum tale vitandum : sicut nec Christus vitare curavit scandalum Pharisæorum. Similiter bonorum temporalium quædam aliquibus committuntur conservanda, ut bona Ecclesiæ prælatis, bona rei publicæ rectoribus, et deposita certis personis. Et quia ad horum conservationem homo tenetur, ideo propter nullius scandalum sunt deserenda. Unde B. Thomas Cantuariensis repetivit bona Ecclesiæ cum ingenti scandalo regis. Alia bona temporalia sunt nostra : et ista omittenda sunt, vel dando ea aliis, vel non repetendo si alius ea habet, propter vitandum scandalum pusillorum ; vel scandalum tale sedandum est bono modo. Non autem propter scandalum ex malitia nascens, dimittenda sunt bona propria temporalia. Daretur enim perversis libertas et magna occasio retinendi aut rapiendi bona aliorum : quod maxime obesset eorum saluti.
paras.en: It is to be noted that scandal is twofold, namely active and passive. Active scandal is a word or deed less than right, giving another an occasion of falling: and there is no doubt that this scandal is always to be avoided. Passive scandal is the evil or fall that another incurs from the word or deed of someone else. About this scandal the question is whether it is always to be avoided. For this it must be known that passive scandal is twofold. One kind arises from the malice of the one scandalized, who out of his perversity will not take another's words or deeds, though good, in a good sense: this is called the scandal of the Pharisees. The other arises from the weakness or ignorance of the one scandalized: this is called the scandal of the little ones. Further, some goods are spiritual, some temporal, and each kind is twofold. For of spiritual goods some are necessary for salvation, as the keeping of the precepts in all, and of the counsels in religious. These goods, then, are in no way to be given up to avoid any scandal whatever. For a man is more bound to provide for his own salvation than for another's. Others are not necessary for salvation: and these are to be hidden or left off for a time to avoid the scandal of the little ones, namely until the reason is given them and they are better informed. But if, when the reason has been given, they do not accept it and do not cease to be scandalized, such scandal will no longer come from ignorance or weakness but from their malice. So these goods are not to be given up to avoid such scandal: just as Christ did not trouble to avoid the scandal of the Pharisees[[Matt 15:13||]][[Matt 15:14||]]. Likewise, of temporal goods some are entrusted to certain people to be kept, as the goods of the Church to prelates, the goods of the commonwealth to rulers, and deposits to certain persons. And because a man is bound to keep these, they are not to be given up because of anyone's scandal. So blessed Thomas of Canterbury reclaimed the goods of the Church to the great scandal of the king. Other temporal goods are our own: and these are to be given up, either by giving them to others or by not reclaiming them if another has them, to avoid the scandal of the little ones; or such scandal is to be calmed in a good way. But one's own temporal goods are not to be given up because of scandal born of malice. For that would give the perverse freedom and a great occasion to keep or seize the goods of others, which would do the greatest harm to their salvation.

paras.t: Scio per rationem, et confido in Domino Jesu per gratiam ejus, quia nihil commune, id est, nullus cibus humanæ vitæ aptus, immundus est, per ipsum, id est per creationem ipsius. Omnia enim per ipsum facta sunt valde bona. Vel minus dicit, et majus significat, ut sit sensus: Nihil commune per ipsum, id est, omnia munda facta sunt per ejus adventum, omnes videlicet cibi apti, in legali prohibiti. Christus enim absolvit a legali prohibitione ciborum, juxta illud: Quæ Deus purificavit, tu commune ne dixeris. Nisi ei qui existimat quid commune esse, id est aliquem cibum esse immundum propter legis præceptum, illi sic existimanti commune, id est immundum, est aliquid alimentorum, secundum suam opinionem et conscientiam. Sicut fricare barbam illicitum est ei qui hoc putat illicitum, quamdiu sic putat, quia contra conscientiam faceret, si fricaret.
paras.en: [[14:14|I know|Scio]] by reason, [[14:14|and am confident in the Lord Jesus|et confido in Domino Jesu]] by His grace, [[14:14|that nothing is unclean|quia nihil commune]] [*commune*, "common", that is, ritually unclean], that is, no food fit for human life is unclean, [[14:14|of itself|per ipsum]] [Denis reads *per ipsum* as "through Him", that is, through Christ], that is, through His creation. For [[John 1:3|All things were made by him|Omnia enim per ipsum facta sunt]], [[Gen 1:31|very good|valde bona]]. Or he says less and means more, so that the sense is: nothing is common through Him, that is, all things have been made clean by His coming, namely all fit foods that were forbidden in the law. For Christ set us free from the legal prohibition of foods, according to the words: [[Acts 10:15|That which God hath cleansed, do not thou call common|Quæ Deus purificavit, tu commune ne dixeris]]. [[14:14|but to him that esteemeth any thing to be unclean|Nisi ei qui existimat quid commune esse]], that is, that some food is unclean because of the precept of the law, [[14:14|to him it is unclean|illi … commune … est]]: to him who thinks so, some food is common, that is, unclean, according to his opinion and conscience. Just as rubbing one's beard is unlawful for one who thinks it unlawful, as long as he thinks so, because he would act against his conscience if he rubbed it.

paras.t: Si enim propter cibum, id est, ob hoc quod quemlibet cibum indiscrete manducas, vel ab aliquibus abstines, frater, id est proximus, tuus contristatur, putans te impie agere, et nesciens quid debeat securius facere, quum tamen licite possis alterum horum eligere, sicque fratris tui contristationem vitare; jam non secundum caritatem ambulas, id est, non caritative te habes, quia non vitas offensam fratris, sed ejus saluti præponis cibum tuum. Noli cibo tuo, id est usu vel abstinentia cibi, illum perdere, id est ad mortale peccatum inducere, pro quo Christus mortuus est, ne videaris pretium mortis et sanguinis Christi parvi pendere.
paras.en: [[14:15|For if, because of thy meat|Si enim propter cibum]], that is, because you eat any food without distinction, or abstain from some, [[14:15|thy brother be grieved|frater tuus contristatur]], your brother, that is, your neighbour, thinking that you act wickedly, and not knowing what he ought more safely to do, when you could lawfully choose either of these and so avoid grieving your brother; [[14:15|thou walkest not now according to charity|jam non secundum caritatem ambulas]], that is, you do not behave with charity, because you do not avoid offending your brother, but put your food before his salvation. [[14:15|Destroy not him with thy meat|Noli cibo tuo illum perdere]], that is, by eating or abstaining from food, do not lead him into mortal sin, [[14:15|for whom Christ died|pro quo Christus mortuus est]], lest you seem to think little of the price of Christ's death and blood.

paras.t: Non ergo blasphemetur, id est, contra Dei honorem vituperetur, bonum nostrum, id est fama nostra. Scriptum est enim: Melius est nomen bonum, quam divitiæ multæ; et alibi: Cura habe de bono nomine; hoc enim magis proderit tibi quam mille thesauri. Porro, ut ait Ambrosius, qui habet opera bona, si reprehendatur in re minima, bonum suum offuscat, et incipit bonum ejus blasphemari. Propterea virtuoso vitanda sunt minima.
paras.en: [[14:16|Let not then our good be evil spoken of|Non ergo blasphemetur bonum nostrum]]: let it not be reviled against the honour of God, our good, that is, our good name. For it is written: [[Prov 22:1|A good name is better than great riches|Melius est nomen bonum, quam divitiæ multæ]]; and elsewhere: [[Ecclus 41:15|Take care of a good name|Cura habe de bono nomine]]; for this will profit thee more [[Ecclus 41:15|than a thousand treasures|quam mille thesauri]]. Further, as Ambrose says, he who has good works, if he is blamed in a very small thing, darkens his good, and his good begins to be evil spoken of. So the virtuous man must avoid even the smallest things.

paras.t: Ideo autem non debes cibo tuo proximum perdere: Non est enim regnum Dei, id est regnatio et inhabitatio Dei in anima tua, esca et potus, id est victus exterior. Esca namque non commendat nos Deo; nec cibus damnatur, sed concupiscentia immoderata. Ideo subditur: sed justitia, reddens Deo quæ Dei sunt; proximo, quæ proximi sunt; et sibi ipsi, quæ expediunt; et pax, id est vera tranquillitas mentis; et gaudium quod habetur in Spiritu Sancto, id est per gratiam Spiritus Sancti ex contemplatione et dilectione divinorum. Ista sunt regnum Dei, quia per ista regnat Deus in nobis, quemadmodum ait Scriptura: Regnum Dei intra vos est. Vel sic: Non est enim regnum Dei causaliter esca et potus, id est, per ista non acquiritur regnum cœlorum; sed justitia et pax, et gaudium in Spiritu Sancto, sunt regnum Dei, quia per talia regnum cœlorum obtinetur. Qui enim in hoc regno Dei, id est in justitia, pace et gaudio spirituali, servit Christo, non scandalizans aliquem propter cibum seu cibi delectationem, vel aliam irrationabilem causam, placet Deo, quia beneplacitum est Domino in populo suo; et probatus, est hominibus, quia exemplaris est ipsis, et laudatur ab eis.
paras.en: You must not destroy your neighbour with your food for this reason: [[14:17|For the kingdom of God|Non est enim regnum Dei]], that is, God's reigning and dwelling in your soul, [[14:17|is not meat and drink|Non est enim regnum Dei causaliter esca et potus]], that is, outward nourishment. For [[1 Cor 8:8|meat doth not commend us to God|Esca namque non commendat nos Deo]]; nor is food condemned, but immoderate desire. So it is added: [[14:17|but justice|sed justitia]], rendering [[Matt 22:21|to God, the things that are God's|Deo quæ Dei sunt]], to one's neighbour what is his, and to oneself what is expedient; [[14:17|and peace|et pax]], that is, true tranquillity of mind; [[14:17|and joy in the Holy Ghost|et gaudium in Spiritu Sancto]], joy which is had in the Holy Ghost, that is, through the grace of the Holy Ghost, from the contemplation and love of divine things. These are the kingdom of God, because through them God reigns in us, as Scripture says: [[Luke 17:21|the kingdom of God is within you|Regnum Dei intra vos est]]. Or thus: the kingdom of God is not meat and drink causally, that is, the kingdom of heaven is not gained by them; but justice and peace and joy in the Holy Ghost are the kingdom of God, because by such things the kingdom of heaven is obtained. [[14:18|For he that in this|Qui enim in hoc]] kingdom of God, that is, in justice, peace and spiritual joy, [[14:18|serveth Christ|servit Christo]], not scandalizing anyone over food or the pleasure of food, or for any other unreasonable cause, [[14:18|pleaseth God|placet Deo]], because [[Ps 149:4|the Lord is well pleased with his people|beneplacitum est Domino in populo suo]]; [[14:18|and is approved of men|et probatus est hominibus]], because he is an example to them and is praised by them.

paras.t: Itaque, quæ pacis sunt, id est ea quæ pacem pariunt, fovent, conservant, sectemur et operemur. Beati enim pacifici, quoniam filii Dei vocabuntur. In pace namque vocavit nos Dominus, et non est Deus dissensionis, sed pacis. Unde per Prophetam Dominus loquitur: Veritatem tantum et pacem diligite. Et quæ ædificationis sunt, id est, ad bonum provocant, videlicet morum probitatem, custodiamus, ut alterutrum, non tantum alium non scandalizet, sed spiritualiter eum ædificet.
paras.en: [[14:19|Therefore, let us follow after the things that are of peace|Itaque quæ pacis sunt, sectemur]], that is, let us pursue and do the things that bring forth, foster and keep peace. For [[Matt 5:9|Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God|Beati enim pacifici, quoniam filii Dei vocabuntur]]. For [[1 Cor 7:15|God hath called us in peace|In pace namque vocavit nos Dominus]], and [[1 Cor 14:33|God is not the God of dissension, but of peace|non est Deus dissensionis, sed pacis]]. So the Lord speaks through the Prophet: [[Zach 8:19|only love ye truth and peace|Veritatem tantum et pacem diligite]]. [[14:19|and keep the things that are of edification|et quæ ædificationis sunt, in invicem custodiamus]], that is, the things that stir to good, namely uprightness of conduct, [[14:19|one towards another|alterutrum]], so that each not only does not scandalize the other, but builds him up spiritually.

paras.t: Ideo, Noli, o homo, [...] id est amore cibi, destruere opus Dei, id est fratrem tuum spiritualiter occidere, seu fidem et gratiam ejus exstinguere. Omnia quidem cibaria munda sunt et licita, in quantum sunt creaturæ boni Dei ; sed malum, id est nocivum, est homini quæcumque cibaria sumere, qui per offendiculum manducat, id est, manducando fratrem suum scandalizat, et Deum offendit, sicut malum erat primo parenti de fructu ligni vitæ comedere. Ne autem quis putet simpliciter utile esse vel melius quolibet cibo et potu uti, eo quod omnia munda sint, adjecit : Bonum est non manducare carnem, et non bibere vinum : per hoc enim concupiscentia minoratur, corpus castigatur, et gratia obtinetur; neque manducare et bibere id in quo frater tuus offenditur, id est, impedimentum seu obicem proficiendi in via Dei incurrit, aut scandalizatur, id est, cadit peccando : quod est majus et gravius quam offendere; potest enim quis pede in aliquid impingere, nec cadere ; aut infirmatur in fide, hæsitans quid sit tenendum : quod valde pœnale periculosumque est.
paras.en: So: [[14:20|Destroy not|Noli]], O man, […] [a word or two of the lemma, "for meat", are lost in the transcription], that is, out of love of food, [[14:20|the work of God|destruere opus Dei]], that is, do not kill your brother spiritually, or extinguish his faith and grace. [[14:20|All things indeed are clean|Omnia quidem cibaria munda sunt]], all foods, and lawful, in so far as they are creatures of the good God; [[14:20|but it is evil for that man|sed malum est homini]], that is, harmful, to take any food whatever, [[14:20|who eateth with offence|qui per offendiculum manducat]], that is, who by eating scandalizes his brother and offends God: as it was evil for our first parent to eat of the fruit of the tree [the transcription has *ligni vitæ*, "of the tree of life"; the forbidden tree was that of the knowledge of good and evil]. Lest anyone think that it is simply useful or better to use any food and drink because all things are clean, he added: [[14:21|It is good not to eat flesh and not to drink wine|Bonum est non manducare carnem, et non bibere vinum]]: for by this concupiscence is lessened, the body chastised, and grace obtained; [[14:21|nor any thing whereby thy brother is offended|neque manducare et bibere id in quo frater tuus offenditur]] [Denis's text: "nor to eat and drink that whereby thy brother is offended"], that is, meets a hindrance or obstacle to progress in the way of God, [[14:21|or scandalized|aut scandalizatur]], that is, falls by sinning: which is greater and graver than being offended, for one can strike one's foot against something and not fall; [[14:21|or made weak|aut infirmatur]] in faith, wavering as to what is to be held: which is very grievous and dangerous.

paras.t: Consequenter hortatur Apostolus ad hoc. Tu fidem quam habes penes temetipsum, id est, intra te firmiter credis omnes cibos per Christum purificatos seu licitos factos, habe coram Deo, id est, sufficiat tibi hanc fidem habere in cordis secreto, Deo spectante, nec fratri tuo aliter æstimanti eam ostendas, ne scandalizetur. Beatus est jam in spe, bene agendo, qui non judicat, id est, damnabilem facit, semetipsum, alium scandalizando, in eo quod probat, id est faciendo quod licitum esse cognoscit in se, quamvis sit illicitum propter scandalum evitandum. Vel sic : Beatus qui non judicat, id est non redarguit, semetipsum in eo quod probat, hoc est approbat, id est, qui nihil agit contra conscientiam suam. Qui autem discernit, id est, judicat quosdam cibos vitandos, si manducaverit tales cibos, damnatus est causaliter, id est, peccando mortaliter damnari promeruit; quia manducat non ex fide, id est contra id quod secundum fidem et conscientiam suam sentit agendum. Omne autem quod non est ex fide, id est, quod fit contra fidem, et propter finem contrarium fini quem edocet fides, peccatum est, quia inordinatum et contra legem divinam.
paras.en: Next the Apostle exhorts to this. [[14:22|Hast thou faith|Tu fidem quam habes]] with yourself, that is, do you firmly believe within yourself that all foods have been cleansed by Christ, that is, made lawful? [[14:22|Have it to thyself before God|penes temetipsum habe coram Deo]]: that is, let it be enough for you to have this faith in the secret of your heart, with God looking on, and do not show it to your brother who thinks otherwise, lest he be scandalized. [[14:22|Blessed is he|Beatus]] now in hope, by doing well, [[14:22|that condemneth not himself|qui non judicat semetipsum]], that is, does not make himself damnable by scandalizing another, [[14:22|in that which he alloweth|in eo quod probat]], that is, by doing what he knows to be lawful in itself, though it is unlawful because scandal must be avoided. Or thus: blessed is he who does not judge, that is, does not reproach, himself in that which he approves, that is, who does nothing against his conscience. [[14:23|But he that discerneth|Qui autem discernit]], that is, judges that certain foods are to be avoided, [[14:23|if he eat|si manducaverit]] such foods, [[14:23|is condemned|damnatus est]] causally, that is, by sinning mortally he has deserved to be damned; [[14:23|because not of faith|quia manducat non ex fide]], because he eats not of faith, that is, against what he feels he should do according to his faith and conscience. [[14:23|For all that is not of faith|Omne autem quod non est ex fide]], that is, what is done against faith, and for an end contrary to the end which faith teaches, [[14:23|is sin|peccatum est]], because it is disordered and against the divine law.

paras.t: Circa hæc duo quæruntur : primo, utrum ratio seu conscientia errans obliget; secundo, an quælibet actio infidelium sit peccatum. — Et respondendum ad primum, quod operatio recipit speciem a termino ad quem, rationem autem boni vel mali moralis sumit ab intentione agentis, seu formali ratione objecti. Quum ergo ratio dicit aliquid bonum vel malum, quamvis ita non sit : tamen si voluntas fertur in id quod ratio ei proponit sub ratione mali, licet sit bonum, certum est quod fertur in illud sub ratione mali, et ideo formaliter peccat : quemadmodum putans falsum asserere, mentitur etiam si verum dicat, eo quod falsum dicere æstimet. Simile est, si quis bonum agat, putans illud esse malum : peccat enim. Ideo ratio seu errans conscientia obligat. Non est tamen homo perplexus, id est necessitate peccandi adstrictus, quoniam potest errorem rationis abjicere. — Ad secundum dicendum, quod infidelitas, sicut et cetera peccata mortalia, aufert vitam gratiæ, non autem tollit bonum naturæ. Quamvis ergo infidelis non agat aliquid meritorie, potest tamen facere opus bonum in genere moris, seu bonum morale, ad quod se extendit naturalis potentia. Et in tali actu non peccat directe, et per se : ut si honoret parentes, vestiat nudum, cibet esurientem. Quidquid vero refert ad finem suæ perfidiæ, in eo peccat, quamvis sit bonum : nam finis perversus est. Quod ergo nunc ait Apostolus, Omne quod non est ex fide, peccatum est, et quod Glossa adjecit, Omnis infidelium vita peccatum est, accipiendum est secundum sensum prætactum, et quia qui fidem non habet, protinus in diversa peccata collabitur.
paras.en: Two questions are asked about this: first, whether erring reason or conscience binds; second, whether every action of unbelievers is a sin. To the first the answer is that an action receives its species from the term to which it tends, but takes its character of moral good or evil from the intention of the agent, that is, from the formal aspect of its object. When, then, reason says that something is good or evil, though it is not so, still, if the will is borne towards what reason puts before it under the aspect of evil, even though it is good, it is certain that the will is borne towards it under the aspect of evil, and so it sins formally: as one who thinks he is asserting something false lies even if he says what is true, because he thinks he is saying what is false. It is the same if someone does good thinking it to be evil: for he sins. Therefore erring reason or conscience binds. Yet a man is not perplexed [that is, caught so that he must sin whichever way he chooses], that is, bound by a necessity of sinning, since he can cast off the error of his reason. To the second it must be said that unbelief, like the other mortal sins, takes away the life of grace, but does not take away the good of nature. So although an unbeliever does nothing meritoriously, he can still do a work good in the moral order, that is, a moral good, to which natural power extends. And in such an act he does not sin directly and of itself: as if he honours his parents, clothes the naked, feeds the hungry. But whatever he refers to the end of his unbelief, in that he sins, though it is good: for the end is perverse. What the Apostle says now, then, [[14:23|For all that is not of faith is sin|Omne quod non est ex fide, peccatum est]], and what the Gloss adds, "The whole life of unbelievers is sin," is to be taken in the sense already touched on, and because he who has not faith at once falls into various sins.

15.title: Expositio capituli quintidecimi: Debemus autem nos firmiores, etc.
15.title_en: Explanation of the fifteenth chapter: Now, we that are stronger
15.note: One page of the transcription (on vv. 8–13) is almost wholly unreadable; only fragments of it are given. Please check against the scan.

paras.t: Debemus autem nos firmiores, id est in virtutibus fortiores, imbecillitates, id est defectus et imperfectiones, infirmorum sustinere, id est æquanimiter ferre et sustentare atque erigere, ut sanentur : sicut et alibi dicitur, Libenter suffertis insipientes, quum sitis ipsi sapientes ; et iterum, Alter alterius onera portate. Nam et in corpore naturali, membra fortiora, ut nervi et ossa, sustinent teneriora. Sed quia ex hoc quod aliquis sustinet imperfectionem alterius tanquam infirmioris, protinus insurgere solet inanis gloria, qua quis de sua perfectione stultissime gloriatur, et alteri se præponit ; ideo optime junxit Apostolus : et non nobis placere, id est non habere complacentiam in nobis ad nos ipsos reflexam, nec gloriari in nobis, nec proprium placitum sequi ; sed potius displicere nobis in nobis, quum nihil ex nobis ipsis habeamus, nisi quod merito inducere debet nobis displicentiam nostri. Unde de reprobis scriptum est : Audaces, sibi placentes. Si pensamus proprias imperfectiones et vitia, non placebimus nobismetipsis. Et quo nobis ipsis magis placemus, eo amplius displicemus Deo.
paras.en: [[15:1|Now, we that are stronger ought|Debemus autem nos firmiores]], that is, stronger in the virtues, [[15:1|to bear the infirmities of the weak|imbecillitates infirmorum sustinere]]: the infirmities, that is, the defects and imperfections, of the weak, to bear them, that is, to put up with them calmly, and to support and raise them up, that they may be healed: as it is said elsewhere, [[2 Cor 11:19|you gladly suffer the foolish: whereas yourselves are wise|Libenter suffertis insipientes, quum sitis ipsi sapientes]]; and again, [[Gal 6:2|Bear ye one another's burdens|Alter alterius onera portate]] [the margin's "Galat. v, 2" is vi, 2]. For in the natural body too, the stronger members, such as the sinews and bones, hold up the more tender. But because from the fact that someone bears with another's imperfection as with a weaker man, vainglory is wont to rise at once, by which one most foolishly glories in one's own perfection and sets oneself above the other, the Apostle very fittingly added: [[15:1|and not to please ourselves|et non nobis placere]], that is, not to take a complacency in ourselves turned back upon ourselves, nor to glory in ourselves, nor to follow our own pleasure; but rather to be displeased with ourselves in ourselves, since we have nothing of ourselves except what ought rightly to make us displeased with ourselves. So it is written of the reprobate: [[2 Pet 2:10|audacious, self willed|Audaces, sibi placentes]] [*sibi placentes*, literally "pleasing themselves"]. If we weigh our own imperfections and vices, we shall not please ourselves. And the more we please ourselves, the more we displease God.

paras.t: Unusquisque vestrum proximo suo placeat in bonum, id est ad bonum finem, seu tendendo in opus bonum, ad ædificationem ipsius, ut ex vobis sumat profectum. Etenim Christus secundum quod homo, non sibi in se placuit, id est, in se ipso gloriatus non est, quasi a se ipso aliquid habens ; nec proprium placitum, sed Dei Patris voluntatem quæsivit. Ideo enim in Evangelio loquitur : Descendi, non ut faciam voluntatem meam, sed ejus qui misit me ; et, Non potest Filius a se facere quidquam ; et, Ego non quæro gloriam meam, sed quæ placita sunt Patri facio semper ; et, Non quod ego volo, sed quod tu. Et si Christus, qui non solum caruit omni culpa, sed insuper ut homo plenus fuit omni virtute et gratia, sibi ipsi non placuit, cur nos miseri, defectibus pleni, nobismetipsis placemus ?
paras.en: [[15:2|Let every one of you Please his neighbour unto good|Unusquisque vestrum proximo suo placeat in bonum]], that is, for a good end, or by aiming at a good work, [[15:2|to edification|ad ædificationem]], to his edification, that he may draw profit from you. [[15:3|For Christ did not please himself|Etenim Christus … non sibi … placuit]]: for Christ as man did not please Himself in Himself, that is, did not glory in Himself as having anything of Himself; nor did He seek His own pleasure, but the will of God the Father. For this is why He says in the Gospel: [[John 6:38|not to do my own will but the will of him that sent me|non ut faciam voluntatem meam, sed ejus qui misit me]] [Denis: "I came down, not to do …"]; and, [[John 5:19|the Son cannot do any thing of himself|Non potest Filius a se facere quidquam]]; and, [[John 8:50|I seek not my own glory|Ego non quæro gloriam meam]], but [[John 8:29|I do always the things that please him|quæ placita sunt Patri facio semper]]; and, [[Mark 14:36|not what I will, but what thou wilt|Non quod ego volo, sed quod tu]]. And if Christ, who not only was free of all guilt but besides, as man, was full of all virtue and grace, did not please Himself, why do we wretches, full of defects, please ourselves?

paras.t: Sed sicut scriptum est in Psalmo, qui ad litteram de Christi passione conscriptus est : Improperia, id est detractiones, opprobria, injuriæ, improperantium tibi, o Pater æterne, in me : nam Judæi improperando mihi, improperaverunt et tibi. Qui enim non honorificat Filium, non honorificat Patrem, qui misit illum. Improperabant autem Judæi Patri et unigenito Filio ejus, ac Sancto Spiritui, adscribentes miracula Christi dæmonibus, ejusque vitam impiam esse dicentes. Dixerunt enim : Nonne bene dicimus nos, quia Samaritanus es tu, et dæmonium habes ? Et alibi : In Beelzebub principe dæmoniorum ejicit dæmonia. Hæc itaque improperia ceciderunt super me, id est, in mea humanitate habuerunt effectum, et me hominem occiderunt. Tibi enim nocere non potuerunt. Et hoc ideo passus sum, quoniam tuam in omnibus feci voluntatem, increpando vitia Judæorum.
paras.en: [[15:3|but, as it is written|Sed sicut scriptum est]] in the Psalm, which was written literally of Christ's passion[[Ps 68:10||]]: [[15:3|The reproaches|Improperia]], that is, the detractions, insults and injuries, [[15:3|of them that reproached thee|improperantium tibi]], O eternal Father, are upon Me: for the Jews, in reproaching Me, reproached Thee too. For [[John 5:23|He who honoureth not the Son honoureth not the Father who hath sent him|Qui enim non honorificat Filium, non honorificat Patrem, qui misit illum]]. The Jews reproached the Father and His only-begotten Son and the Holy Ghost, ascribing Christ's miracles to demons and saying that His life was wicked. For they said: [[John 8:48|Do not we say well that thou art a Samaritan and hast a devil|Nonne bene dicimus nos, quia Samaritanus es tu, et dæmonium habes]]? And elsewhere: [[Luke 11:15|He casteth out devils by Beelzebub, the prince of devils|In Beelzebub principe dæmoniorum ejicit dæmonia]]. These reproaches, then, [[15:3|fell upon me|ceciderunt super me]], that is, took effect in My humanity, and killed Me as man. For they could not harm Thee. And I suffered this because I did Thy will in all things, rebuking the vices of the Jews.

paras.t: Quæcumque enim scripta sunt. Quasi dicat Apostolus : Merito allegavi scripturam istam de Christo : Quæcumque enim scripta sunt in libris divinis, præsertim de Christo et ejus mysteriis, ad nostram doctrinam, id est informationem, scripta sunt. Nam Christi actio, nostra est instructio. Ut per patientiam in adversis : quam verbis et exemplis docet Scriptura, dicendo, In patientia vestra possidebitis animas vestras; et Jacobus : Exemplum accipite longanimitatis et patientiæ, Prophetas : ecce beatificamus eos qui sustinuerunt; et consolationem Scripturarum consolantium animas studiosas ac pias, quoniam multa jucunda et delectabilia continent : unde primo Machabæorum Jonathas et alii dicebant, Habemus solatio sanctos libros ; spem habeamus, id est certam fiduciam obtinendi gratiam in præsenti, et gloriam in futuro. Omnis namque Scriptura divinitus inspirata, utilis est ad docendum et arguendum, ad erudiendum in justitia, ut perfectus sit homo Dei ad omne opus bonum.
paras.en: [[15:4|For what things soever were written|Quæcumque enim scripta sunt]]. As if the Apostle said: I was right to bring in that passage of Scripture about Christ: for whatever things were written in the divine books, especially about Christ and His mysteries, [[15:4|were written for our learning|ad nostram doctrinam scripta sunt]], that is, our instruction. For Christ's action is our instruction. [[15:4|that, through patience|Ut per patientiam]] in adversity, which Scripture teaches by words and examples, saying, [[Luke 21:19|In your patience you shall possess your souls|In patientia vestra possidebitis animas vestras]]; and James: [[Jas 5:10|Take, my brethren, for example|Exemplum accipite]] of long-suffering and [[Jas 5:10|patience, the prophets|patientiæ, Prophetas]]: [[Jas 5:11|Behold, we account them blessed who have endured|ecce beatificamus eos qui sustinuerunt]]; [[15:4|and the comfort of the scriptures|et consolationem Scripturarum]], which comfort studious and devout souls, since they contain many pleasant and delightful things: so in the first book of Machabees Jonathas and the others said, [[1 Mach 12:9|having for our comfort the holy books|Habemus solatio sanctos libros]]; [[15:4|we might have hope|spem habeamus]], that is, a sure confidence of obtaining grace in the present and glory in the future. For [[2 Tim 3:16|All scripture, inspired of God, is profitable to teach, to reprove|Omnis namque Scriptura divinitus inspirata, utilis est ad docendum et arguendum]], [[2 Tim 3:16|to instruct in justice|ad erudiendum in justitia]], [[2 Tim 3:17|That the man of God may be perfect, furnished to every good work|ut perfectus sit homo Dei ad omne opus bonum]].

paras.t: Porro, ut hanc gratiam consequamur, orat Apostolus : Deus autem patientiæ dator, conservator et remunerator : de quo ait Psalmista, Nonne Deo subjecta erit anima mea? ab ipso enim patientia mea; et, Quoniam tu es patientia mea, Domine ; et solatii, id est consolationis infusor, qui consolatur nos in omni tribulatione nostra : de quo in Tobiæ libro dicitur, Post tempestatem tranquillum facis, et post fletum exsultationem infundis ; det vobis id ipsum sapere in alterutrum, id est idem sentire ad invicem, secundum Jesum Christum, id est secundum voluntatem et doctrinam Salvatoris, non secundum sensum vestrum, ut sitis conformes, et eadem sentientes : juxta illud, Viriliter agite, confortamini, idem sapite. Sic etiam multitudinis credentium erat cor unum et anima una. Hanc identitatem non facit nisi magna gratia Dei, quæ humanarum opinionum, falsitatum, imaginationum et inflationum diversitatem nebulamque expellit, et corda diversa in uno veritatis ac sanctitatis splendore recolligit. Unde ait beatissimus Dionysius, quod sicut lumen naturæ, ratione suæ defectuositatis, est causa diversitatis in assertionibus hominum, sic lumen gratiæ a diversitate in unitatem reducit, et omnes idem asserere facit.
paras.en: Further, that we may obtain this grace, the Apostle prays: [[15:5|Now the God of patience|Deus autem patientiæ]], its giver, keeper and rewarder: of whom the Psalmist says, [[Ps 61:2|Shall not my soul be subject to God? for from him|Nonne Deo subjecta erit anima mea? ab ipso enim]] [[Ps 61:6|is my patience|patientia mea]] [Denis joins vv. 2 and 6 of the Psalm, as the margin shows]; and, [[Ps 70:5|For thou art my patience, O Lord|Quoniam tu es patientia mea, Domine]]; [[15:5|and of comfort|et solatii]], that is, the pourer-in of consolation, [[2 Cor 1:4|Who comforteth us in all our tribulation|qui consolatur nos in omni tribulatione nostra]]: of whom it is said in the book of Tobias, [[Tob 3:22|after a storm thou makest a calm, and after tears and weeping thou pourest in joyfulness|Post tempestatem tranquillum facis, et post fletum exsultationem infundis]]; [[15:5|grant you to be of one mind, one towards another|det vobis id ipsum sapere in alterutrum]], that is, to think the same towards one another, [[15:5|according to Jesus Christ|secundum Jesum Christum]], that is, according to the will and teaching of the Saviour, not according to your own sense, so that you may be conformed and of the same mind: according to the words, [[2 Par 32:7|Behave like men, and take courage|Viriliter agite, confortamini]][[1 Cor 16:13||]], [[2 Cor 13:11|be of one mind|idem sapite]]. So too [[Acts 4:32|the multitude of believers had but one heart and one soul|multitudinis credentium erat cor unum et anima una]]. Nothing but the great grace of God brings about this sameness, which drives out the variety and fog of human opinions, falsehoods, fancies and conceits, and gathers different hearts together in the one splendour of truth and holiness. So the most blessed Dionysius says that just as the light of nature, by reason of its defectiveness, is the cause of diversity in men's assertions, so the light of grace leads back from diversity to unity, and makes all assert the same thing.

paras.t: Ut unanimes, id est affectu et sensu conformes, uno ore, id est simili vocis laudatione, honorificetis Deum et Patrem Domini nostri Jesu Christi, id est Deum Patrem, qui est Deus Christi secundum naturam assumptam, et Pater ipsius, secundum naturam divinam. De quo ait ipse : Ascendo ad Patrem meum et Patrem vestrum, Deum meum et Deum vestrum. Propter quod, videlicet ut Deum unanimiter honorificetis, suscipite invicem, id est, unus suscipiat alium in omni caritate et pietate, mutuo consulendo, condolendo, succurrendo, et cetera opera misericordiæ corporalia ac spiritualia impendendo. Unde prima ad Thessalonicenses ipse ait : Corripite inquietos, consolamini pusillanimes, suscipite infirmos, patientes estote ad omnes. Sicut et Christus suscepit vos sub alis suæ protectionis, sanavitque vos. Qui apud Joannem ait : Eum qui venit ad me non ejiciam foras. Et Isaias ait : Vere languores nostros ipse tulit, et peccata nostra ipse portavit. Denique : Suscepit Israel puerum suum, recordatus misericordiæ suæ. Et David in Psalmo : Misit, inquit, de cœlo, et accepit me, et assumpsit me de aquis multis. In honorem Dei. Hoc ad utrumque refertur, quia et nos debemus suscipere invicem, et Christus suscepit nos, ad honorem et gloriam Dei.
paras.en: [[15:6|That with one mind|Ut unanimes]], that is, conformed in affection and sense, [[15:6|and with one mouth|uno ore]], that is, with like praise of the voice, [[15:6|you may glorify God and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ|honorificetis Deum et Patrem Domini nostri Jesu Christi]], that is, God the Father, who is the God of Christ according to the nature He assumed, and His Father according to the divine nature. Of whom He Himself says: [[John 20:17|I ascend to my Father and to your Father, to my God and to your God|Ascendo ad Patrem meum et Patrem vestrum, Deum meum et Deum vestrum]]. [[15:7|Wherefore|Propter quod]], namely that you may glorify God with one mind, [[15:7|receive one another|suscipite invicem]], that is, let one receive another in all charity and kindness, by counselling one another, feeling for one another, helping, and doing the other bodily and spiritual works of mercy. So he himself says in the first Epistle to the Thessalonians: [[1 Thess 5:14|rebuke the unquiet: comfort the feeble minded: support the weak: be patient towards all men|Corripite inquietos, consolamini pusillanimes, suscipite infirmos, patientes estote ad omnes]]. [[15:7|as Christ also hath received you|Sicut et Christus suscepit vos]] under the wings of His protection, and healed you. He says in John: [[John 6:37|him that cometh to me, I will not cast out|Eum qui venit ad me non ejiciam foras]]. And Isaias says: [[Is 53:4|Surely he hath borne our infirmities and carried our sorrows|Vere languores nostros ipse tulit, et peccata nostra ipse portavit]] [Denis has *peccata*, "sins", for *dolores*]. And again: [[Luke 1:54|He hath received Israel his servant, being mindful of his mercy|Suscepit Israel puerum suum, recordatus misericordiæ suæ]]. And David in the Psalm: [[Ps 17:17|He sent from on high, and took me: and received me out of many waters|Misit, inquit, de cœlo, et accepit me, et assumpsit me de aquis multis]]. [[15:7|unto the honour of God|In honorem Dei]]. This refers to both, because we must receive one another, and Christ received us, to the honour and glory of God.

paras.t: Quod autem Christus susceperit nos, ostendit Apostolus primo de populo Judæorum. Dico enim Christum Jesum ministrum fuisse circumcisionis, id est Deo Patri servisse, secundum formam servilem, in prædicatione qua prædicavit Judæis. Imo et Christus se servum præbuit Judæorum, juxta illud : Ego in medio vestrum sum sicut qui ministrat; et alibi : Filius enim hominis non venit ministrari, sed ministrare. Dicitur ergo Christus minister circumcisionis, id est prædicator atque apostolus Judæorum, ad quos specialiter missum se perhibet, dicens, Non sum missus nisi ad oves quæ perierunt domus Israel : et hoc, propter veritatem Dei, id est, quia Deus ita prædixit, et ut Deus verus esse cognosceretur, ad […]
paras.en: That Christ received us, the Apostle shows first of the Jewish people. [[15:8|For I say that Christ Jesus was minister of the circumcision|Dico enim Christum Jesum ministrum fuisse circumcisionis]], that is, served God the Father, in the form of a servant, in the preaching by which He preached to the Jews. Indeed Christ even made Himself the servant of the Jews, according to the words: [[Luke 22:27|I am in the midst of you, as he that serveth|Ego in medio vestrum sum sicut qui ministrat]]; and elsewhere: [[Matt 20:28|the Son of man is not come to be ministered unto, but to minister|Filius enim hominis non venit ministrari, sed ministrare]]. Christ, then, is called minister of the circumcision, that is, preacher and apostle of the Jews, to whom He declares Himself specially sent, saying, [[Matt 15:24|I was not sent but to the sheep, that are lost of the house of Israel|Non sum missus nisi ad oves quæ perierunt domus Israel]]: and this [[15:8|for the truth of God|propter veritatem Dei]], that is, because God had so foretold, and that God might be known to be true, [[15:8|to confirm|ad]] […] [the next page is almost wholly unreadable in the transcription: the rest of v. 8 and most of the commentary on vv. 9–13 are lost].

paras.t: Gentes autem, id est gentiles conve[…] […] id est gratias agere Deo, eique ser[…] […] mittitur : Deus, qui das vindictas [mihi], et subdis populos sub me, etc.), con[…] hoc tibi Deo Patri in gentibus, id [est] gentes faciam tibi confiteri confess[…] […] quod psalmus ille ad litteram de Ch[risto] loquatur. Apostolus enim per verba […] […] Christo loco suo. […] iterum dicit Dominus per Prophetam in […] Psalmo […] vocatæ, Dominum, et magnifice, id est, magnifice honorate, et verbis ac factis […] [po]puli, hoc est duodecim tribus Israel.
paras.en: [Only fragments of this page can be read in the transcription; they are given here as they stand.] [[15:9|But that the Gentiles|Gentes autem]], that is, the Gentiles conve[rted] … […] … that is, to give thanks to God, and to serve Him … […] … [a verse of the Psalm] … *O God, who avengest me, and subduest the people under me*, etc.)[[Ps 17:48||]] … to Thee, God the Father, among the Gentiles, that is, I will make the Gentiles confess to Thee … […] … that that psalm speaks literally of Christ. For the Apostle by the words … […] … Christ in His place. […] [[15:11|And again|iterum]] the Lord says through the Prophet in […] the Psalm […] … called, [[15:11|the Lord|Dominum]], [[15:11|and magnify him|et magnifice]], that is, honour Him magnificently, and by words and deeds … […] … [[15:11|ye people|puli]], that is, the twelve tribes of Israel.

paras.t: […] in eum gentes sperabunt. Nostra translatio habet sic : Radix Jesse, qui stat in signum populorum, ipsum gentes deprecabuntur. Est itaque sensus : Erit radix Jesse, id est Christus de semine Jesse (seu Isai) patris David descendens. Quamvis autem Christus de Jesse sit natus, et per hoc posterior eo secundum naturam humanam, est tamen radix illius, quia secundum divinitatem est origo et fundamentum ipsius Jesse. Et qui, scilicet Christus, exsurget, procedendo in actum; vel, Ex[surget] a mortuis. […] Ecclesiam ex gentibus congregatam, quam regit per se ipsum, per angelorum custodiam, et per prælatos : in eum gentes sperabunt, tanquam in Salvatorem.
paras.en: [[15:12|And again|Et]] […] [[15:12|in him the Gentiles shall hope|in eum gentes sperabunt]] [the beginning of the lemma is lost in the transcription]. Our translation has it thus: [[Is 11:10|the root of Jesse, who standeth for an ensign of the people, him the Gentiles shall beseech|Radix Jesse, qui stat in signum populorum, ipsum gentes deprecabuntur]]. So the sense is: [[15:12|There shall be a root of Jesse|Erit radix Jesse]], that is, Christ, descending from the seed of Jesse (or Isai), the father of David. Though Christ was born of Jesse, and so is later than he according to human nature, He is yet his root, because according to His divinity He is the origin and foundation of Jesse himself. [[15:12|and he that shall rise up|Et qui, scilicet Christus, exsurget]], namely Christ, shall rise up by going forth into act; or, shall rise from the dead. […] [a few words are lost here, with "to rule the Gentiles"] … the Church gathered from the Gentiles, which He rules by Himself, by the guardianship of angels, and by prelates: [[15:12|in him the Gentiles shall hope|in eum gentes sperabunt]], as in their Saviour.

paras.t: Deus autem spei, id est, in quo speramus, et a quo spes vera infunditur, repleat vos in hac via inchoative, omni […] spirituali, […] tranquillitate, passionibus exstirpatis, in […] per fidem [...] […] stolus, ut divina fideliter contemplando, […] [abun]detis in spe, id est in actu spei, certius atque avidius exspectando felicitatem futuram ex prælibatione ejus in hac vita. Ex perceptione nempe præsentium munerum, certa fit exspectatio futurorum. Et virtute, id est gratia, Spiritus Sancti; vel, In virtute, id est efficacia bonæ operationis Spiritus Sancti, id est, quæ datur a Spiritu Sancto.
paras.en: [[15:13|Now the God of hope|Deus autem spei]], that is, in whom we hope, and by whom true hope is poured in, [[15:13|fill you|repleat vos]] on this way, in a beginning, [[15:13|with all|omni]] … spiritual … […] … tranquillity, the passions having been rooted out, [[15:13|in believing|in]] … through faith […] [several words are lost here] … the Apostle … that, by faithfully contemplating divine things, […] [[15:13|you may abound in hope|detis in spe]], that is, in the act of hope, awaiting the happiness to come more surely and more eagerly from a foretaste of it in this life. For from receiving present gifts, the expectation of future ones becomes sure. [[15:13|and in the power|Et virtute]], that is, the grace, [[15:13|of the Holy Ghost|Spiritus Sancti]]; or, in the power, that is, the efficacy of good working, of the Holy Ghost, that is, which is given by the Holy Ghost.

paras.t: Certus sum autem, fratres mei, et ego ipse de vobis, vel per revelationem divinam, vel per operationem vestram quam percepi : quemadmodum scriptum est, Ex fructibus eorum cognoscetis eos ; quoniam et ipsi pleni estis, secundum conditionem status vestri et exigentiam hujus viæ, vel quantum requiritur ad salutem, dilectione Dei et proximi. Non tamen simpliciter plenus est aliquis viator dilectione divina, quum nullus viator possit perfecte implere præceptum caritatis divinæ; et durante vita præsenti, quilibet potest in caritate proficere. Et estis repleti omni scientia ad salutem necessaria, non autem absolute omni scientia, ita ut possitis alterutrum monere, id est vos mutuo exhortari. Hoc dicit Apostolus, ne videatur eis scribere quasi ignaris et imperfectis, et ut hac laude provocet eos ad meliora. Verumtamen, quoniam a principio hujus epistolæ declaravit discordiam, infirmitatem et imperfectionem Romanorum, mirum videtur quomodo jam dicat eos dilectione et omni scientia plenos. Et respondendum, quod ista non sunt ad eosdem referenda. Nam quidam eorum valde perfecti erant, de quibus jam loquitur ; alii imperfecti fuerunt, quos superius increpavit et concordavit.
paras.en: [[15:14|And I myself also, my brethren, am assured of you|Certus sum autem, fratres mei, et ego ipse de vobis]], either by divine revelation or by your working, which I have perceived: as it is written, [[Matt 7:20|by their fruits you shall know them|Ex fructibus eorum cognoscetis eos]]; [[15:14|that you also are full of love|quoniam et ipsi pleni estis dilectione]], of the love of God and neighbour, according to the condition of your state and the needs of this way, or as much as is required for salvation. Yet no wayfarer [*viator*: one still on the way, in this life, as opposed to the blessed in the fatherland] is simply full of divine love, since no wayfarer can perfectly fulfil the precept of divine charity; and while the present life lasts, anyone can make progress in charity. And you are [[15:14|replenished with all knowledge|repleti omni scientia]] necessary for salvation, though not absolutely with all knowledge, [[15:14|so that you are able to admonish one another|ita ut possitis alterutrum monere]], that is, to exhort one another. The Apostle says this lest he seem to write to them as to ignorant and imperfect men, and to stir them to better things by this praise. Yet since at the beginning of this epistle he declared the discord, weakness and imperfection of the Romans, it seems strange that he now says they are full of love and all knowledge. The answer is that these things are not to be referred to the same people. For some of them were very perfect, and of these he now speaks; others were imperfect, whom he rebuked above and brought to concord.

paras.t: Consequenter excusat se de præsumptione. Audacius autem scripsi vobis, fratres : id est, quamvis, o Romani, ita perfecti sitis, ut dixi, tamen audacter ex magna fiducia scripsi vobis præsentem epistolam, ex parte, id est aliquibus vestrum, præcipue scilicet imperfectioribus, qui magis informatione hac indigent; vel, Ex parte, id est non plene, sed partim ac breviter ; tanquam in memoriam, id est ad actualem considerationem eorum quæ habitualiter scitis, vos reducens et excitans : scientibus enim legem loquor, ut dixi superius. Scribo tamen vobis, ut actualiter memores sitis eorum quæ scribo. Unde Salomon : Da sapienti, inquit, occasionem, et addetur ei sapientia; doce justum, et festinabit accipere. Cur autem scripserit, subdit : propter gratiam quæ data est mihi a Deo, id est propter apostolatum, vel sapientiam mihi divinitus præstitam, ad hoc, ut sim minister Jesu Christi in gentibus, id est, Christo deserviam gentes instruendo, sicut ipse mihi præcipit, sicque gratiam mihi collatam vobis communicem ; sanctificans, id est sanctum ostendens per divina miracula, Evangelium Dei, id est evangelicam doctrinam quam prædico, ut fiat oblatio, id est servitus, gentium : vel oblatio qua gentes se ipsas Domino offerunt; vel oblatio qua ego eas offero; accepta Deo per devotionem eorum, et sanctificata, id est purgata a vitiis, in Spiritu Sancto, id est virtute et gratia Spiritus Sancti.
paras.en: Next he excuses himself of presumption. [[15:15|But I have written to you, brethren, more boldly|Audacius autem scripsi vobis, fratres]]: that is, though you are so perfect, O Romans, as I have said, yet I have written you this letter boldly, out of great confidence, [[15:15|in some sort|ex parte]], that is, to some of you, namely chiefly the less perfect, who most need this instruction; or, in part, that is, not fully, but partly and briefly; [[15:15|as it were putting you in mind|tanquam in memoriam]], that is, bringing you back and stirring you to actually consider what you know habitually: [[Rom 7:1|for I speak to them that know the law|scientibus enim legem loquor]], as I said above. Yet I write to you that you may actually remember what I write. So Solomon says: [[Prov 9:9|Give an occasion to a wise man, and wisdom shall be added to him. Teach a just man, and he shall make haste to receive it|Da sapienti, inquit, occasionem, et addetur ei sapientia; doce justum, et festinabit accipere]]. Why he wrote, he adds: [[15:15|because of the grace which is given me from God|propter gratiam quæ data est mihi a Deo]], that is, because of the apostleship, or the wisdom given me by God, to this end, [[15:16|That I should be the minister of Christ Jesus among the Gentiles|ut sim minister Jesu Christi in gentibus]], that is, that I may serve Christ by instructing the Gentiles, as He commands me, and so share with you the grace bestowed on me; [[15:16|sanctifying|sanctificans]], that is, showing to be holy by divine miracles, [[15:16|the gospel of God|Evangelium Dei]], that is, the Gospel teaching which I preach, [[15:16|that the oblation of the Gentiles may be made|ut fiat oblatio gentium]], that is, the service of the Gentiles: or the offering by which the Gentiles offer themselves to the Lord; or the offering by which I offer them; [[15:16|acceptable|accepta]] to God through their devotion, [[15:16|and sanctified|et sanctificata]], that is, cleansed of vices, [[15:16|in the Holy Ghost|in Spiritu Sancto]], that is, by the power and grace of the Holy Ghost.

paras.t: Habeo igitur gloriam, id est, quum data sit mihi gratia tanta, ideo habeo gloriam, hoc est gloriationem internam, non vanam, sed veram, in Christo Jesu, id est secundum voluntatem ipsius, ad Deum, id est ad sanctæ Trinitatis honorem. Ex consideratione enim beneficiorum sibi collatorum lætabatur Apostolus in Deo : quod et nos imitari debemus. Vel, Habeo gloriam, id est meritum gloria dignum, seu apostolicam auctoritatem.
paras.en: [[15:17|I have therefore glory|Habeo igitur gloriam]]: that is, since so great a grace has been given me, I have glory, that is, an inward glorying, not vain but true, [[15:17|in Christ Jesus|in Christo Jesu]], that is, according to His will, [[15:17|towards God|ad Deum]], that is, for the honour of the holy Trinity. For the Apostle rejoiced in God from considering the benefits bestowed on him: which we too ought to imitate. Or, I have glory, that is, merit worthy of glory, or apostolic authority.

paras.t: Non enim audeo aliquid eorum loqui, quæ per me non efficit Christus : id est, nihil præsumo dicere, nisi quod a Christo percepi; nihil doceo alios, quod ipse non facio; nec majora affirmo de me in verbo vel facto, quam Christus operetur per me, vel quæ ego efficio virtute Christi ; in obedientiam gentium, id est ad hoc, ut gentes Evangelio Dei obediant. Itaque, Non audeo aliquid loqui, quod Christus non facit per me, verbo prædicationis, et factis bonæ conversationis, in virtute signorum, id est minorum miraculorum, et prodigiorum, id est miraculorum majorum, factorum non arte magica, sed in virtute Spiritus Sancti. Hoc dicit Apostolus contra pseudapostolos, et ut ceteris Apostolis qui cum Christo corporaliter sunt conversati, probet se parem, non ob propriam laudem, sed ut omnes suam doctrinam veram agnoscant, diligentiusque intendant ac impleant. In tantum ergo operatus est Christus per me, ita ut ab Jerusalem, unde cœpit prædicatio Apostolorum, per circuitum, id est diversis locis et urbibus, usque ad Illyricum mare, in fine Græciæ situm, repleverim, id est, plene disseminaverim, Evangelium Christi, id est, Evangelio Christi tot gentes impleverim, convertendo eas ad evangelicam fidem. In quo admiranda potestas Spiritus Sancti apparet, qui per unum virum, sine humano præsidio, tantos populos, ad tam supernaturalem, arduam, et incomprehensibilem legem convertit. Agnoscatur ergo operata Divinitas, habeaturque semper fides certissima, tanquam a Deo firmata ac insignita.
paras.en: [[15:18|For I dare not to speak of any of those things which Christ worketh not by me|Non enim audeo aliquid eorum loqui, quæ per me non efficit Christus]]: that is, I presume to say nothing but what I have received from Christ; I teach others nothing that I do not do myself; nor do I claim greater things of myself in word or deed than Christ works through me, or than I do by the power of Christ; [[15:18|for the obedience of the Gentiles|in obedientiam gentium]], that is, to this end, that the Gentiles may obey the Gospel of God. So: I dare not speak of anything which Christ does not do through me, [[15:18|by word|verbo]] of preaching, [[15:18|and deed|et factis]] of good conduct [the transcription reads *finitis*; *factis*, the Vulgate's word, must be meant], [[15:19|By the virtue of signs|in virtute signorum]], that is, of lesser miracles, [[15:19|and wonders|et prodigiorum]], that is, of greater miracles, done not by magic art but [[15:19|in the power of the Holy Ghost|in virtute Spiritus Sancti]]. The Apostle says this against the false apostles, and to prove himself equal to the other Apostles, who lived with Christ in the body, not for his own praise, but that all may recognize his teaching as true, and attend to it and fulfil it more diligently. So far, then, has Christ worked through me, [[15:19|so that from Jerusalem|ita ut ab Jerusalem]], where the preaching of the Apostles began[[Luke 24:47||]], [[15:19|round about|per circuitum]], that is, through different places and cities, [[15:19|as far as unto Illyricum|usque ad Illyricum]], the sea lying at the end of Greece, [[15:19|I have replenished the gospel of Christ|repleverim Evangelium Christi]], that is, have fully spread it abroad, have filled so many nations with the Gospel of Christ, converting them to the faith of the Gospel. In this the wonderful power of the Holy Ghost appears, who through one man, without human help, converted such great peoples to so supernatural, hard and incomprehensible a law. Let the Godhead, then, be acknowledged as having worked this, and let the faith be held always as most certain, as confirmed and marked out by God.

paras.t: Sic autem in illis locis Evangelium hoc prædicavi, non ubi nominatus est Christus, id est, non illis gentibus quibus ab aliis prædicatus fuerat Christus, ne super alienum fundamentum, id est doctrinam ab aliis traditam, ædificarem, id est, verbum spiritualis ædificationis adjicerem. Et in hoc prædicatio Apostoli comprobatur fuisse laboriosior et efficacior, quia materia non fuit disposita. Sed sicut scriptum est in Isaia : Quoniam quibus non est annuntiatum de eo, id est gentes, quibus non erat factus sermo de Christo per Prophetas sicut Judæis, videbunt Christum et opera ejus, oculo fidei, per prædicationem apostolicam; et qui non audierunt prædicationem Evangelii prius ab aliis Apostolis, intelligent evangelica documenta per prædicationem Pauli.
paras.en: [[15:20|And I have so preached this gospel, not where Christ was named|Sic autem in illis locis Evangelium hoc prædicavi, non ubi nominatus est Christus]]: in those places, that is, not to those nations to whom Christ had been preached by others, [[15:20|lest I should build upon another man a foundation|ne super alienum fundamentum ædificarem]], upon another's foundation, that is, the teaching handed on by others, build, that is, add the word of spiritual edification. And in this the Apostle's preaching is proved to have been more laborious and more effective, because the matter had not been prepared. [[15:21|But as it is written|Sed sicut scriptum est]] in Isaias[[Is 52:15||]]: [[15:21|They to whom he was not spoken of|Quoniam quibus non est annuntiatum de eo]], that is, the Gentiles, to whom the word about Christ had not come through the Prophets as it had to the Jews, [[15:21|shall see|videbunt]] Christ and His works with the eye of faith, through the apostolic preaching; [[15:21|and they that have not heard|et qui non audierunt]] the preaching of the Gospel before from the other Apostles, [[15:21|shall understand|intelligent]] the teachings of the Gospel through Paul's preaching.

paras.t: Propter quod, id est propter occupationem meam in prædicando his gentibus, et impediebar plurimum, id est vehementer et diu, venire ad vos Romanos, et prohibitus sum, id est impeditus, vel a Spiritu Sancto vetitus, usque adhuc. Nunc vero ulterius locum, id est necessariam causam manendi, seu locum convenientem, non habens in his regionibus Græciæ, ubi præcipue prædicavi. Jam enim competenter instructi et reformati fuerunt; erantque per civitates et loca ordinati episcopi, presbyteri, atque diaconi, qui suffecerant supplere vicem Apostoli. Cupiditatem autem, id est desiderium magnum, habens veniendi ad vos ex multis jam præcedentibus annis. Quoniam enim Roma erat caput mundi, sciebat Apostolus quod conversio Romanorum exemplaris et utilis esset toti mundo: ideo pene a principio suæ conversionis optavit prædicare Romanis. Nam et ideo appellavit Cæsarem, quatenus occasionem habeat veniendi Romam. Quum in Hispaniam proficisci cœpero, ut in ea evangelizem: optabat namque Apostolus, etiam in occidente prædicare Christum, sicut in orientalibus partibus fecerat; spero quod præteriens, id est, per loca vestra velociter transiens Hispaniam versus, videam vos, id est, aliquanto tempore apud vos ero. Non enim proposuit diu manere in Urbe, eo quod Petrum sufficere sciret ad conversionem Romæ, qui tunc cum suis discipulis Romæ sedit, et per loca Italiæ discipulos suos misit. Et a vobis Romanis deduci illuc, id est ad Hispaniam, quæ tunc erat Romanis subjecta, si vobis, id est præsentia vestra, primum ex parte temporis, id est modico tempore, fruitus, id est delectabiliter usus, fuero, habendo aliquem fructum in vobis, et de vestro profectu lætando. Frequenter sumit Apostolus, Frui, communiter. Proprie autem, Frui, est summo bono inhærere seu ultimo fine.
paras.en: [[15:22|For which cause also|Propter quod]], that is, because of my being busy preaching to these nations, [[15:22|I was hindered very much from coming to you|et impediebar plurimum venire ad vos]], very much, that is, greatly and for long, from coming to you Romans, [[15:22|and have been kept away till now|et prohibitus sum usque adhuc]], kept away, that is, hindered, or forbidden by the Holy Ghost. [[15:23|But now, having no more place in these countries|Nunc vero ulterius locum non habens in his regionibus]], no more place, that is, no necessary cause for staying, or no fitting place, in these regions of Greece, where I have chiefly preached. For they had now been suitably instructed and reformed; and there were bishops, priests and deacons ordained in the cities and places, who were enough to take the Apostle's place. [[15:23|and having a great desire these many years past to come unto you|Cupiditatem autem, id est desiderium magnum, habens veniendi ad vos ex multis jam præcedentibus annis]]: desire, that is, great longing. For since Rome was the head of the world, the Apostle knew that the conversion of the Romans would be an example and a help to the whole world: so almost from the beginning of his conversion he wished to preach to the Romans. For this is also why he appealed to Caesar, so as to have an occasion of coming to Rome[[Acts 25:11||]]. [[15:24|When I shall begin to take my journey into Spain|Quum in Hispaniam proficisci cœpero]], to preach the Gospel there: for the Apostle wished to preach Christ in the west too, as he had done in the eastern parts; [[15:24|I hope that, as I pass, I shall see you|spero quod præteriens videam vos]]: as I pass, that is, passing quickly through your parts towards Spain; I shall see you, that is, I shall be with you for some time. For he did not intend to stay long in the City, because he knew that Peter was enough for the conversion of Rome, who was then seated at Rome with his disciples and sent his disciples through the places of Italy. [[15:24|and be brought on my way thither by you|Et a vobis Romanis deduci illuc]] Romans, thither, that is, to Spain, which was then subject to the Romans, [[15:24|if first, in part, I shall have enjoyed you|si vobis … primum ex parte … fruitus … fuero]]: you, that is, your presence; in part, that is, of time, for a little while; enjoyed, that is, used with delight, by having some fruit among you and rejoicing in your progress. The Apostle often uses "to enjoy" in the common sense. Properly, to enjoy is to cleave to the highest good, that is, to the last end [*frui*, "to enjoy", in Augustine's sense: to rest in something for its own sake, which is right only of God].

paras.t: Nunc autem proficiscor Jerusalem, ministrare sanctis, id est eleemosynas […] gentium deferre Ecclesiæ Jerosolymitarum (quibus præfuit Jacobus). Qui ut omnibus credentibus essent forma christianæ perfectionis, vendiderunt omnia sua, et in paupertate voluntaria Christo servierunt : pro quorum sustentatione Apostoli erant solliciti. Petrus quoque et Joannes commiserunt Paulo et Barnabæ, ut gentes conversas inducerent ad mittendum eleemosynas Jerosolymitis : quod et diligenter fecerunt. Probaverunt enim, id est, opere ostenderunt et sponte acquieverunt, Macedonia et Achaia, id est fideles harum terrarum, quæ sunt partes Græciæ. Metropolis autem Macedoniæ, est Philippi (unde dicuntur Philippenses), et Thessalonica. Metropolis vero Achaiæ, est Corinthus. Collectionem, id est eleemosynarum collationem ac dationem, aliquam facere in pauperes sanctorum, id est ad sustentationem sanctorum pauperum, qui sunt in Jerusalem, et erant ex Judaismo conversi. Placuit enim eis collationem hanc facere; et debitores sunt eorum, id est sanctorum in Jerusalem. Nam si spiritualium eorum participes facti sunt gentiles, id est, quoniam gentes conversæ spiritualia bona, videlicet fidem, instructionem et sacramenta Christi, a Judæis conversis receperunt, mediate vel immediate, debent, id est, tenentur debito necessitatis, vel debito honestatis, imo utroque modo, et in carnalibus ministrare eis, id est necessaria vitæ corporalis eis præbere.
paras.en: [[15:25|But now I shall go to Jerusalem, to minister unto the saints|Nunc autem proficiscor Jerusalem, ministrare sanctis]], that is, to bring the alms […] [a word or two are lost at the page break] of the Gentiles to the Church of Jerusalem (over which James presided). They, to be for all believers a pattern of Christian perfection, sold all they had[[Luke 18:22||]][[Acts 2:45||]][[Acts 4:34||]] and served Christ in voluntary poverty: and the Apostles were careful for their support. Peter and John too charged Paul and Barnabas to lead the converted Gentiles to send alms to the Christians of Jerusalem: which they diligently did[[Acts 11:29||]][[Acts 11:30||]]. [[15:26|For it hath pleased them of Macedonia and Achaia|Probaverunt enim Macedonia et Achaia]]: it hath pleased, that is, they showed it in deed and freely agreed; Macedonia and Achaia, that is, the faithful of these lands, which are parts of Greece. The metropolis of Macedonia is Philippi (whence the Philippians are named), and Thessalonica. The metropolis of Achaia is Corinth. [[15:26|to make a contribution|Collectionem, id est eleemosynarum collationem ac dationem, aliquam facere]], that is, a gathering and giving of alms, [[15:26|for the poor of the saints that are in Jerusalem|in pauperes sanctorum, qui sunt in Jerusalem]], that is, for the support of the holy poor who are in Jerusalem, who had been converted from Judaism. [[15:27|For it hath pleased them|Placuit enim eis]] to make this contribution; [[15:27|and they are their debtors|et debitores sunt eorum]], that is, of the saints in Jerusalem. [[15:27|For, if the Gentiles have been made partakers of their spiritual things|Nam si spiritualium eorum participes facti sunt gentiles]], that is, since the converted Gentiles received spiritual goods, namely the faith, instruction and sacraments of Christ, from the converted Jews, mediately or immediately, [[15:27|they ought|debent]], that is, they are bound by a debt of necessity or a debt of fittingness, indeed in both ways, [[15:27|also in carnal things to minister to them|et in carnalibus ministrare eis]], that is, to provide them with what is needed for bodily life.

paras.t: Hoc ergo quum consummavero, id est, eleemosynas istas detulero in Jerusalem ad prædictos sanctos, et assignavero eis fructum hunc, id est collationem gentium eis missam, proficiscar per vos in Hispaniam. Quæritur, an Paulus prædicavit in Hispania? Dicunt quidam, quod non ; sed proposuit, non autem exsecutus est, superveniente impedimento. Unde quod nunc dicit, Proficiscar in Hispaniam, intelligendum est conditionaliter, scilicet, si Deus permiserit, vel ita concesserit. Allegant autem pro se Decretum, distinctione 11, Quis nesciat : ubi dicitur, quod de Apostolis solus Petrus prædicavit in provinciis, scilicet Italia, Gallia, Hispania, Africa et Sicilia. Isidorus vero in libro de Ortu et obitu Sanctorum, dicit oppositum, asserens Paulum in Hispania prædicasse. Hieronymus quoque in libro de Viris illustribus, dicit : Paulus in prima satisfactione a Nerone dimissus, in partibus occidentis prædicavit. — Ad Decretum autem diversimode respondetur. Lyra vero respondet, quod Decreti intentio est, quod nemo prædicavit in prædictis provinciis, nisi Petrus, vel alii de ordinatione ac missione ipsius. Sed huic non consonat, quod Paulus sæpe testatur, sibi imminere prædicationis officium in omnibus gentibus, quantum fieri potuit, ratione sui apostolatus, imo auctoritate sibi commissa. Unde non indiget ex ordinatione Petri in Hispania prædicare, præsertim quum proposuerit hoc facere, antequam venisset Romam ad Petrum. Constat etiam sanctum apostolum Jacobum in Hispania prædicasse. Nec potest negari quin Paulus Romæ (quæ est caput Italiæ) prædicavit, et per consequens in Italia. Scriptum est enim in Actibus : Mansit autem biennio toto in suo conducto, prædicans regnum Dei, et docens quæ sunt de Domino Jesu Christo, cum omni fiducia, sine prohibitione. Melius ergo dici posse opinor, quod Decretum ideo asserit solum Petrum ex Apostolis in his prædicasse provinciis, quoniam alii Apostoli, scilicet Paulus et Jacobus, non diu prædicaverunt in terris præfatis.
paras.en: [[15:28|When therefore I shall have accomplished this|Hoc ergo quum consummavero]], that is, when I have brought these alms to Jerusalem to the saints just mentioned, [[15:28|and consigned to them this fruit|et assignavero eis fructum hunc]], that is, the contribution of the Gentiles sent to them, [[15:28|I will come by you into Spain|proficiscar per vos in Hispaniam]]. It is asked whether Paul preached in Spain. Some say that he did not: he intended to, but did not carry it out, a hindrance having come up. So what he says now, "I will go into Spain," is to be understood conditionally, namely, if God permits, or so grants. For themselves they cite the Decretum, distinction 11, *Quis nesciat* [Gratian's Decretum, the standard collection of canon law], where it is said that of the Apostles Peter alone preached in the provinces, namely Italy, Gaul, Spain, Africa and Sicily. But Isidore, in the book *On the Birth and Death of the Saints*, says the opposite, asserting that Paul preached in Spain. Jerome too, in the book *On Illustrious Men*, says: Paul, released by Nero at his first defence, preached in the parts of the west. The Decretum is answered in different ways. Lyra answers that the intention of the Decretum is that no one preached in those provinces except Peter, or others by his ordering and sending. But this does not agree with what Paul often testifies, that the office of preaching to all the nations, as far as possible, lay upon him by reason of his apostleship, indeed by authority committed to him[[Rom 1:5||]][[Gal 1:16||]][[Gal 2:8||]][[2 Tim 1:11||]]. So he did not need Peter's ordering to preach in Spain, especially since he intended to do so before he came to Peter at Rome. It is also certain that the holy apostle James preached in Spain. Nor can it be denied that Paul preached at Rome (which is the head of Italy), and so in Italy. For it is written in the Acts: [[Acts 28:30|And he remained two whole years in his own hired lodging|Mansit autem biennio toto in suo conducto]], [[Acts 28:31|Preaching the kingdom of God and teaching the things which concern the Lord Jesus Christ, with all confidence, without prohibition|prædicans regnum Dei, et docens quæ sunt de Domino Jesu Christo, cum omni fiducia, sine prohibitione]].
