It can better be said, then, I think, that the Decretum asserts that Peter alone of the Apostles preached in these provinces because the other Apostles, namely Paul and James, did not preach long in those lands.

paras.t: Scio autem, id est, certe confido, vel per revelationem agnosco, quoniam veniens ad vos, in abundantia benedictionis Christi, id est in magna plenitudine gratiæ, veniam, ita quod meus adventus sit vobis multum proficuus, et mihi ipsi non parum meritorius. Obsecro igitur vos, fratres, id est, per rem sacram vos rogo, imo per Sanctum Sanctorum, videlicet per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, et per caritatem Spiritus Sancti, quam nobis infudit Spiritus Sanctus, ut adjuvetis me in orationibus vestris pro me fusis ad Deum, id est, orando Deum pro me, mihi subveniatis ; ut liberer ab infidelibus, id est obstinatis Judæis, qui sunt in Judæa, ne rapiant quod affero sanctis, et obsequii mei oblatio, id est repræsentatio eleemosynarum quas porto secundum ministerium mihi injunctum, accepta, id est placens et grata, fiat in Jerusalem sanctis illic degentibus, quatenus affectum meum erga ipsos intelligant ; ut veniam ad vos in gaudio spirituali, id est spiritualiter gaudens, negotiis meis salubriter expeditis, per voluntatem Dei, id est divina voluntate annuente ac operante, et refrigerer vobiscum, id est, insimul refrigerium spiritualis consolationis habeamus, vobis ad concordiam revocatis, et unoquoque nostrum de profectu alterius gloriante. Deus autem pacis dator et amator, sit cum omnibus vobis, per gratiosam inhabitationem. Quamvis enim ubique sit, tamen, ut Salomon ait, Longe est Dominus ab impiis. Amen.
paras.en: [[15:29|And I know|Scio autem]], that is, I surely trust, or know by revelation, [[15:29|that when I come to you I shall come in the abundance of the blessing|quoniam veniens ad vos, in abundantia benedictionis Evangelii Christi veniam]] [[15:29|of Christ|Christi]], that is, in a great fullness of grace, so that my coming may be very profitable to you, and not a little meritorious for myself. [[15:30|I beseech you therefore, brethren|Obsecro igitur vos, fratres]], that is, I ask you by a sacred thing, indeed by the Holy of Holies, namely [[15:30|through our Lord Jesus Christ and by the charity of the Holy Ghost|per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, et per caritatem Spiritus Sancti]], which the Holy Ghost has poured into us, [[15:30|that you help me in your prayers for me to God|ut adjuvetis me in orationibus vestris pro me fusis ad Deum]], your prayers poured out to God for me, that is, that you come to my help by praying to God for me; [[15:31|That I may be delivered from the unbelievers that are in Judea|ut liberer ab infidelibus, qui sunt in Judæa]], the unbelievers, that is, the obstinate Jews, lest they seize what I bring to the saints, [[15:31|and that the oblation of my service|et obsequii mei oblatio]], that is, the presenting of the alms which I carry according to the ministry laid upon me, [[15:31|may be acceptable|accepta fiat]], that is, pleasing and welcome, [[15:31|in Jerusalem to the saints|in Jerusalem sanctis]] who live there, so that they may understand my affection towards them; [[15:32|That I may come to you with joy|ut veniam ad vos in gaudio]], spiritual joy, that is, rejoicing spiritually, my affairs having been happily settled, [[15:32|by the will of God|per voluntatem Dei]], that is, with the divine will consenting and working, [[15:32|and may be refreshed with you|et refrigerer vobiscum]], that is, that we may have the refreshment of spiritual consolation together, you having been called back to concord, and each of us glorying in the other's progress. [[15:33|Now the God of peace|Deus autem pacis]], its giver and lover, [[15:33|be with, you all|sit cum omnibus vobis]], by His gracious indwelling. For although He is everywhere, yet, as Solomon says, [[Prov 15:29|The Lord is far from the wicked|Longe est Dominus ab impiis]]. [[15:33|Amen|Amen]].

16.title: Declaratio capituli sextidecimi et ultimi: Commendo autem vobis, etc.
16.title_en: Explanation of the sixteenth and last chapter: And I commend to you, etc.

paras.t: Hucusque Apostolus instruxit Romanos moraliter verbis prædicationis, jam agit idem exemplo operis, proponens eis personas imitatione dignissimas.
paras.en: Up to this point the Apostle has instructed the Romans in morals by the words of his preaching; now he does the same by the example of deeds, setting before them persons most worthy of imitation.

paras.t: Commendo autem, id est, commendabilem dico, laudo, committo, vobis Phœben sororem nostram spiritualem fide et religione, quæ est in ministerio Ecclesiæ quæ est Cenchris, id est, ministrat Ecclesiæ exsistenti in loco qui dicitur Cenchræ. Cenchris autem est portus maris Corinthi. Phœbe vero, mulier nobilissima erat atque ditissima, et de suis facultatibus Ecclesiam illam nutrivit.
paras.en: [[16:1|And I commend|Commendo autem]], that is, I call her worthy of commendation, I praise her, I entrust her, [[16:1|to you Phebe, our sister|vobis Phœben sororem nostram]], our spiritual sister by faith and religion, [[16:1|who is in the ministry of the church, that is in Cenchrae|quæ est in ministerio Ecclesiæ quæ est Cenchris]]: that is, she ministers to the Church that is in the place called Cenchrae. Now Cenchris is the seaport of Corinth. Phebe, moreover, was a most noble and most wealthy woman, and from her own means she supported that Church.

paras.t: Ut eam suscipiatis in Domino, id est secundum voluntatem Dei, et sicut Deus requirit, videlicet caritative, reverenter et pie, digne sanctis, id est, prout decet recipi sanctos ; et adsistatis ei in quocunque negotio vestri indiguerit. Venit enim hæc mulier Romam propter certa negotia sua : et forte in curia Cæsaris habuit aliqua expedire, sicque indiguit auxilio Romanorum. Meruit etiam ipsa, ut sibi subveniretur hoc modo : etenim ipsa quoque adstitit, id est subvenit, multis fidelibus, et mihi ipsi. In Ecclesia autem Romanorum erant quidam de familia imperatoris, juxta illud, Salutant vos qui sunt ex Cæsaris domo : et isti præcipue poterant auxiliari fidelibus.
paras.en: [[16:2|That you receive her in the Lord|Ut eam suscipiatis in Domino]], that is, according to the will of God and as God requires, namely charitably, reverently and devoutly, [[16:2|as becometh saints|digne sanctis]], that is, as it is fitting that saints be received; [[16:2|and that you assist her in whatsoever business she shall have need of you|et adsistatis ei in quocunque negotio vestri indiguerit]]. For this woman came to Rome on certain business of her own, and perhaps she had some matters to settle at Caesar's court, and so she needed the help of the Romans. And she herself deserved to be helped in this way: [[16:2|For she also hath assisted|etenim ipsa quoque adstitit]], that is, helped, [[16:2|many|multis]] of the faithful, [[16:2|and myself also|et mihi ipsi]]. Now in the Church of the Romans there were some of the emperor's household, according to the saying, [[Phil 4:22|they that are of Caesar's household|Salutant vos qui sunt ex Cæsaris domo]] salute you; and these especially were able to help the faithful.

paras.t: Salutate Priscam, et Aquilam virum Priscæ. De quibus in Actibus habetur ; ubi etiam Prisca hæc appellatur Priscilla. Et erant ambo valde eruditi in via Domini : nam et Apollinem plenius instruxerunt. Veneruntque Romam ut confirmarent Romanos : quod secundum Glossam, intelligendum est de omnibus quos hic salutat Apostolus, scilicet, quod venerunt Romam ad confirmandum Romanos in fide et gratia. Adjutores mei in Christo Jesu, id est in prædicatione Evangelii Christi ; qui pro anima mea, id est defensione vitæ meæ, suas cervices supposuerunt, id est, se ipsos mortis periculo exposuerunt. Debemus enim pro fratribus animas ponere. Quibus non ego solus gratias ago pro beneficiis mihi impensis, qui in Corinthi in domo eorum mansi, et operabar cum eis manibus propriis : sed et cunctæ Ecclesiæ gentium gratias agunt, quoniam mihi gentium Apostolo taliter adstiterunt. Salutate quoque et domesticam eorum ecclesiam, id est eorum familiam, vel congregationem fidelium in domo eorum exsistentem.
paras.en: [[16:3|Salute Prisca and Aquila|Salutate Priscam, et Aquilam]], the husband of Prisca. Of them we read in the Acts[[Acts 18:2||]], where this Prisca is also called Priscilla. And both were very learned in the way of the Lord, for they also instructed Apollo more fully[[Acts 18:26||]]. And they came to Rome to strengthen the Romans; and according to the Gloss this is to be understood of all whom the Apostle greets here, namely that they came to Rome to strengthen the Romans in faith and grace. [[16:3|my helpers, in Christ Jesus|Adjutores mei in Christo Jesu]], that is, in preaching the Gospel of Christ; [[16:4|who have for my life|qui pro anima mea]], that is, in defence of my life, [[16:4|laid down their own necks|suas cervices supposuerunt]], that is, exposed themselves to the danger of death. For [[1 John 3:16|we ought to lay down our lives for the brethren|Debemus enim pro fratribus animas ponere]]. [[16:4|to whom not I only give thanks|Quibus non ego solus gratias ago]] for the kindnesses shown me, who stayed in their house at Corinth and worked with them with my own hands, [[16:4|but also all the churches of the Gentiles|sed et cunctæ Ecclesiæ gentium]] give thanks, since they stood by me, the Apostle of the Gentiles, in this way. Salute also [[16:5|the church which is in their house|et domesticam eorum ecclesiam]], that is, their household, or the congregation of the faithful gathered in their house.

paras.t: Salutate Ephænetum dilectum mihi, id est familiarem, qui est primitivus Asiæ in Christo, id est ex Asia primo conversus, ac regeneratus in Christo : et sic erat aliis exemplar credulitatis seu fidei. Salutate Mariam, quæ multum laboravit in vobis, id est pro vobis concordandis. Nuntiavit enim Apostolo discordiam Romanorum.
paras.en: [[16:5|Salute Epenetus, my beloved|Salutate Ephænetum dilectum mihi]], that is, my close friend, [[16:5|who is the firstfruits of Asia in Christ|qui est primitivus Asiæ in Christo]], that is, the first to be converted from Asia and reborn in Christ; and so he was an example to others of belief, or faith. [[16:6|Salute Mary, who hath laboured much among you|Salutate Mariam, quæ multum laboravit in vobis]], that is, to bring you to concord. For she told the Apostle of the discord among the Romans.

paras.t: Salutate Andronicum et Juliam, cognatos et concaptivos meos, id est, de tribu mea existentes, qui interdum capti fuerunt pro fide, et multa perpessi, ut ego : qui sunt nobiles nobilitate sanctissimæ conversationis, in Apostolis. Secundum Origenem, hi duo viri erant de numero septuaginta discipulorum, quorum aliqui (ut Silas) nominantur apostoli. Sic et isti dicuntur nobiles in Apostolis, id est inter Apostolos, quia apostoli dicti sunt ratione discipulatus et validæ prædicationis. Qui et ante me fuerunt in Christo per fidem.
paras.en: [[16:7|Salute Andronicus and Junias, my kinsmen and fellow prisoners|Salutate Andronicum et Juliam, cognatos et concaptivos meos]] [Denis reads *Juliam*, Julia, where the Vulgate has *Juniam*], that is, men of my own tribe, who were at times taken captive for the faith and suffered many things, as I have: [[16:7|who are of note|qui sunt nobiles]] [*nobiles*, literally "noble"] with the nobility of a most holy way of life, [[16:7|among the apostles|in Apostolis]]. According to Origen, these two men were of the number of the seventy disciples, some of whom (as Silas) are called apostles. So these too are called noble among the Apostles, that is, in the number of the Apostles, because they were called apostles by reason of their discipleship and their powerful preaching. [[16:7|who also were in Christ before me|Qui et ante me fuerunt in Christo]] through faith.

paras.t: Salutate Ampliatum dilectissimum mihi in Domino…. Salutate eos qui sunt ex Narcissi domo, id est, ad ejus familiam pertinent. Narcissus iste, ut dicitur, presbyter fuit, et circumeundo confirmabat fideles. Salutate Rufum electum ad sacerdotium, et matrem ejus carnalem et meam spiritualem. Propter præcipuam hujus feminæ sanctitatem, nominat eam matrem. Cetera patent.
paras.en: [[16:8|Salute Ampliatus, most beloved to me in the Lord|Salutate Ampliatum dilectissimum mihi in Domino]]…. [[16:11|Salute them that are of Narcissus' household|Salutate eos qui sunt ex Narcissi domo]], that is, who belong to his household. This Narcissus, it is said, was a priest, and he went about strengthening the faithful. [[16:13|Salute Rufus, elect|Salutate Rufum electum]] to the priesthood, [[16:13|and his mother|et matrem ejus]] according to the flesh, [[16:13|and mine|et meam]] according to the spirit. Because of this woman's exceptional holiness he calls her his mother. The rest is plain.

paras.t: Salutate invicem in osculo sancto, spirituali, caritativo, quod sit veræ concordiæ et internæ dilectionis indicium, non in osculo carnali, impudico, adulatorio, simulatorio, aut proditorio. Absalon osculabatur populum adulatorie ; Joab Amasam, simulatorie ; Judas Christum, proditorie. Erat quippe in primitiva Ecclesia consuetudo recipiendi ac salutandi fideles cum osculo oris. Tunc enim arsit spiritualis dilectio, nec erat periculum de carnalitatis mixtura, ut modo.
paras.en: [[16:16|Salute one another with an holy kiss|Salutate invicem in osculo sancto]]: a spiritual, charitable kiss, such as is a sign of true concord and inward love; not with a carnal kiss, unchaste, flattering, feigned or treacherous. Absalom kissed the people to flatter them[[2 Kings 15:5||]] [the margin gives II Reg. xv, 3; the kisses are told in v. 5]; Joab kissed Amasa in feigning[[2 Kings 20:9||]]; Judas kissed Christ in treachery. For in the early Church there was a custom of receiving and greeting the faithful with a kiss on the mouth. For then spiritual love burned, and there was no danger of carnality mixing in, as there is now.

paras.t: Rogo autem vos, fratres, ut observetis, id est, notetis et discernatis ab aliis, eos qui dissensiones, id est discordias et contrarias opiniones circa fidei veritatem, et offendicula, id est scandala, præter, id est contra, doctrinam evangelicam quam vos didicistis a Christi discipulis, faciunt, inducendo vos ad mutuam offensionem ac dissensionem, et declinate ab eis, non solum mente, sed etiam corporali recessu, si fieri potest, ne pervertamini cum perversis.
paras.en: [[16:17|Now I beseech you, brethren, to mark|Rogo autem vos, fratres, ut observetis]], that is, take note of and distinguish from others, [[16:17|them who make dissensions|eos qui dissensiones]], that is, discords and opinions contrary to the truth of the faith, [[16:17|and offences|et offendicula]], that is, scandals, [[16:17|contrary to|præter]] [*præter*, literally "beside" or "beyond"], that is, against, [[16:17|the doctrine|doctrinam]] of the Gospel [[16:17|which you have learned|quam vos didicistis]] from the disciples of Christ, making them by leading you to offend one another and to fall into dissension; [[16:17|and avoid them|et declinate ab eis]], not only in mind but also by keeping away from them in body, if it can be done, lest you be perverted with the perverse.

paras.t: Hujusmodi enim perversi, Christo Domino nostro non serviunt, qui talia vitia suis servis prohibuit, sed suo ventri, quem quærunt implere, quum sint gulosi ; et per dulces sermones, id est verba composita atque placentia, et benedictiones, id est falsas laudationes, seducunt corda innocentium, id est inexpertorum et incircumspectorum : qui in se boni sunt, sine dolo et felle, putantque alios tales esse quales ipsi sunt, ideo citó credunt et falluntur. Unde in Proverbiis scriptum est : Innocens credit omni verbo ; astutus considerat gressus suos.
paras.en: [[16:18|For they that are such|Hujusmodi enim]] perverse men [[16:18|serve not Christ our Lord|Christo Domino nostro non serviunt]], who forbade such vices to his servants, [[16:18|but their own belly|sed suo ventri]], which they seek to fill, being gluttons; [[16:18|and by pleasing speeches|et per dulces sermones]], that is, by words well turned and agreeable, [[16:18|and good words|et benedictiones]] [*benedictiones*, literally "blessings"], that is, false praises, [[16:18|seduce the hearts of the innocent|seducunt corda innocentium]], that is, of the inexperienced and unwary, who are good in themselves, without guile or gall, and think others are such as they are themselves; and so they believe quickly and are deceived. Hence it is written in Proverbs: [[Prov 14:15|The innocent believeth every word: the discreet man considereth his steps|Innocens credit omni verbo ; astutus considerat gressus suos]].

paras.t: Debetis autem, o Romani, ab his declinare : Vestra enim obedientia, qua veræ fidei et apostolicæ traditioni paretis, in omnem locum, id est per omnes Ecclesias, divulgata est. Quoniam enim Romani monarchiam tenebant, quotidie erat confluxus extraneorum ad Romam, qui redeuntes ad sua, divulgabant facta Romanorum : et ita fideles venientes Romam, quum vidissent gratiam Romanorum, revertentes nuntiaverunt ceteris Christianis fidem et opera eorum, sicque alii animabantur, et confortabantur in fide. Propterea error Romanorum magis omnibus nocuisset, quam aliorum.
paras.en: And you ought, O Romans, to turn away from these: [[16:19|For your obedience|Vestra enim obedientia]], by which you obey the true faith and the apostolic tradition, [[16:19|is published|divulgata est]] [[16:19|in every place|in omnem locum]], that is, throughout all the Churches. For since the Romans held the rule of the world, there was a daily flow of strangers to Rome, who on returning home spread abroad the doings of the Romans; and so the faithful who came to Rome, having seen the grace of the Romans, told the other Christians on their return of their faith and works, and so others were encouraged and strengthened in the faith. Therefore an error of the Romans would have harmed everyone more than an error of others.

paras.t: Gaudeo igitur in vobis, in consideratione gratiæ vobis concessæ, et congratulor vobis. Sed volo vos sapientes esse in bono, id est in cognitione et operatione eorum quæ bona sunt, ut discernatis pretiosum a vili, virtutem a vitio, verum a falso, et simplices, id est ignaros et inexpertos, in malo, ut nec operando experiamini, nec approbando sciatis, nec studiose discatis quæ mala sunt.
paras.en: [[16:19|I rejoice therefore in you|Gaudeo igitur in vobis]], considering the grace granted to you, and I rejoice with you. [[16:19|But I would have you to be wise in good|Sed volo vos sapientes esse in bono]], that is, in knowing and doing the things that are good, so that you may tell the precious from the vile, virtue from vice, the true from the false, [[16:19|and simple|et simplices]], that is, ignorant and inexperienced, [[16:19|in evil|in malo]], so that you neither come to know evil things by doing them, nor know them by approving them, nor learn them with zeal.

paras.t: Deus autem pacis conteret, id est dejiciet, Satanam, id est diabolum (de quo legitur in Job, Dixit Dominus ad Satan : et in Zacharia, Increpet Dominus in te, Satan), sub pedibus, id est affectibus, vestris velociter. De quibus pedibus in Canticis scribitur : Lavi pedes meos, quomodo inquinabo eos? et in Psalmo, Non veniat mihi pes superbiæ. Hoc est : Dominus dabit vobis virtutem resistendi diabolo, eumque vincendi. Propter quod ait Salvator : Ecce dedi vobis potestatem calcandi supra omnem virtutem inimici, et nihil vobis nocebit. Itemque in Psalmo : Super aspidem et basiliscum ambulabis. Gratia Domini nostri Jesu Christi vobiscum.
paras.en: [[16:20|And the God of peace crush|Deus autem pacis conteret]] [Denis reads *conteret*, "shall crush"], that is, cast down, [[16:20|Satan|Satanam]], that is, the devil (of whom we read in Job, [[Job 1:12|the Lord said to Satan|Dixit Dominus ad Satan]], and in Zacharias, [[Zach 3:2|The Lord rebuke thee, O Satan|Increpet Dominus in te, Satan]]), [[16:20|under your feet|sub pedibus]], that is, under your affections, [[16:20|speedily|velociter]]. Of these feet it is written in the Canticles: [[Cant 5:3|I have washed my feet, how shall I defile them?|Lavi pedes meos, quomodo inquinabo eos?]] And in the Psalm: [[Ps 35:12|Let not the foot of pride come to me|Non veniat mihi pes superbiæ]]. That is: the Lord will give you the strength to resist the devil and to overcome him. Wherefore the Saviour says: [[Luke 10:19|Behold, I have given you power to tread upon|Ecce dedi vobis potestatem calcandi supra]] [[Luke 10:19|all the power of the enemy: and nothing shall hurt you|omnem virtutem inimici, et nihil vobis nocebit]]. And likewise in the Psalm: [[Ps 90:13|Thou shalt walk upon the asp and the basilisk|Super aspidem et basiliscum ambulabis]]. [[16:20|The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you|Gratia Domini nostri Jesu Christi vobiscum]].

paras.t: Salutat vos Timotheus, adjutor meus in cultura vineæ Christi, Ephesiorum episcopus : cum quo, secundum Hieronymum, misit Apostolus istam epistolam. Alii dicunt quod prædicta Phœbes detulit eam. Et puto quod utrisque commisit hanc bajulationem, ut si quid uni in via occurreret impedimenti, alter negotium expediret. Et Lucius. Quidam dicit, Et Lucas, exponitque de Luca evangelista ; sed nec textus correctus, nec Glossa sic habet. Et Jason, et Sosipater, qui sunt cognati mei secundum carnem.
paras.en: [[16:21|Timothy, my fellow labourer, saluteth you|Salutat vos Timotheus, adjutor meus]] in the tilling of Christ's vineyard, the bishop of the Ephesians, by whom, according to Jerome, the Apostle sent this epistle. Others say that the Phebe mentioned above carried it. And I think that he entrusted the carrying of it to both, so that if any hindrance befell one on the way, the other might see the business through. [[16:21|and Lucius|Et Lucius]]. A certain writer reads "And Lucas", and explains it of Luke the Evangelist; but neither the corrected text nor the Gloss has this. [[16:21|and Jason and Sosipater|Et Jason, et Sosipater]], who are [[16:21|my kinsmen|cognati mei]] according to the flesh.

paras.t: Salutat vos ego Tertius, id est taliter nominatus, qui scripsi epistolam hanc in Domino, id est ad Dei honorem, tanquam notarius Apostoli, de cujus licentia ego nominatus vos saluto, et nomen meum hic exprimo, ad perpetuam rei memoriam.
paras.en: [[16:22|I, Tertius|Salutat vos ego Tertius]], that is, one so named, [[16:22|who wrote this epistle, salute you in the Lord|qui scripsi epistolam hanc in Domino]], that is, to the honour of God, as the Apostle's scribe; with his leave I, who am named here, greet you, and set down my name here as a lasting record of the matter.

paras.t: Salutat vos Caius hospes meus jam in civitate Corinthi, unde mitto præsentem epistolam. Iste Caius erat Corinthiorum episcopus : ad quem scribit Joannes apostolus tertiam suam Canonicam, laudans eum de virtute hospitalitatis. Unde et Paulus in domo ejus manere solebat. Et universa Ecclesia Caii hujus. Salutat vos Erastus archarius civitatis Atheniensium, secundum Glossam. Dicitur autem archarius, ab ἀρχός, quod est princeps ; vel ab arca, quoniam præerat arcæ, custodiens eam, in qua ponebantur vectigalia et tributa. Et Quartus frater. Quartus, proprium nomen est, sicut et Tertius, eratque frater religione, non natione.
paras.en: [[16:23|Caius, my host|Salutat vos Caius hospes meus]] greets you, my host now in the city of Corinth, from which I am sending this present epistle. This Caius was bishop of the Corinthians; to him the apostle John writes his third canonical epistle, praising him for the virtue of hospitality[[3 John 1:5||]][[3 John 1:6||]]. Hence Paul too used to stay in his house. [[16:23|and the whole church|Et universa Ecclesia]] of this Caius. [[16:23|Erastus, the treasurer|Salutat vos Erastus archarius]] [[16:23|of the city|civitatis]] of the Athenians, according to the Gloss, greets you [Denis writes *archarius*; the margin gives the other reading, *arcarius*, which is the Vulgate's]. Now he is called *archarius* from ἀρχός, which means "prince"; or from *arca*, "chest", because he was in charge of the chest in which the taxes and tributes were put, and kept it. [[16:23|and Quartus, a brother|Et Quartus frater]]. Quartus is a proper name, as Tertius is too, and he was a brother by religion, not by birth.

paras.t: Gratia Domini nostri Jesu Christi cum omnibus vobis. Amen. Ex ardenti amore resumit Apostolus quod prædixit de præsentia gratiæ Christi.
paras.en: [[16:24|The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.|Gratia Domini nostri Jesu Christi cum omnibus vobis. Amen.]] Out of burning love the Apostle takes up again what he said before about the presence of the grace of Christ.

paras.t: Ei autem, videlicet Deo Trinitati, qui potens est vos confirmare in omni bono, juxta evangelium meum, id est secundum prædicationem meam, et prædicationem Jesu Christi, a cujus prædicatione evangelium meum non dissonat : prædicationem (inquam) Christi factam secundum revelationem mysterii, id est in manifestatione divini secreti de incarnatione Christi et redemptione generis humani, vel secundum quod revelatum est mihi de isto mysterio : mysterii, dico, temporibus æternis taciti, id est ab æterno in Deo absconditi. Tempora autem æterna Apostolus dicit durationem præcedentem hunc mundum, quæ aliud nihil est nisi æternitas : quam exprimit Apostolus per Æterna tempora, quia non potest apprehendi a nobis, nisi per comparationem ad tempus infinitum. Unde et ad Titum dicit : Ante tempora sæcularia.
paras.en: [[16:25|Now to him|Ei autem]], namely to God the Trinity, [[16:25|that is able to establish you|qui potens est vos confirmare]] in every good, [[16:25|according to my gospel|juxta evangelium meum]], that is, according to my preaching, [[16:25|and the preaching of Jesus Christ|et prædicationem Jesu Christi]], from whose preaching my gospel does not differ: the preaching (I say) of Christ, made [[16:25|according to the revelation of the mystery|secundum revelationem mysterii]], that is, in the making known of the divine secret of the incarnation of Christ and the redemption of mankind; or, according to what has been revealed to me of this mystery: of the mystery, I say, [[16:25|which was kept secret from eternity|temporibus æternis taciti]] [literally, "kept silent in eternal times"], that is, hidden in God from eternity. Now by eternal times the Apostle means the duration that went before this world, which is nothing other than eternity; and the Apostle expresses it as eternal times because it cannot be grasped by us except by comparison with an infinite time. Hence he also says to Titus: [[Tit 1:2|before the times of the world|Ante tempora sæcularia]].

paras.t: Quod mysterium nunc, tempore novæ legis, in Christi adventu, patefactum est mundo per scripturas Prophetarum ab ipso Christo declaratas. Qui, ut apud Lucam legitur, aperuit illis sensum, ut intelligerent Scripturas. Et iterum, promisit Apostolis : Quum venerit ille Spiritus veritatis, docebit vos omnem veritatem. Tunc namque apparuerunt fontes aquarum, et revelata sunt fundamenta orbis terrarum. Quod totum factum est secundum præceptum æterni Dei. Christus enim secundum formam servi, erat minister Trinitatis in hac revelatione. Propter quod ait Sicut mandatum dedit mihi Pater, sic facio. Et facta est revelatio ista ad obeditionem fidei in cunctis gentibus, id est, ut omnes gentes obediant fidei, credendo et operando.
paras.en: [[16:26|Which|Quod mysterium]] mystery [[16:26|now|nunc]], in the time of the new law, at the coming of Christ, [[16:26|is made manifest|patefactum est]] to the world [[16:26|by the scriptures of the prophets|per scripturas Prophetarum]], as declared by Christ himself; who, as we read in Luke, [[Luke 24:45|opened their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures|aperuit illis sensum, ut intelligerent Scripturas]]. And again, he promised the Apostles: [[John 16:13|when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will teach you all truth|Quum venerit ille Spiritus veritatis, docebit vos omnem veritatem]]. For then [[Ps 17:16|the fountains of waters appeared, and the foundations of the world were discovered|apparuerunt fontes aquarum, et revelata sunt fundamenta orbis terrarum]] [the verse number in the margin cannot be read; the words are those of Ps. xvii, 16]. All this was done [[16:26|according to the precept of the eternal God|secundum præceptum æterni Dei]]. For Christ, according to the form of a servant, was the minister of the Trinity in this revelation. Wherefore he says: [[John 14:31|as the Father hath given me commandments, so do I|Sicut mandatum dedit mihi Pater, sic facio]]. And this revelation was made [[16:26|for the obedience of faith|ad obeditionem fidei]] [[16:26|among all nations|in cunctis gentibus]], that is, so that all nations may obey the faith, by believing and by doing.

paras.t: Mysterii, dico, cogniti plenarie atque perfecte soli sapienti Deo, id est Deo Trinitati, qui solus est sapiens per essentiam : cujus tanta est sapientia, ut comparatione ipsius, omnis sapientia creata pro nihilo reputetur, sicut in comparatione divinæ puritatis, cœli dicuntur immundi, et comparatione aliorum, solus dicitur esse. Patefacti autem per Jesum Christum, ut dictum est, cui sit honor, id est debita exhibitio reverentiæ, et gloria, id est clara cum laude notitia, vel vera lætitia : ita ut honor sit ei a nobis, gloria autem in se. Ipse enim est cum Patre et Spiritu Sancto super omnia Deus sublimis et benedictus. Amen.
paras.en: Of the mystery, I say, [[16:26|known|cogniti]] fully and perfectly [[16:27|to God, the only wise|soli sapienti Deo]] [Denis takes *cogniti*, "known", with what follows: known to the only wise God], that is, to God the Trinity, who alone is wise by essence, whose wisdom is so great that in comparison with it all created wisdom is reckoned as nothing; just as in comparison with the divine purity the heavens are said to be unclean[[Job 15:15||]], and in comparison with other things he alone is said to be. Made manifest, moreover, [[16:27|through Jesus Christ|per Jesum Christum]], as has been said; [[16:27|to whom be honour|cui sit honor]], that is, the showing of due reverence, [[16:27|and glory|et gloria]] [a footnote in the edition gives the rest of the verse as a variant: *in sæcula sæculorum. Amen*, "for ever and ever. Amen"], that is, a clear knowledge joined with praise, or true joy: so that honour is given him by us, but glory is in himself. For he, with the Father and the Holy Ghost, is God over all, exalted and blessed. Amen.
